GFNBounds.Silva.wSupport.type: {X : Type u_1} → {T : Type u_2} → [Fintype X] → [Fintype T] → (X → T → ℝ) → Finset (X × T)
GFNBounds.Silva.wSupport.doc: The pairs `(x,τ)` over which `w_min` is a minimum: those with `p_B(τ|x) > 0`.

GFNBounds.Silva.wMin_pos.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] {pET : X → ℝ} {pB : X → T → ℝ}
  (h : (GFNBounds.Silva.wSupport pB).Nonempty), (∀ (x : X), 0 < pET x) → 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.wMin pET pB h

GFNBounds.Silva.wMin.type:
{X : Type u_1} →
  {T : Type u_2} →
    [inst : Fintype X] → [inst_1 : Fintype T] → (X → ℝ) → (pB : X → T → ℝ) → (GFNBounds.Silva.wSupport pB).Nonempty → ℝ

GFNBounds.Silva.unif.doc: The uniform law `q_{E,T}` on a finite set.

GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_sqrt_residual_max.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] {pET π pT : X → ℝ} {pB : X → T → ℝ} {pF : T → ℝ}
  (hX : Finset.univ.Nonempty) (hsupp : {p | 0 < pB p.1 p.2}.Nonempty),
  (∀ (x : X), 0 < pET x) →
    ∑ x, pET x = 1 →
      (∀ (x : X), 0 < π x) →
        (∀ (x : X) (τ : T), 0 ≤ pB x τ) →
          (∀ (x : X), ∑ τ, pB x τ = 1) →
            (∀ (x : X) (τ : T), 0 < pB x τ → 0 < pF τ) →
              (∀ (x : X), pT x = ∑ τ, pB x τ * (pF τ / pB x τ)) →
                GFNBounds.Silva.tv pT π ≤
                  ↑(Fintype.card X) / 2 *
                      max ({p | 0 < pB p.1 p.2}.sup' hsupp fun p => pF p.2 / pB p.1 p.2) (Finset.univ.sup' hX π) *
                    √((1 + GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq (GFNBounds.Silva.unif X) pET) * GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF)
GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_sqrt_residual_max.doc:
**`prop:silva_explicit` with the paper's own constants**: `M` is the maximum of
`p_F(τ)/p_B(τ|x)` over the support of `p_B`, and `‖π‖_∞` the maximum of `π`. The two
nonemptiness arguments are forced by `Finset.sup'`; both follow from the other hypotheses, and
neither is a restriction (see SCOPE). The paper's `‖π‖_∞` is the maximum of `π` because `π > 0`
is assumed.

GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_sqrt_residual.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] {pET π pT : X → ℝ} {pB : X → T → ℝ} {pF : T → ℝ}
  {M Pinf : ℝ},
  (∀ (x : X), 0 < pET x) →
    ∑ x, pET x = 1 →
      (∀ (x : X), 0 < π x) →
        (∀ (x : X) (τ : T), 0 ≤ pB x τ) →
          (∀ (x : X), ∑ τ, pB x τ = 1) →
            (∀ (x : X) (τ : T), 0 < pB x τ → 0 < pF τ) →
              (∀ (x : X), pT x = ∑ τ, pB x τ * (pF τ / pB x τ)) →
                (∀ (x : X) (τ : T), 0 < pB x τ → pF τ / pB x τ ≤ M) →
                  (∀ (x : X), π x ≤ Pinf) →
                    GFNBounds.Silva.tv pT π ≤
                      ↑(Fintype.card X) / 2 * max M Pinf *
                        √((1 + GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq (GFNBounds.Silva.unif X) pET) *
                            GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF)
GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_sqrt_residual.doc:
**`prop:silva_explicit`** (`silva_comparison.tex:29–39`), with `M` and `‖π‖_∞` presented as
upper bounds: if `p_{E,T}` and `π` have full support, `p_B(·|x)` is a probability law dominating
the forward trajectories into `x` (`hdom`), `p_F` is positive on the support of `p_B`, and
`p_F(τ)/p_B(τ|x) ≤ M`, `π ≤ Pinf`, then

`TV(p_T, π) ≤ (|𝒳|/2) · max(M, Pinf) · sqrt((1 + χ²(q_{E,T}‖p_{E,T})) · 𝓔(p_F))`.

`tv_le_sqrt_residual_max` is the instance in which `M` and `Pinf` are the paper's maxima.

GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_exp_sqrt_energy_wm.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] {pET : X → ℝ} {pB : X → T → ℝ} {pF : T → ℝ}
  {π pT : X → ℝ} (h : (GFNBounds.Silva.wSupport pB).Nonempty),
  (∀ (x : X), 0 < π x) →
    ∑ x, π x = 1 →
      (∀ (x : X), 0 < pET x) →
        (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 ≤ pB x t) →
          (∀ (x : X), ∑ t, pB x t = 1) →
            (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 < pB x t → 0 < pF t) →
              (∀ (x : X), pT x = ∑ t, pB x t * (pF t / pB x t)) →
                GFNBounds.Silva.tv pT π ≤
                  2⁻¹ * (Real.exp √(GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF / GFNBounds.Silva.wMin pET pB h) - 1)

GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_exp_sqrt_energy.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] {pET : X → ℝ} {pB : X → T → ℝ} {pF : T → ℝ}
  {π pT : X → ℝ} {w : ℝ},
  (∀ (x : X), 0 < π x) →
    ∑ x, π x = 1 →
      (∀ (x : X), 0 ≤ pET x) →
        (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 ≤ pB x t) →
          (∀ (x : X), ∑ t, pB x t = 1) →
            (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 < pB x t → 0 < pF t) →
              (∀ (x : X), pT x = ∑ t, pB x t * (pF t / pB x t)) →
                0 < w →
                  (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 < pB x t → w ≤ pET x * pB x t) →
                    GFNBounds.Silva.tv pT π ≤ 2⁻¹ * (Real.exp √(GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF / w) - 1)
GFNBounds.Silva.tv_le_exp_sqrt_energy.doc:
**`prop:silva_no_uniform`(i)**, in the form its proof uses: with `w` any positive lower bound
for `p_{E,T}(x) p_B(τ|x)` on the support of `p_B`,
`TV(p_T,π) ≤ ½ (e^{√(𝓔(p_F)/w)} − 1)`. The paper's `w_min` is the largest such `w`; see
`tv_le_exp_sqrt_energy_wmin`.

GFNBounds.Silva.tv.type: {X : Type u_1} → [Fintype X] → (X → ℝ) → (X → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Silva.tv.doc:
Total variation on a finite set, with the ½-convention:
`TV(p,q) = ½ ∑_x |p(x) − q(x)|`.

GFNBounds.Silva.sum_unif.type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype X], ↑(Fintype.card X) ≠ 0 → ∑ x, GFNBounds.Silva.unif X x = 1
GFNBounds.Silva.sum_unif.doc: The uniform law is a probability law on a nonempty finite set.

GFNBounds.Silva.sum_sq_div_eq_one_add_ch.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype X] {q p : X → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : X), 0 < p x) → ∑ x, q x = 1 → ∑ x, p x = 1 → ∑ x, q x ^ 2 / p x = 1 + GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq q p
GFNBounds.Silva.sum_sq_div_eq_one_add_ch.doc:
`∑_x q(x)²/p(x) = 1 + χ²(q‖p)`, the identity the factor `1 + χ²` of `eq:silva_bound` stands
for. It is the place the normalizations `∑ q = 1` and `∑ p = 1` are consumed.

GFNBounds.Silva.star_tv.doc: **`TV(p_T,π) = ⅛`** for the star witness, for every `K`.

GFNBounds.Silva.star_energy.type:
∀ {K : ℕ},
  0 < K →
    GFNBounds.Silva.residual (GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K)
        (GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB (GFNBounds.Silva.Star K)) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K) =
      (Real.log (3 / 2) ^ 2 + Real.log 2 ^ 2) / (↑K + 2)
GFNBounds.Silva.star_energy.doc:
**`𝓔(p_F) = ((log 3/2)² + (log 2)²)/(K+2)`** for the star witness: the log-ratios vanish on
the `bᵢ`.

GFNBounds.Silva.star_chiSq.doc: `χ²(q_{E,T}‖p_{E,T}) = 0`: the training distribution *is* the uniform one.

GFNBounds.Silva.star_Mprime.type:
∀ {K : ℕ},
  0 < K →
    GFNBounds.Silva.MprimeLe (GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB (GFNBounds.Silva.Star K)) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K)
      (GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K) 1
GFNBounds.Silva.star_Mprime.doc:
**`M' ≤ 1`** for the star witness. The paper's parenthetical `M = ⅜`, `‖π‖_∞ = ¼` holds
for `K ≥ 2`; at `K = 1` the filler weight `1/(2K) = ½` is the largest, so `M = ½`. Either way
`M' ≤ 1`, which is all the statement claims, and `K` is taken large.

GFNBounds.Silva.starPi_sum.type: ∀ {K : ℕ}, 0 < K → ∑ x, GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K x = 1

GFNBounds.Silva.starPi_pos.type: ∀ {K : ℕ}, 0 < K → ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Silva.Star K), 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K x

GFNBounds.Silva.starPi.doc: The target `π` of the star witness: `π(x*) = π(x') = ¼`, `π(bᵢ) = 1/(2K)`.

GFNBounds.Silva.starPF_sum.type: ∀ {K : ℕ}, 0 < K → ∑ x, GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K x = 1

GFNBounds.Silva.starPF_pos.type: ∀ {K : ℕ}, 0 < K → ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Silva.Star K), 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K x

GFNBounds.Silva.starPF.doc:
The forward policy of the star witness: `p_F(s_o→x*) = ⅜`, `p_F(s_o→x') = ⅛`,
`p_F(s_o→bᵢ) = 1/(2K)`.

GFNBounds.Silva.starPET_pos.type: ∀ (K : ℕ) (x : GFNBounds.Silva.Star K), 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K x

GFNBounds.Silva.starPET.doc: The uniform training distribution on the `K+2` terminals.

GFNBounds.Silva.sq_sub_weighted_le.type:
∀ {T : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype T] {w f : T → ℝ} {c : ℝ},
  (∀ (τ : T), 0 ≤ w τ) → ∑ τ, w τ = 1 → (c - ∑ τ, w τ * f τ) ^ 2 ≤ ∑ τ, w τ * (c - f τ) ^ 2
GFNBounds.Silva.sq_sub_weighted_le.doc:
For a probability weight `w` on a finite set, `(c − ∑ w f)² ≤ ∑ w (c − f)²`. With
`w = p_B(·|x)`, `f = p_F/p_B` and `c = π(x)` this is the second display of the proof of
`prop:silva_explicit`.

GFNBounds.Silva.sq_sub_le_sq_mul_log_sq.type: ∀ {a b C : ℝ}, 0 < a → 0 < b → a ≤ C → b ≤ C → (a - b) ^ 2 ≤ C ^ 2 * Real.log (a / b) ^ 2
GFNBounds.Silva.sq_sub_le_sq_mul_log_sq.doc:
The squared form used in the proof: `(a − b)² ≤ C² (log(a/b))²` for `0 < a ≤ C`,
`0 < b ≤ C`.

GFNBounds.Silva.residual_eq.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] (pET π : X → ℝ) (pB : X → T → ℝ) (pF : T → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF = ∑ x, pET x * ∑ t, pB x t * Real.log (pF t / (π x * pB x t)) ^ 2
GFNBounds.Silva.residual_eq.doc: `residual` with the log written out, for rewriting.

GFNBounds.Silva.residual.type: {X : Type u_1} → {T : Type u_2} → [Fintype X] → [Fintype T] → (X → ℝ) → (X → ℝ) → (X → T → ℝ) → (T → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Silva.residual.doc:
The residual `𝓔(p_F) = E_{x∼p_{E,T}} E_{τ∼p_B(·|x)}[(log(p_F(τ)/(π(x) p_B(τ|x))))²]`
of `silva_comparison.tex:24–26`. Off the support of `p_B(·|x)` the factor `p_B(τ|x)` kills the
term, which is the intended reading of the inner expectation.

GFNBounds.Silva.no_three_argument_bound.type:
¬∃ F,
    Filter.Tendsto (fun e => F e 0 1) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ (X T : Type) [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] (pET : X → ℝ) (pB : X → T → ℝ) (pF : T → ℝ) (π pT : X → ℝ)
        (c : ℝ),
        (∀ (x : X), 0 < π x) →
          ∑ x, π x = 1 →
            (∀ (x : X), 0 < pET x) →
              ∑ x, pET x = 1 →
                (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 ≤ pB x t) →
                  (∀ (x : X), ∑ t, pB x t = 1) →
                    (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 < pB x t → 0 < pF t) →
                      (∀ (x : X), pT x = ∑ t, pB x t * (pF t / pB x t)) →
                        GFNBounds.Silva.MprimeLe pB pF π c →
                          GFNBounds.Silva.tv pT π ≤
                            F (GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF)
                              (GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq (GFNBounds.Silva.unif X) pET) c
GFNBounds.Silva.no_three_argument_bound.doc:
**`prop:silva_no_uniform`, the "in particular" in the paper's three-argument form**: no
`F(𝓔, χ², M')` with `F(·,0,1) → 0` bounds `TV`, when `F`'s third slot may be fed any bound on
`M'`. See SCOPE for why the third slot is quantified rather than evaluated at the instance's
own `M'`.

GFNBounds.Silva.no_state_space_free_boun.type:
¬∃ F,
    Filter.Tendsto F (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ (X T : Type) [inst : Fintype X] [inst_1 : Fintype T] (pET : X → ℝ) (pB : X → T → ℝ) (pF : T → ℝ) (π pT : X → ℝ),
        (∀ (x : X), 0 < π x) →
          ∑ x, π x = 1 →
            (∀ (x : X), 0 < pET x) →
              ∑ x, pET x = 1 →
                (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 ≤ pB x t) →
                  (∀ (x : X), ∑ t, pB x t = 1) →
                    (∀ (x : X) (t : T), 0 < pB x t → 0 < pF t) →
                      (∀ (x : X), pT x = ∑ t, pB x t * (pF t / pB x t)) →
                        GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq (GFNBounds.Silva.unif X) pET = 0 →
                          GFNBounds.Silva.MprimeLe pB pF π 1 →
                            GFNBounds.Silva.tv pT π ≤ F (GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π pB pF)
GFNBounds.Silva.no_state_space_free_boun.doc:
**`prop:silva_no_uniform`, the "in particular"**: no function of the residual alone,
vanishing as the residual vanishes, bounds the total variation over all finite instances with
`χ²(q_{E,T}‖p_{E,T}) = 0` and `M' ≤ 1`.

GFNBounds.Silva.log_sq_sum_le_one.doc:
`(log 3/2)² + (log 2)² ≤ 1`: `log(3/2) ≤ 1/2` because `log x ≤ x − 1`, and
`log 2 < 0.6931471808` by `Real.log_two_lt_d9`; the sum of squares is at most `0.7305`.

GFNBounds.Silva.logRatio.type: {X : Type u_1} → {T : Type u_2} → (X → ℝ) → (X → T → ℝ) → (T → ℝ) → X → T → ℝ
GFNBounds.Silva.logRatio.doc:
The log-ratio `ℓ(τ) = log (p_F(τ) / (π(x) p_B(τ|x)))` of the proof at
`silva_comparison.tex:89`.

GFNBounds.Silva.logLipschitz.type: ∀ {a b C : ℝ}, 0 < a → 0 < b → a ≤ C → b ≤ C → |a - b| ≤ C * |Real.log a - Real.log b|
GFNBounds.Silva.logLipschitz.doc:
`|a − b| ≤ C |log a − log b|` for `0 < a ≤ C` and `0 < b ≤ C`. This is the third display of
the proof of `prop:silva_explicit`; `C` is the paper's `M' = max(M, ‖π‖_∞)`, and the hypothesis
`b ≤ C` is exactly what is unavailable for `C = M`, since `π(x) ≤ M` is not implied by the
definition of `M` — item 5 of `rem:silva_hypotheses`.

GFNBounds.Silva.hdom_deltaPB.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq X] [inst_1 : Fintype X] (pF : X → ℝ) (x : X),
  pF x = ∑ t, GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X x t * (pF t / GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X x t)
GFNBounds.Silva.hdom_deltaPB.doc: The domination identity holds for the one-parent kernel, with `p_T = p_F`.

GFNBounds.Silva.exists_star_witness.type:
∀ {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∃ K,
      0 < K ∧
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Silva.Star K), 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K x) ∧
          (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Silva.Star K), 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K x) ∧
            ∑ x, GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K x = 1 ∧
              ∑ x, GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K x = 1 ∧
                (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Silva.Star K), 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K x) ∧
                  ∑ x, GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K x = 1 ∧
                    GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq (GFNBounds.Silva.unif (GFNBounds.Silva.Star K)) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K) =
                        0 ∧
                      GFNBounds.Silva.MprimeLe (GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB (GFNBounds.Silva.Star K))
                          (GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K) 1 ∧
                        0 <
                            GFNBounds.Silva.residual (GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K)
                              (GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB (GFNBounds.Silva.Star K)) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K) ∧
                          GFNBounds.Silva.residual (GFNBounds.Silva.starPET K) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K)
                                (GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB (GFNBounds.Silva.Star K)) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K) ≤
                              ε ∧
                            GFNBounds.Silva.tv (GFNBounds.Silva.starPF K) (GFNBounds.Silva.starPi K) = 1 / 8
GFNBounds.Silva.exists_star_witness.doc:
**`prop:silva_no_uniform`(ii)**: for every `ε > 0` the star witness with `K` large has
`χ² = 0`, `M' ≤ 1`, `𝓔(p_F) ≤ ε` and `TV(p_T,π) = ⅛`. The `K` is effective — the proof takes
`K = ⌈1/ε⌉₊ + 1`, since `𝓔 = ((log 3/2)² + (log 2)²)/(K+2) ≤ 1/(K+2)`.

GFNBounds.Silva.energy_deltaPB.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq X] [inst_1 : Fintype X] (pET pF π : X → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Silva.residual pET π (GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X) pF = ∑ x, pET x * Real.log (pF x / π x) ^ 2
GFNBounds.Silva.energy_deltaPB.doc: `𝓔(p_F)` for the one-parent kernel: one term per terminal state.

GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB_sum.type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq X] [inst_1 : Fintype X] (x : X), ∑ t, GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X x t = 1

GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB_pos_iff.type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq X] {x t : X}, 0 < GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X x t ↔ t = x

GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB_nonneg.type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq X] (x t : X), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X x t

GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB.congr_simp.type:
∀ (X : Type u_2) {inst : DecidableEq X} [inst_1 : DecidableEq X] (a a_1 : X),
  a = a_1 → ∀ (a_2 a_3 : X), a_2 = a_3 → GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X a a_2 = GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB X a_1 a_3

GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB.type: (X : Type u_2) → [DecidableEq X] → X → X → ℝ
GFNBounds.Silva.deltaPB.doc:
The backward kernel of a graph in which each terminal `x` has one incoming trajectory,
identified with `x` itself: `p_B(τ|x) = 1` for `τ = x` and `0` otherwise.

GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq_self.type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype X] (p : X → ℝ), GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq p p = 0
GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq_self.doc: `χ²(p‖p) = 0`: the training law that *is* the uniform one has no `χ²` term.

GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq_nonneg.type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype X] {q p : X → ℝ}, (∀ (x : X), 0 ≤ p x) → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq q p
GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq_nonneg.doc:
`χ²(q‖p) ≥ 0` whenever `p ≥ 0`: the factor `1 + χ²` under the square root is nonnegative,
which is what lets the final Cauchy–Schwarz step be multiplied through.

GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq.type: {X : Type u_1} → [Fintype X] → (X → ℝ) → (X → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Silva.chiSq.doc:
The `χ²`-divergence in its standard finite form,
`χ²(q‖p) = ∑_x (q(x) − p(x))²/p(x)`.

GFNBounds.Silva.abs_exp_sub_one_le.type: ∀ {u s : ℝ}, |u| ≤ s → |Real.exp u - 1| ≤ Real.exp s - 1
GFNBounds.Silva.abs_exp_sub_one_le.doc:
If `|u| ≤ s` then `|e^u − 1| ≤ e^s − 1`: the upper half is monotonicity of `exp`, the lower
half is `1 − e^{−s} ≤ s ≤ e^s − 1`.

GFNBounds.Silva.Star.doc:
The terminal states of the star DAG: `x* = inl false`, `x' = inl true`, and the `K` filler
states `b₁,…,b_K = inr i`.

GFNBounds.Silva.MprimeLe.type: {X : Type u_1} → {T : Type u_2} → [Fintype X] → [Fintype T] → (X → T → ℝ) → (T → ℝ) → (X → ℝ) → ℝ → Prop
GFNBounds.Silva.MprimeLe.doc:
`M' ≤ c`, with `M' = max(M, ‖π‖_∞)` and `M = max{p_F(τ)/p_B(τ|x) : p_B(τ|x) > 0}`
(`silva_comparison.tex:32`), unfolded into its two halves.

GFNBounds.Graph.visits.congr_simp.type:

Finiteness of `𝒱` is *not* a field: it is the instance `[Fintype V]`, required only where a sum
over the vertices is taken.

GFNBounds.Graph.Leveled.isHitExp.doc:
**On a leveled graph the height *is* the hitting time.** Off `s₀` every backward step drops
the height by exactly one, so `ℓ = 1 + Qℓ`; with `ℓ(s₀) = 0` that is the hitting system, and by
uniqueness `E(σ ∣ X₀ = ·) = ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Graph.Leveled.bsigma_le.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableEq V]
  {B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G} (L : GFNBounds.Graph.Leveled G),
  G.PathConnected →
    ∀ {N : V → ℝ},
      0 < GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G N →
        GFNBounds.Graph.sigmaStar G L.lvl * √((2 + B.sigmaBar L.lvl) / GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G N) ≤
          (L.lvl G.snk + 1) * √((2 + L.lvl G.snk) / GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G N)
GFNBounds.Graph.Leveled.bsigma_le.doc:
**The leveled witness for `B̂_σ`** (`proofs.tex:855`): with `t_m := ℓ(s_f)`,
`B̂_σ ≤ (t_m + 1)√((2 + t_m)/min_x N(x))` — a finite bound with no aperiodicity anywhere, on the
graphs where the paper says the mixing constant `B̂` is infinite.

Sharper on this reading of *leveled*: `σ_* = t_m` and `σ̄ = t_m − 1` exactly
(`sigmaStar_eq`, `sigmaBar_eq`). The paper's looser form is stated because its `σ(s_f) ≤ t_m + 1`
points to a convention one shorter than this one; see the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.Leveled.type: {V : Type u_1} → GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V → Type u_1
GFNBounds.Graph.Leveled.doc:
A **leveled** marked graph: a height rising by exactly one along every edge, with the source
at height `0`. Every source-to-sink walk then has the same length `ℓ(s_f)`, which is the paper's
`t_m`. The height is real-valued so that `ℓ(y) = ℓ(x) − 1` needs no truncation.

GFNBounds.Graph.IsCirculation.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → Prop
GFNBounds.Graph.IsCirculation.doc:
**A `0`-flow**, in the sense `eq:def_stability` quantifies over
(`cv_divergence.tex:179–181`): an edgeflow that neither creates nor destroys mass at any vertex,
i.e. a circulation.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl_pos.type: ∀ {M : ℝ}, 0 < M → ∀ (x : Fin 5), 0 < GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M x

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl.doc:
The over-inflated density of the remark: `u = M` on the cycle `{x₁,x₂,x₃}` and `u = 1` at the
two marks. It is `dμ/dλ`, as in `prop:no_distant_equilibrium`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.two_add_sig.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  2 + (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p) =
    (5 - 2 * p) / (1 - p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.two_add_sig.doc: `2 + σ̄ = (5−2p)/(1−p)`, the expected length of one loop-closed excursion.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaStar_e.type:
∀ {p : ℝ},
  0 < p →
    p < 1 →
      GFNBounds.Graph.sigmaStar GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p) =
        (4 - p) / (1 - p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaStar_e.doc: `σ_* = max_x E(σ ∣ X₀ = x) = (4−p)/(1−p)`, attained at `s_f`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaBar_un.doc:
**`σ̄` is unbounded on `(0,1)`** — the certified half of the remark's closing clause "as
`p → 1` the backward-length bound blows up". The witness is explicit: `p = 1 − 3/(|C|+4)`. That
`B̂` blows up too is an operator-norm statement and is not stated; see the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaBar_ne.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p) ≠ (1 + 2 * p) / (1 - p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaBar_ne.doc:
**The value the remark used to give for `σ̄` is not `σ̄`.** `3/(1−p) = (1+2p)/(1−p)` forces `p = 1`, which the
hypothesis excludes, so the two disagree at *every* `p ∈ (0,1)`. Both are finite and both diverge
as `p → 1`, which is all the remark uses the number for.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaBar_eq.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p) = 3 / (1 - p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.sigmaBar_eq.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 1, corrected.** The expected backward-trajectory length
`σ̄ = E_{x ∼ π̂_←(s_f→·)} E(σ ∣ X₀ = x)` of `prop:morozov_rate` is `3/(1−p)`: the target row
`π̂_←(s_f→·)` is the point mass at `x₃`, so `σ̄ = E(σ ∣ X₀ = x₃)`, and a backward excursion runs
`x₃ → x₂ → x₁` and leaves to `s₀` with probability `1 − p` each lap.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_x3_te.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun M =>
      GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 3)
    Filter.atTop (nhds p)

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_x3.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 3 =
      p + (1 - p) / M
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_x3.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 3 at `x₃`**: `r(x₃) = p + (1−p)/M` exactly, hence `→ p`.
This is the remark's *persistent leak-ratio at the junction*: the cycle feeds `x₃` with the
fraction `p` of the inflated mass, and the un-inflated `s_f` supplies the rest.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_x2.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 2 =
      1

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_x1.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 1 =
      1
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_x1.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 3 at `x₁`**: `r(x₁) = 1` *exactly*, at every `M` — the
remark's `→ 1` is attained, not approached. Mass enters `x₁` only from `x₂`, and `λ(x₁) = λ(x₂)`,
`u(x₁) = u(x₂)`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_src_t.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  Filter.Tendsto

      GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0)
    Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_src_t.doc: **`r(s₀) → ∞`** as `M → ∞`, linearly — the starved source of the remark.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_src.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0 =

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_src.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 3 at `s₀`**: on the paper's own convention `u = dμ/dλ`
(`prop:no_distant_equilibrium`), `r(s₀) = M` *exactly*. The remark's `M(1−p)` is the counting
reading — see `ratio_counting_src` — the factor `(1−p)` being already carried by `λ(s₀)`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_snk.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 4 =
      1
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_snk.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 3 at `s_f`**: `r(s_f) = 1` exactly. The wrap edge carries
`λ(s₀)u(s₀)` into `s_f`, and `λ(s_f) = λ(s₀)`, `u(s_f) = u(s₀) = 1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_count.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (fun x => 1)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 3 =
      p + 1 / M
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_count.doc: `r(x₃) = p + 1/M` against the counting measure — the same limit `p`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_count.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (fun x => 1)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0 =
      M * (1 - p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_count.doc:
**`r(s₀) = M(1−p)`, the remark's own value**, obtained by reading `u` as the density against
the counting measure rather than against `λ`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_count.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (fun x => 1)
          (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 1 =
        1 ∧
      GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (fun x => 1)
            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 2 =
          1 ∧
        GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (fun x => 1)
            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 4 =
          1
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.ratio_count.doc: `r(x₁) = r(x₂) = r(s_f) = 1` against the counting measure too.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.positiveOnE.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the frozen policy is positive on the edges** — the hypothesis of
`theo:universality_graphs` and of `prop:morozov_rate`. This is where `0 < p` (the edge `x₃ → x₁`)
and `p < 1` (the edge `s₀ → x₁`) are consumed; the other three edges carry probability `1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol.congr_s.type:
∀ {p p_1 : ℝ} (e_p : p = p_1) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1 = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol ⋯ ⋯

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the frozen policy as a `BackwardPolicy`.** Of the three fields
only non-negativity constrains `p`, and it asks for `0 ≤ p` and `p ≤ 1`; the row sum
`(1−p) + p = 1` at `x₁` and the support condition are identities. The *strict* halves are the
binders because every statement below consumes one of them — `0 < p` for `PositiveOnEdges` at the
edge `x₃ → x₁`, `p < 1` for it at `s₀ → x₁` and for `1 − p ≠ 0` in every closed form.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.phat_eq.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.kern p

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pbFun.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the frozen policy**: `π_←(x₁→x₃) = p`, `π_←(x₁→s₀) = 1−p`, and
the three remaining rows deterministic — `π_←(x₂→x₁) = π_←(x₃→x₂) = π_←(s_f→x₃) = 1`. The `s₀`
row is left at `0`, the paper leaving `π_←(s₀→·)` undefined; `phat` overwrites it.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pathConnect.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate` is path-connected** (`def:path_connected`), the hypothesis every
result cited below carries. The single walk `s₀ → x₁ → x₂ → x₃ → s_f` passes through all five
vertices, so each vertex is split off it.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.no_stalemat.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  1 < M →
    ∀ {w : Fin 5 → ℝ},
      (∀ (x : Fin 5), 0 < w x) →
        (GFNBounds.Balance.gradMass (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) w fun x => 2 * Real.log x / x) <
          0
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.no_stalemat.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 4**: at the over-inflated configuration the total mass of
the gradient density is *strictly* negative, for every training measure of positive density. So
the frozen-policy constraint and the inflation force do not cancel — "*the candidate stalemate
between the two forces never forms (consistently with the mass identity)*".

The proof is the remark's own: `prop:no_distant_equilibrium`*(1)* makes the mass `≤ 0` with
equality only at balance, and `ratio_x3` shows this configuration is not balanced — `r(x₃)` is
`p + (1−p)/M < 1` at every `M > 1`. The generator enters only through
`g' = 2 log x / x`, strictly unimodal by `Balance.strictlyUnimodal_logSqDeriv`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.minOver_vis.type:
∀ {p : ℝ},
  0 < p →
    p < 1 →
      GFNBounds.Graph.minOver GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc
          (GFNBounds.Graph.visits GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.green p)) =
        1
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.minOver_vis.doc: `N ≡ 1/(1−p)` on the cycle and `N(s₀) = N(s_f) = 1`, so `min_x N(x) = 1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam_src_eq_.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 0 =
    1 / (2 + (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p))
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam_src_eq_.doc:
**`prop:morozov_rate`*(1)* at `s₀`, on this graph**: `λ(s₀) = 1/(2+σ̄)`. Read backwards with
claim 2's `λ(s₀) = (1−p)/(5−2p)`, this *forces* `σ̄ = 3/(1−p)`; the old `(1+2p)/(1−p)` would
give `λ(s₀) = (1−p)/3`, which is claim 2 only at `p = 1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam_pos.type: ∀ {p : ℝ}, p < 1 → ∀ (x : Fin 5), 0 < GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p x

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam.doc:
The invariant probability of the backward chain: `q = 1/(5−2p)` at each of `x₁, x₂, x₃` and
`(1−p)q` at `s₀` and `s_f`. Normalization fixes `q`, which the remark leaves free.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.kern.doc:
The loop-closed kernel `π̂_←` of the remark, written out: the wrap row `π̂_←(s₀→s_f) = 1`
(`def:loop_closure`) on top of `pbFun`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.isInvProb.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).IsInvProb (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.isInvProb.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 2**: `lam p` is an invariant probability of the loop-closed
backward chain. Stationarity at `x₃` is the one row the cycle enters — `q = qp + (1−p)q` — and at
`s₀` it is the leak `(1−p)q`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.isHitExp.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).IsHitExp (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.isHitExp.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the backward-trajectory length**: `hitExp p` solves the linear
system `IsHitExp` of `prop:morozov_rate` — `u(s₀) = 0` and `u = 1 + Qu` off `s₀`. Each row is one
`field_simp`; the cycle closes at `x₁`, where `u(x₁) = 1 + p·u(x₃)` and `1 − p ≠ 0` is what makes
the system solvable.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.isGreen.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).IsGreen (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.green p)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.isGreen.doc:
**`green p` solves `prop:morozov_rate`'s renewal equation** `g(s₀) = 0`,
`g = π̂_←(s_f→·) + gP̂` off `s₀`. The source term lands at `x₃`, the only in-neighbour of `s_f`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.invProb_pap.type:
∀ {p : ℝ},
  p < 1 →
    ∃ q,
      0 < q ∧
        GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 1 = q ∧
          GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 2 = q ∧
            GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 3 = q ∧
              GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 0 = (1 - p) * q ∧ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 4 = (1 - p) * q
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.invProb_pap.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 2 in the remark's own words**: there is a `q > 0` with mass
`q` at each of the three cycle states and `(1−p)q` at `s₀` and at `s_f`. Here `q = 1/(5−2p)`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.invProb_eq.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) {l : Fin 5 → ℝ},
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).IsInvProb l → l = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.invProb_eq.doc: **`theo:universality_graphs`*(1)* on this graph**: `lam p` is *the* invariant probability.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.inflation_f.type: Filter.Tendsto (fun M => 2 * Real.log M) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.inflation_f.doc:
**… and it *grows*, not vanishes, with the imbalance**: `2 log M → ∞`. This is the whole of
the remark's "*growing, not vanishing*"; the *rate* at which the source refills is a statement
about the gradient flow and is not stated.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.inflation_f.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  0 < M →
    2 *
            Real.log
              (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0) /
          GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0 *
        GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p)
          (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0 =
      2 * Real.log M
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.inflation_f.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, claim 4, the magnitude**: for `g = (log x)²`, so
`g'(x) = 2 log x / x`, the force at the starved source is `|g'(r)r| = 2 log r(s₀) = 2 log M`
exactly (on the counting reading it is `2 log(M(1−p))`, the same to leading order).

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp_x1.doc:
**The number the remark printed before its 2026-09-08 correction**, `(1+2p)/(1−p)`, is
`E(σ ∣ X₀ = x₁)` — the expected hitting
time of `s₀` from the far end of the cycle, not the backward-trajectory length.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp_uniq.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) {u : Fin 5 → ℝ},
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).IsHitExp u → u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp_uniq.doc: `hitExp p` is *the* solution: `prop:morozov_rate`'s system has at most one.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp.doc:
`E(σ ∣ X₀ = ·)`, the hitting time of `s₀` by the backward chain, in closed form: `0` at `s₀`,
`(1+2p)/(1−p)` at `x₁`, `(2+p)/(1−p)` at `x₂`, `3/(1−p)` at `x₃` and `(4−p)/(1−p)` at `s_f`.
Characterized, not constructed — see the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.green.doc:
The occupation measure `N` of `prop:morozov_rate`, killed at `s₀`: `g ≡ 1/(1−p)` on the cycle
and `0` at the two marks. Characterized by the renewal equation `IsGreen`, not constructed.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.edgeB.doc: The edges of the remark's graph: `s₀ → x₁`, the cycle `x₁ → x₂ → x₃ → x₁`, and `x₃ → s_f`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cycle_no_st.type:
∀ {p M : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  1 < M →
    ∀ {w : Fin 5 → ℝ},
      (∀ (x : Fin 5), 0 < w x) →
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p) = 3 / (1 - p) ∧
          (∃ q,
              0 < q ∧
                GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 1 = q ∧
                  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 2 = q ∧
                    GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 3 = q ∧
                      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 0 = (1 - p) * q ∧
                        GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p 4 = (1 - p) * q) ∧
            (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                    (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 1 =
                  1 ∧
                GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                      (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 2 =
                    1 ∧
                  GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 4 =
                      1 ∧
                    GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                          (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 3 =
                        p + (1 - p) / M ∧
                      GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                          (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) 0 =
                        M) ∧
              (GFNBounds.Balance.gradMass (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).phat
                  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.lam p) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.uInfl M) w fun x =>
                  2 * Real.log x / x) <
                0
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cycle_no_st.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`** (`proofs.tex:816–818`), its four claims at once, on the graph
`cyc` with the frozen policy `pol` and the over-inflated density `uInfl M`.

Two departures from the printed text, both disclosed in the module docstring and neither touching
what the remark concludes. Claim 1 is stated with the **corrected** backward-trajectory length
`σ̄ = 3/(1−p)` — the formerly printed `(1+2p)/(1−p)` is `E(σ ∣ X₀ = x₁)`, `hitExp_x1` — and claim 3's
`r(s₀)` is stated on the paper's own convention `u = dμ/dλ`, where it is exactly `M`; the printed
`M(1−p)` is the counting reading, `ratio_counting_src`. Claim 4 is stated as what the mass
identity delivers: the two forces do not cancel, the gradient mass being *strictly* negative.
The remark's dynamical readings — the `M/log M` transient, the handover to
`theo:local_convergence`, `B̂ → ∞` as `p → 1` — are not stated; see the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc.doc:
**`rem:cycle_no_stalemate`, the graph**: `𝒱 = {s₀,x₁,x₂,x₃,s_f}` with `s₀ → x₁`, the cycle
`x₁ → x₂ → x₃ → x₁` and `x₃ → s_f`. The two marks `s₀ = 0` and `s_f = 4` carry no incoming resp.
outgoing edge, which `decide` settles.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.bSigma_eq.type:
∀ {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1),
  GFNBounds.Graph.sigmaStar GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p) *
      √((2 + (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.pol hp0 hp1).sigmaBar (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.hitExp p)) /
          GFNBounds.Graph.minOver GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc
            (GFNBounds.Graph.visits GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.cyc (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.green p))) =
    (4 - p) / (1 - p) * √((5 - 2 * p) / (1 - p))
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.bSigma_eq.doc:
**`prop:morozov_rate`*(2)* on this graph, with the constant computed**:
`B̂_σ = σ_*√((2+σ̄)/min N) = ((4−p)/(1−p))·√((5−2p)/(1−p))`, finite at every `p ∈ (0,1)`. This is
what "*the condition of Morozov et al. holds and the circulation cannot explode*" buys in the
paper's own variables; the dynamical reading of that sentence is not stated (see SCOPE).

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleExample.Edge.doc: The edge relation of the remark's graph, as a decidable `Prop`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC_ne_sr.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (i : Fin (M + 2)), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i ≠ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC_ne_sn.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (i : Fin (M + 2)), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i ≠ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC_inj.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} {i j : Fin (M + 2)}, GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M j ↔ i = j

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC.doc: The internal state `x_{i+1}`; `xC M 0` is the paper's `x₁` and `xC M 1` its `x₂`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] (a b u : V),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b u b = if u = a then 1 else 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] {a b u v : V},
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b u v ≠ 0 → u = a ∧ v = b
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] (a b u v : V), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b u v

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] (a b v : V),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b a v = if v = b then 1 else 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] {a b v : V},
  v ≠ b → ∀ (u : V), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b u v = 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] {a b u : V},
  u ≠ a → ∀ (v : V), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b u v = 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] {a b u v : V},
  ¬(u = a ∧ v = b) → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b u v = 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} {inst : DecidableEq V} [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] (a a_1 : V),
  a = a_1 →
    ∀ (b b_1 : V),
      b = b_1 →
        ∀ (a_2 a_3 : V),
          a_2 = a_3 →
            ∀ (a_4 a_5 : V),
              a_4 = a_5 →
                GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b a_2 a_4 =
                  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a_1 b_1 a_3 a_5
{V : Type u_1} → [DecidableEq V] → V → V → V → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge.doc:
The edgeflow carrying mass `1` on the single transition `a → b` and nothing elsewhere. Every
flow below is a finite sum of these.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin_te.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) {delta : ℝ},
  0 ≤ delta →
    delta ≤ 1 →
      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin
          (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M)
            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k))
          (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) =
        1 - delta / (↑M + 1)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin_te.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the total variation is `1 − δ/(N−1)`** (`proofs.tex:390`):
`TV(δ_{x₂} ‖ target) = 1 − target(x₂)`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : MeasurableSpace V] [MeasurableSingletonClass V] (p q : V → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin p q = GFNBounds.Core.tvD MeasureTheory.Measure.count p q
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin_eq.doc:
**`tvFin` is `GFNBounds.Core.tvD` against the counting measure** — the `½`-convention TV of
`app:notation` read on a finite state space, so the value `1 − δ/(N−1)` above is the paper's
`TV(s_τ ‖ target)` and not a separate notion.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin.doc:
The `½`-convention total variation of `app:notation` between two densities on a finite state
space, `TV(p‖q) = ½ ∑ |p − q|`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw_.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (x : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M)
      (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) x =
    if x = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 1 then 1 else 0
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw_.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the terminal law is `δ_{x₂}` for every `k`**
(`proofs.tex:388`): the circulation charges no terminal edge, so `F_k` and `F̂` have the same
terminal flow `μ = δ_{x₂}`, of mass `1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V → (V → V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw.doc:
The **normalized terminal flow** of an edgeflow, `F(·→s_f)/F(𝒮→s_f)`. This is the law
`theo:sampling_theorem` identifies with `s_τ`; that identification is cited, not proved — see the
module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tendsto_.type: ∀ (a b : ℝ), Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (a + k) / (b + k)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tendsto_.doc:
**`ρ_k → 1`** (`proofs.tex:395`): a quotient of two affine functions of `k` with the same
slope tends to `1`, whatever the intercepts — this is the scale invariance along `0`-flows.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC_.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (delta : ℝ), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) = 0
∀ {M : ℕ} (delta : ℝ), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) = 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the target** (`proofs.tex:387`): `target(x₁) = 1 − δ` and
`target(xᵢ) = δ/(N−1)` for `i ≥ 2`, with `N − 1 = M + 1`. The two marks carry no target mass —
the target is a measure on the internal state space `𝒮`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_term.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ), ∑ y, GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k y (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) = 1

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_targ.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (delta : ℝ), ∑ v, GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta v = 1
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_targ.doc: **The target is a probability measure on `𝒮`**: `(1 − δ) + (N − 1)·δ/(N − 1) = 1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_inte.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (F : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ)
  (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  ∑ v ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal, F u v =
    GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow F u - F u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) -
      F u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M)

∀ {M : ℕ} (f : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ),
  ∑ x ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal, f x = ∑ i, f (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_inte.doc: A sum over `𝒮` is a sum over the `N` internal indices.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_fin_.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (A B : ℝ), (∑ i, if i = 0 then A else B) = A + (↑M + 1) * B
∀ {M : ℕ} (A B C : ℝ), (∑ i, if i = 0 then A else if i = 1 then B else C) = A + B + ↑M * C

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_cycV.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (f : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ),
  ∑ v, f v =
    f (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) +
      (f (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) + ∑ i, f (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i))
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.sum_cycV.doc: Every sum over the vertices splits into the two marks and the `N` internal states.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC_ne_.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (i : Fin (M + 2)), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M ≠ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC_ne_.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (i : Fin (M + 2)), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M ≠ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.ratio_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] [inst_1 : Fintype V] (G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V) (target : V → ℝ)
  (F : V → V → ℝ),
  (∀ (x : V), target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v = 0 → ∀ (y : V), F x y = 0) →
    ∀ (y : V),
      GFNBounds.Balance.ratio (fun x y => F x y / (target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v))
          (fun x => target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v) 1 y =
        GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio G target F y
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.ratio_eq.doc:
**The ratio `ρ` is `GFNBounds.Balance`'s `r = d(μT)/dμ`** at `λ := target + f_→`, `u := 1`
and the kernel `T(x→y) := F(x→y)/λ(x)` normalising each row of the flow. The hypothesis is the
only thing that can go wrong: where `λ` vanishes the kernel is Lean's `x/0 = 0` and the row is
lost, so the row of `F` there must already be empty.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.no_bound.type:
∀ (M : ℕ) (g : ℝ → ℝ),
  g 1 = 0 →
    ContinuousAt g 1 →
      ∀ (nu : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ) {eps : ℝ},
        0 < eps →
          ∀ {eta : ℝ},
            eta < 1 →
              ∃ delta F,
                0 < delta ∧
                  delta < 1 ∧
                    (∀ (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), 0 ≤ F u v) ∧
                      (∀ (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
                          F u v ≠ 0 → (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).Edge u v) ∧
                        (∀ x ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal,
                            GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow F x = GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow F x) ∧
                          GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTarget (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M) g nu
                                (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) F ≤
                              eps ∧
                            eta <
                              GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin
                                (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M) F)
                                (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.no_bound.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the `= 1` reading**: the supremum is not attained but is `1`,
because `δ` is free. For every `η < 1` some `δ ∈ (0,1)` puts a flow of loss `≤ ε` at total
variation more than `η` from its target.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.no_bound.type:
∀ (M : ℕ) (g : ℝ → ℝ),
  g 1 = 0 →
    ContinuousAt g 1 →
      ∀ (nu : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ) {delta eps : ℝ},
        0 < delta →
          delta < 1 →
            0 < eps →
              ∃ F,
                (∀ (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), 0 ≤ F u v) ∧
                  (∀ (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
                      F u v ≠ 0 → (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).Edge u v) ∧
                    (∀ x ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal,
                        GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow F x = GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow F x) ∧
                      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTarget (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M) g nu
                            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) F ≤
                          eps ∧
                        GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.tvFin
                            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.termLaw (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M) F)
                            (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) =
                          1 - delta / (↑M + 1)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.no_bound.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`** — `cv_divergence.tex:7–19`, proof `proofs.tex:385–400` — on
the cyclic graph `𝒞_N`, `N = M + 2`.

For every generator `g` continuous at `1` with `g(1) = 0`, every training distribution `ν`, every
`δ ∈ (0,1)` and every `ε > 0` there is an edgeflow `F` on `𝒞_N` which is non-negative, rides on
the edges, is **exactly** flow-matching at every internal state, has FM loss at most `ε`, and
whose normalized terminal flow is at total variation `1 − δ/(N−1)` from the target. Letting
`δ → 0` (`no_bound_divergence_sup`) pushes that distance above every `η < 1`.

The construction does not depend on `ν`, which is the paper's "the construction being
independent of `ν_train`, the infimum over `ν_train` is also `1`".

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.mem_inte.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} {v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M},
  v ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal ↔ ∃ i, v = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.mem_inte.doc: Membership in `𝒮`, in the paper's names.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.isCircul.doc:
**`γ` is a `0`-flow** (`proofs.tex:388`): every internal state gains `1` and loses `1`, and
the cycle touches neither mark.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.internal.type:
∀ (M : ℕ),
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal =
    Finset.map { toFun := GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M, inj' := ⋯ } Finset.univ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.internal.doc: The internal state space `𝒮 = 𝒱 ∖ {s₀, s_f}` is exactly the `N` states `x₁,…,x_N`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.indicato.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (j : Fin (M + 2)),
  ((if j = 0 then 1 else 0) + if j = 1 then 1 else 0) = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.aC M j
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.indicato.doc: `aᵢ` is the sum of the two indicators `F̂` contributes to the inflow at `xᵢ`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaMC.doc:
**`γ` as the `MarkedCirculation` of `GFNBounds.Graph`** — the hypothesis bundle
`prop:frozen_unstable_full` consumes of its own `1_γ`, here discharged rather than assumed.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC_s.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) = 0

∀ {M : ℕ} (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) = 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC_n.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M u v

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC_a.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M u v =
    ∑ i,
      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M (i + 1)) u v

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC.type: (M : ℕ) → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the unit circulation `γ`** (`proofs.tex:388`): `γ = 1` on each
cycle edge `xᵢ → x_{i+1}`, `0` elsewhere.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.foutC_Fk.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)),
  ∑ v ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal,
      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M j) v =
    (if j = 0 then 1 else 0) + k
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.foutC_Fk.doc:
**The outflow half of the denominator**: `f^k_→(xᵢ) = 1_{i=1} + k`, the circulation adding
`k` at every internal state.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.foutC_Fk.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ),
  ∑ v ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal,
      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) v =
    1
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.foutC_Fk.doc: `F_k` sends unit mass out of `s₀`, along the initial edge: `F_init(𝒮) = 1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio_.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (delta : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)),
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun k =>
      GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k)
        (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M j))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

∀ {M : ℕ} (k delta : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M)
      (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k)
      (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M j) =
    (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.aC M j + k) / (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.bC M delta j + k)
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio_.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the closed form of the ratio** (`proofs.tex:395`):
`ρ_k(xᵢ) = (aᵢ + k)/(bᵢ + k)`, with `a₁ = a₂ = 1`, `aᵢ = 0` for `i ≥ 3`, `b₁ = 2 − δ` and
`bᵢ = δ/(N−1)` for `i ≥ 2`. At `x₁` the target mismatch `1 − δ` sits in `b₁ = 2 − δ`: it is what
the circulation drowns.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio..type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {inst : DecidableEq V} [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] [inst_2 : Fintype V]
  (G G_1 : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V),
  G = G_1 →
    ∀ (target target_1 : V → ℝ),
      target = target_1 →
        ∀ (F F_1 : V → V → ℝ),
          F = F_1 →
            ∀ (x x_1 : V),
              x = x_1 →
                GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio G target F x =
                  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio G_1 target_1 F_1 x_1

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio.type: {V : Type u_1} → [DecidableEq V] → [Fintype V] → GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V → (V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmRatio.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the ratio of the two sides of `equ:FM_const`**
(`proofs.tex:393`): `ρ(x) = (F_init + f_←)(x)/(target + f_→)(x)`, with the **target** in the
denominator in place of the flow's own terminal flow. On a marked graph `F_init + f_←` is the
total inflow `∑_u F(u → x)` — `s_f` emits nothing — and `f_→` is the outflow along the internal
edges, `∑_{v ∈ 𝒮} F(x → v)`. See the module SCOPE for why the denominator carries the target.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTa.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] [inst_1 : Fintype V] (G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V) (g : ℝ → ℝ)
  (nu target : V → ℝ) (F : V → V → ℝ),
  (∀ (x : V), target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v = 0 → ∀ (y : V), F x y = 0) →
    GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTarget G g nu target F =
      GFNBounds.Balance.loss (fun x y => F x y / (target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v))
        (fun x => target x + ∑ v ∈ G.internal, F x v) (fun x => if x ∈ G.internal then nu x else 0) 1 g
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTa.doc:
**`fmLossTarget` is `GFNBounds.Balance.loss`**, not a new notion: the divergence FM loss of
`theo:no_bound_divergence` is the library's `𝓛_{g,ν}(μ) = ∑_x ν(x) g(r(x))` at the kernel and
reference measure above, with `ν` extended by `0` off the internal states.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTa.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (g : ℝ → ℝ),
  g 1 = 0 →
    ContinuousAt g 1 →
      ∀ (nu : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ) (delta : ℝ),
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun k =>
            GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTarget (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M) g nu
              (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k))
          Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

{V : Type u_1} →
  [DecidableEq V] → [Fintype V] → GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V → (ℝ → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTa.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, a divergence-based FM loss** (`proofs.tex:393`):
`𝓛(F) = ∫ g(ρ) dν_train`, the integral over the internal states of a generator `g` of the ratio
of the two sides of the flow-matching constraint.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.exists_c.doc:
**The supremum ranges over graphs of size `N`**: for every `N ≥ 2` the family above contains
a graph with exactly `N` internal states, which is what `#𝒢 = N` asks.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.exists_F.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (g : ℝ → ℝ),
  g 1 = 0 →
    ContinuousAt g 1 →
      ∀ (nu : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ) (delta : ℝ) {eps : ℝ},
        0 < eps →
          ∃ k,
            0 ≤ k ∧
              GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.fmLossTarget (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M) g nu
                  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) ≤
                eps

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.edgeOutf.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] [inst_1 : Fintype V] (a b u : V),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b) u = if u = a then 1 else 0

∀ {M : ℕ} (i : Fin (M + 2)),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i) = 1

∀ {M : ℕ} (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M) u =
    ∑ i, if u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i then 1 else 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (F G : V → V → ℝ) (u : V),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (F + G) u = GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow F u + GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow G u

∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) u =
    GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M) u +
      k * GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M) u

∀ {M : ℕ} (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M) u =
    ((if u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M then 1 else 0) +
        if u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 0 then 1 else 0) +
      if u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 1 then 1 else 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.edgeInfl.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] [inst_1 : Fintype V] (a b v : V),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.unitEdge a b) v = if v = b then 1 else 0

∀ {M : ℕ} (j : Fin (M + 2)),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M j) = 1

∀ {M : ℕ} (v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M) v =
    ∑ i, if v = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M (i + 1) then 1 else 0

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (F G : V → V → ℝ) (v : V),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (F + G) v = GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow F v + GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow G v

∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (j : Fin (M + 2)),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M j) =
    GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.aC M j + k
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.edgeInfl.doc: **The numerator of `ρ_k` at an internal state**: `(F_init + f^k_←)(xᵢ) = aᵢ + k`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.edgeInfl.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) v =
    GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M) v +
      k * GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.gammaC M) v

∀ {M : ℕ} (v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M) v =
    ((if v = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 0 then 1 else 0) +
        if v = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 1 then 1 else 0) +
      if v = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M then 1 else 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV_cas.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} {p : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → Prop},
  p (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) →
    p (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) →
      (∀ (i : Fin (M + 2)), p (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M i)) →
        ∀ (v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), p v
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV_cas.doc: Case analysis on a vertex, in the paper's names.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV.doc:
The vertices of the cyclic graph `C_N`, `N = M + 2`: `none` is `s₀`, `some none` is `s_f`,
and `some (some i)` is the internal state `x_{i+1}`. Writing `N` as `M + 2` is how `N ≥ 2` is
carried: it makes `0` and `1` available in `Fin N` and `N − 1 = M + 1` non-zero.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} {u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M},
  (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).Edge u v ↔ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycEdge M u v

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the marked graph `𝒞_N`**: `s₀` receives no edge (the three
edge families all end at an internal state or at `s_f`) and `s_f` emits none.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycEdge.type: (M : ℕ) → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → Prop
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycEdge.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the graph `𝒞_N`** (`proofs.tex:387`): the initial edge
`s₀ → x₁`, a terminal edge `xᵢ → s_f` for every `i`, and the cycle edges `xᵢ → x_{i+1 mod N}`.
The wrap-around is `Fin N`'s own arithmetic: `(N−1) + 1 = 0`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.card_int.doc:
**`#𝒞_N = N`**: the graph has exactly `N = M + 2` internal states, which is what the
supremum of `theo:no_bound_divergence` ranges over.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_supp.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} {k : ℝ} {u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M},
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k u v ≠ 0 → (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).Edge u v
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_supp.doc:
Every transition `F_k` charges is an edge of `𝒞_N`: `F̂` rides on the initial edge, one
cycle edge and one terminal edge, and `γ` on the cycle.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_srcC.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) = 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_snk_r.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (y : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) y = 0
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_snk_r.doc: `s_f` emits nothing under `F_k` — it emits nothing in `𝒞_N`.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_snkC.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ) (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) =
    if u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 1 then 1 else 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_nonne.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} {k : ℝ},
  0 ≤ k → ∀ (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k u v

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_lam_n.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} {k delta : ℝ},
  0 ≤ k →
    0 < delta →
      delta < 1 →
        ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
          GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.targetC M delta x +
                ∑ v ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal,
                  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k x v =
              0 →
            ∀ (y : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k x y = 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_flowM.type:
∀ {M : ℕ} (k : ℝ),
  ∀ x ∈ (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycGraph M).internal,
    GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) x =
      GFNBounds.Graph.edgeOutflow (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk M k) x
GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk_flowM.doc:
**`F_k` is flow-matching for every `k`** (`proofs.tex:388`): the circulation adds `k` to the
inflow and `k` to the outflow of every internal state, so the constraint `equ:FM_const` at `𝒮`
— which on a marked graph is conservation at the internal states — is untouched.

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fk.type: (M : ℕ) → ℝ → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M → ℝ

  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.srcC M) = 0

∀ {M : ℕ} (u : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M),
  GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M u (GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.snkC M) =
    if u = GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.xC M 1 then 1 else 0

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat_non.type: ∀ {M : ℕ} (u v : GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.cycV M), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat M u v

GFNBounds.Graph.CycleDivergence.Fhat.doc:
**`theo:no_bound_divergence`, the flow `F̂`** (`proofs.tex:388`): the unit-mass flow routed
`s₀ → x₁ → x₂ → s_f`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.universal.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G),
  G.PathConnected →
    B.PositiveOnEdges →
      ∀ {lam : V → ℝ},
        B.IsInvProb lam →
          (∀ (pf : V → V → ℝ) (fout : V → ℝ),
              (∀ (u : V), ∑ v, pf u v = 1) →
                (∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ fout x) →
                  fout ≠ 0 →
                    B.FrozenBalance pf fout → ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ (∀ (x : V), fout x = c * lam x) ∧ pf = B.reversal lam) ∧
            (∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → B.FrozenBalance (B.reversal lam) fun x => c * lam x) ∧
              (∀ (u v : V), 0 ≤ B.reversal lam u v) ∧ ∀ (u : V), ∑ v, B.reversal lam u v = 1
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.universal.doc:
**`theo:universality_graphs`*(2)*** (`proofs.tex:970–974`, proof `proofs.tex:987–991`), in
one statement: apart from `f_out ≡ 0`, the frozen-backward family on the loop closure is exactly
the ray `f_out = c λ`, `c > 0`, carrying the `λ`-reversal — and the `λ`-reversal is a genuine
Markov kernel.

The first conjunct assumes of `π_→` only that its rows sum to `1`; the second and third *prove*
that the reversal is a non-negative kernel, so no member of the family is lost by the weakening.
See the module's modelling decisions.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.universal.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G),
  G.PathConnected →
    B.PositiveOnEdges →
      ∀ {lam : V → ℝ},
        B.IsInvProb lam →
          ∀ {Z c : ℝ},
            0 < Z →
              c = Z / lam G.src →
                0 < c ∧
                  c * lam G.src = Z ∧
                    B.edgeFlow lam c G.snk G.src = Z ∧
                      ∑ v, B.initFlow lam c v = Z ∧
                        (∀ (x : V), B.termFlow lam c x = Z * B.pb G.snk x) ∧
                          (∀ (x : V), G.Edge x G.snk → 0 < B.termFlow lam c x) ∧
                            (∀ (u : V), 0 ≤ B.outflowStar lam c u) ∧ ∀ v ∈ G.internal, B.fmDefect lam c v = 0
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.universal.doc:
**`theo:universality_graphs`*(3)*** (`proofs.tex:975–979`, proof `proofs.tex:993–1009`), in
one statement. At `c = Z/λ(s₀)`, the flow of item *(2)* with its wrap edge cut is a generative
flow on `G`: the wrap edge carried `Z`, the initial flow has total mass `Z`, the terminal flow is
`κ = Z π_←(s_f → ·)` and is positive on every terminating state, the star outflow is
non-negative, and the flow-matching constraint holds **exactly** at every internal state.

The sampler clause of item *(3)* is not here; it rests on `theo:sampling_theorem`, which the
paper cites and does not prove. See the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.universal.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G),
  G.PathConnected →
    B.PositiveOnEdges →
      (∀ (x y : V), B.BReach x y) ∧
        (∃ lam, B.IsInvProb lam) ∧
          (∀ (lam lam' : V → ℝ), B.IsInvProb lam → B.IsInvProb lam' → lam = lam') ∧
            ∀ (lam : V → ℝ), B.IsInvProb lam → (∀ (x : V), 0 < lam x) ∧ lam G.snk = lam G.src
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.universal.doc:
**`theo:universality_graphs`*(1)*** (`proofs.tex:967–969`, proof `proofs.tex:985`).

On a finite path-connected marked graph with a backward policy positive on every edge, the
backward chain of the loop closure is irreducible and admits a unique invariant probability `λ`;
moreover `λ > 0` everywhere and `λ(s₀) = λ(s_f)`.

The four conjuncts are the paper's four assertions, in its order. `Z > 0` and the counting measure
`μ` play no part in item *(1)*; see the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.two_add_s.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableEq V]
  {B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G} {u : V → ℝ}, B.IsHitExp u → 0 < 2 + B.sigmaBar u

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.termFlow_.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G),
  B.PositiveOnEdges →
    ∀ {lam : V → ℝ}, (∀ (x : V), 0 < lam x) → ∀ {c : ℝ}, 0 < c → ∀ {x : V}, G.Edge x G.snk → 0 < B.termFlow lam c x
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.termFlow_.doc:
**`κ` is positive on every terminating state** (`proofs.tex:1003`): `π_←` is positive on
every edge `x → s_f`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.termFlow..type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {inst_1 : DecidableEq V} [inst_2 : DecidableEq V]
  {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} (B B_1 : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G),
  B = B_1 →
    ∀ (lam lam_1 : V → ℝ),
      lam = lam_1 → ∀ (c c_1 : ℝ), c = c_1 → ∀ (x x_1 : V), x = x_1 → B.termFlow lam c x = B_1.termFlow lam_1 c_1 x_1

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.termFlow.type:
{V : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Fintype V] →
    [DecidableEq V] → {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} → GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G → (V → ℝ) → ℝ → V → ℝ

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.supp.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} (self : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G)
  ⦃s s' : V⦄, s ≠ G.src → self.pb s s' ≠ 0 → G.Edge s' s
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.supp.doc: `π_←(s → s') > 0` only if `s' → s` is an edge of `G`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_rever.doc: The `λ`-reversal is a Markov kernel: its rows sum to `1`, by stationarity of `λ`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_initF.doc:
**The initial flow has total mass `c λ(s₀)`** (`proofs.tex:998`), which is `Z` at
`c = Z/λ(s₀)`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_fwdSt.doc:
**`π_→^*` is a Markov kernel on `𝒮`** where the star outflow does not vanish: nothing leaves
an internal state towards `s₀`, so the row already summing to `1` over `𝒱 ∖ {s_f}` sums to `1`
over `𝒮`. Not a claim of the paper — a consistency check on calling `π_→^*` a policy.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_fwdSt.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) {lam : V → ℝ},
  B.IsInvProb lam →
    ∀ (c : ℝ) {u : V}, B.outflowStar lam c u ≠ 0 → ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase G.snk, B.fwdStar lam c u v = 1
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_fwdSt.doc: Where the star outflow does not vanish, `π_→^*(u → ·)` is a probability on `𝒱 ∖ {s_f}`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_edgeI.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) {lam : V → ℝ},
  B.IsInvProb lam →
    ∀ (eps : ℝ) (c : V → V → ℝ),
      ∑ v, GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow (B.perturbedFlow lam eps c) v = 1 - eps * ∑ v, GFNBounds.Graph.edgeInflow c v
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_edgeI.doc: The total mass of the perturbed state flow, `∑ μ_F = 1 − ε ∑_v ∂γ(v)`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_edgeF.doc:
**`e` is a circulation, outgoing half** (`proofs.tex:995`): `∑_v e(u → v) = c λ(u)`, by
stationarity of `λ`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_edgeF.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) (lam : V → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (v : V), ∑ u, B.edgeFlow lam c u v = c * lam v
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_edgeF.doc:
**`e` is a circulation, incoming half** (`proofs.tex:996`): `∑_u e(u → v) = c λ(v)`, because
`π̂_←(v → ·)` is a probability.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_densM.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) (l : V → ℝ), ∑ y, B.densMap l y = ∑ x, l x
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.sum_densM.doc: The density action preserves total mass: the rows of `π̂_←` sum to `1`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.stateRati.doc:
**The ratio is positive at every state flow of positive density.** The paper's `g > 0`
elsewhere is a statement on `ℝ_{>0}`, so this is what lets it be applied.

**`r ≡ 1` if and only if the state flow is `π̂_←`-invariant** — `ratio_eq_one_iff_balanced`
of `GFNBounds.Balance`, read here.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.stateRati.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) (mu : V → ℝ) (y : V), B.stateRatio mu y = (∑ x, mu x * B.phat x y) / mu y

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {inst_1 : DecidableEq V} [inst_2 : DecidableEq V]
  {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} (B B_1 : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G),
  B = B_1 → ∀ (mu mu_1 : V → ℝ), mu = mu_1 → ∀ (a a_1 : V), a = a_1 → B.stateRatio mu a = B_1.stateRatio mu_1 a_1

{V : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Fintype V] →
    [DecidableEq V] → {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} → GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G → (V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.stateRati.doc:
**`prop:frozen_unstable_full`, the ratio `r = d(μ π̂_←)/dμ`** (`proofs.tex:673`), in the
coordinates of `GFNBounds.Balance`: `μ = u λ` at `λ := μ` and `u := 1`, so that
`ratio π̂_← μ 1 = (μ π̂_←)/μ`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.src_row_u.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} (q : V → ℝ),
  ∑ s', q s' = 1 → (∀ (s' : V), q s' ≠ 0 → G.hatEdge s' G.src) → q = fun s' => if s' = G.snk then 1 else 0
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.src_row_u.doc:
**`def:loop_closure`, the source row.** A row summing to `1` and supported on the
in-neighbours of `s₀` in `Ĝ` is the point mass at `s_f`, the wrap edge being the only one.

The policy plays no part — this is a statement about `Ĝ` alone — and non-negativity, which the
paper's "probability distribution" carries, is not used either: the support condition kills every
entry off `s_f` and the total mass fixes the one that is left. Both are strengthenings in the safe
direction; the paper's statement is the case `q ≥ 0`.

  {B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G} {u : V → ℝ}, B.IsHitExp u → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.sigmaStar G u

`σ̄ := E_{x ∼ π̂_←(s_f→·)} E(σ ∣ X₀ = x)`, the expected backward-trajectory length of Morozov
et al. (`proofs.tex:838`). The target row is `π̂_←(s_f→·)`, so the average against it is `Q` read
at `s_f`.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.row_sum.doc: `π_←(s → ·)` is a probability distribution at every `s ≠ s₀`.

  [inst : Fintype V] →
    [DecidableEq V] → {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V} → GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G → (V → ℝ) → V → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.reversal.doc:
**`theo:universality_graphs`*(2)*, the `λ`-reversal `π̂_←^λ`** (`proofs.tex:974`):
`π_→(s → s') = λ(s') π̂_←(s' → s) / λ(s)`, the elementary finite-space form of the disintegration
of Lemma `lem:adjoint`. Well-defined wherever `λ > 0`, which item *(1)* supplies.

GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.residuals.doc:
**The residuals vanish** (`proofs.tex:981`, "all residuals `δF_init`, `δF_term` are zero").
Pointwise on `𝒮`, hence in every `L^p` at once, the state space being finite — the `p`-uniformity
of the paper's closing sentence is subsumed by a pointwise identity. `δf_init = D⁻` and
`δf_term = D⁺` is the sign convention of `theo:universality_L2_full` and of
`GFNBounds.Core.resInit` / `resTerm`.

The linear map whose kernel is the homogeneous Poisson system: `u ↦ u(s₀)` at `s₀` and
`u ↦ u − Qu` elsewhere. Its injectivity is the minimum principle, and in finite dimension
injectivity is surjectivity — the route `GFNBounds/Graph/Setting.lean`'s `exists_fixed` takes.

∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) (Q : V → V → ℝ),
  (∀ (s : V), ∑ s', Q s s' = 1) →
    (∀ (s s' : V), Q s s' ≠ 0 → G.hatEdge s' s) → (∀ ⦃s : V⦄, s ≠ G.src → Q s = B.pb s) → Q = B.phat
GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy.phat_uniq.doc:
**`def:loop_closure`: the extension is unique.** A backward policy `Q` on `Ĝ` — rows summing
to `1`, supported on the in-neighbours in `Ĝ` — that agrees with `π_←` at every state other than
`s₀` is `π̂_←`. This is the definition's "extends uniquely", in full: `phat` is not merely *an*
extension but the only one.

function action of the `λ`-reversal.
