GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp_self.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), inner ℝ L.oneLp L.oneLp = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp_psta.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), inner ℝ L.oneLp (L.pstarLp F) = inner ℝ L.oneLp F
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp_psta.doc:
**`P⋆` preserves the mean on `L²`.** This is `λ`-invariance, tested against a
square-integrable function.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), inner ℝ L.oneLp F = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * ↑↑F x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp.doc: **`Π`, read as an inner product.** `⟪1, F⟫ = ∫ F dλ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum_of.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {F G : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)} {f g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  ↑↑F =ᵐ[L.mu] f → ↑↑G =ᵐ[L.mu] g → inner ℝ F G = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x * g x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum_of.doc:
The same, read against any representatives: off the chain `λ` vanishes, so a.e. equality of
the integrands suffices term by term.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F G : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), inner ℝ F G = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * ↑↑F x * ↑↑G x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum.doc:
**The Bochner half of the `LpLayer` dictionary.** `⟪F,G⟫_{L²(μ)} = ∑' x, λ(x)F(x)G(x)`.

`L2.integrable_inner` makes the pointwise product integrable, `integral_countable` turns the
integral into a sum over the countable `St`, and `Stat.mu_singleton` evaluates the weight.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_densL2_lef.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (U V : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  inner ℝ ((L.densL2 hrow) U) V = inner ℝ U ((L.pstarL2 hrow) V)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_densL2_lef.doc:
**`⟪PU, V⟫ = ⟪U, P⋆V⟫` on `L²(μ)`** — `Stat.tsum_dens_mul_sq` read through the inner
product.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_succ_sub.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (n : ℕ),
  L.hitInt (n + 1) - L.hitInt n =
    1 - L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) - (1 + GFNBounds.Doubling.sbar S cap n) * L.lam GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_succ_sub.doc: **The one-step identity.** `a_{n+1} − a_n = 1 − λ(s₀) − (1 + σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾) λ(s_f)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_mono.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), Monotone L.hitInt

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {c : ℝ},
  c < 1 → (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / (↑j + 1)) → 0 < c → ∀ (n : ℕ), L.hitInt n ≤ ↑K / (1 - c)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_le.doc:
On the truncation the supersolution is bounded by `K/(1−c)`, which is what makes the
hitting integrals converge.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → ℕ → ℝ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_tailShift.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (m : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun k => L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k + m))) (L.tailMass m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_tailShift.doc: The tail mass is the tail of a summable series over the ladder.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_tailMass.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailInd cap m x) (L.tailMass m)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_one.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), HasSum L.lam 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_kern_flux.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.kern S cap x y) (L.lam y)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux_pt.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.ptFn y) x) (L.lam y)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux_pt.doc: Total flux into `y` is `λ(y)`: invariance tested against the point mass at `y`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (j : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.dirac j) x)
    (L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux.doc:
**Pointwise balance, from the integral form.** `λ_j` is the total one-step flux into `j`.

This is `Stat.inv` tested against `dirac j`; the right-hand side is `λ_j` by
`tsum_lam_mul_dirac`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_coTail.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * (1 - GFNBounds.Doubling.tailInd cap m x)) (1 - L.tailMass m)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.flux_nonneg.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (j : ℕ)
  (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.dirac j) x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.flux_nonneg.doc: Every one-step flux term is non-negative, so a single one may be kept and the rest discarded.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const_memL.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu →
    (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x = f x) →
      ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = f (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const_memL.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P⋆` half, at the paper's hypothesis.** A fixed point of the
function action in `L²(λ)` is constant on the chain.

The ladder is climbed by the decrement alone, exactly as in `FixedPoints.fixed_const`; what is
new is that `f` is only assumed square-integrable, and the fixed-point equation only `λ`-a.e.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f = f →
      ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = f (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P⋆` half.** A bounded fixed point of the function action is
constant on the chain.

The ladder is climbed by the decrement alone: at a state whose doubling edge has been truncated
away the fixed-point equation gives `f(m) = f(m−1)` outright, and where it survives, equality in
Jensen gives `f(2m) = f(m−1)` and the fixed-point equation then averages the two into
`f(m) = f(m−1)`. The target row is never used.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.finset_sum_le_ta.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {m b : ℕ},
  b ≤ K → ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m b, L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ≤ L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.finset_sum_le_ta.doc: A finite block of the ladder below the cap is part of the tail.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_unsolvabl.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∃ fi fe,
      (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ fi x) ∧
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ fe x) ∧
          MeasureTheory.MemLp fi 2 L.mu ∧
            MeasureTheory.MemLp fe 2 L.mu ∧
              ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * fi x = 1 ∧
                ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * fe x = 1 ∧
                  ¬∃ f,
                      MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu ∧
                        ∀ᵐ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St) ∂L.mu, f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none f x = fi x - fe x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_unsolvabl.doc:
**`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(2).** There are probability densities `f_init, f_term ∈ L²(λ)`
whose difference is not a flow-matching defect: no `f ∈ L²(λ)` has `(Id − P⋆)f = f_init − f_term`.

The pair is not explicit: it is built from a `ψ ∈ ker Π` outside the range of `Id − P⋆`, and that
`ψ` exists only because the range is proper (`defectRange_ne_kerPi`), which is an open-mapping
argument.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_tailRatio.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∀ (Q : ℝ) (m₁ : ℕ), ∃ m, m₁ ≤ m ∧ Q * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) < L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_tailRatio.doc:
**Step 1 of `theo:doubling_unbounded`(2).** Under (★) the ratio `L(m)/λ_m` is unbounded above
*every* cut: an exponentially decaying tail would force `Σ_{i<D} log(1/ε(2^i))` to grow like `2^D`,
which (★) forbids.

The start `m₁` is a parameter, which is the paper's "dropping finitely many cuts from the supremum
leaves it infinite" — proved rather than asserted.

⚠ weakened hypothesis: no relation between `m₁` and `d` is needed. The paper's supremum runs over
`m > d`; the decay argument never uses that, because the geometric bound starts at `m₁` and the
lower bound `λ_{2^D} ≥ λ_1 ∏ ε(2^i)` starts at `1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_mas.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∀ {p : ℝ},
      1 ≤ p →
        ∀ {t : ℝ},
          0 < t →
            ∃ m,
              S.d < m ∧
                (L.mass p fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤
                  t * L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_mas.doc:
**`eq:doubling_inf`.** For every `t > 0` some centred tail indicator has flow-matching defect
of mass at most `t` times its own mass: the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient over the mean-zero
functions of unit norm is `0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_def.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S → ∀ {t : ℝ}, 0 < t → ∃ F ∈ L.kerPi, F ≠ 0 ∧ ‖L.defect F‖ ^ 2 ≤ t * ‖F‖ ^ 2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_def.doc:
**`eq:doubling_inf` at `p = 2`, in `L²(λ)`.** For every `t > 0` some non-zero mean-zero class
has `‖(Id − P⋆)F‖² ≤ t‖F‖²`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_rayleigh_.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  0 < c₁ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
        ∃ m₂,
          S.d < m₂ ∧
            ∀ (m : ℕ),
              m₂ ≤ m →
                (c₁ * ↑m * L.mass 2 fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤
                  4 * c₂ * (D.p - 1) * L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_rayleigh_.doc:
**`cor:doubling_family`.** The cut `m₂` past which the rate holds exists, because
`L(m) → 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_diffusion.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K))
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S (some K)),
  ∃ R,
    (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow + L.piL2) * R = 1 ∧
      R * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow + L.piL2) = 1 ∧
        (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) * (R - L.piL2) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧
          (R - L.piL2) * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.piL2 * (R - L.piL2) = 0 ∧ (R - L.piL2) * L.piL2 = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_diffusion.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(2), instantiated.** On the truncation `Id − P⋆ + Π` is invertible and
the diffusion operator `S := (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` satisfies `eq:doubling_resolvent`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_centredRa.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (N : ℕ), ∃ x, ↑N / 2 ≤ |L.centredRamp N x|
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_centredRa.doc:
**`eq:doubling_ramp`, first line.** The centred ramp attains `N/2` in absolute value: the two
values `r_N(s₀) = 0` and `r_N(N) = N` are both attained, so one of `Π r_N` and `N − Π r_N` is at
least `N/2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_bhat.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K))
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S (some K)),
  ∃ Sop,
    (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) * Sop = 1 - L.piL2 ∧
      Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧
        L.piL2 * Sop = 0 ∧
          Sop * L.piL2 = 0 ∧ ∀ (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ ‖Sop‖ * ‖F - (L.pstarL2 hrow) F‖
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_bhat.doc:
**`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible` Step 4, and `cor:doubling_truncation` Step 1.**

There is a diffusion operator `S` on `L²(λ^K)` satisfying `eq:doubling_resolvent`, and its norm
`B̂_K` is a real number — which is `B̂_K < +∞`. The last clause is what Step 3 of
`cor:doubling_truncation` consumes: `‖F − ΠF‖ = ‖S(Id − P⋆)F‖ ≤ B̂_K‖(Id − P⋆)F‖`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain_inject.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)), Function.Injective ⇑L.evalChain
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain_inject.doc:
Evaluation on the chain is injective: `λ` charges every state of the chain and vanishes off
it, so a class vanishing there is the zero class.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {K : ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) →
      ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →ₗ[ℝ] { x // GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain (some K) x } → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain.doc:
**Evaluation at the states of the chain**, as a linear map into a finite product. It is linear
because a.e. equality is equality on the chain (`Stat.ae_iff_eq`), so the representative of a sum
*is* the sum of the representatives there.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_zero_of_mem_k.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  F ∈ L.kerPi → L.pstarLp F = F → F = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  (L.pstarL2 hrow) F = F → F = ↑↑F (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) • L.oneLp
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.doc:
A fixed point of `P⋆` in `L²(λ)` is a constant class — `lem:doubling_fixed_points`' `P⋆` half
(`Stat.fixed_const_memLp`), transported to `Lp` at an arbitrary cap.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  L.pstarLp F = F → F = ↑↑F (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) • L.oneLp
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.doc:
A fixed point of `P⋆` in `L²(λ)` is a constant class: `lem:doubling_fixed_points`, `P⋆` half,
transported to `Lp`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_two_psta.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu →
    MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) 2 L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f 2 L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_two_psta.doc:
**`P⋆` is a contraction of `L²(μ)`** — the `p = 2` case of `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s
first clause.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {p : ENNReal},
      1 ≤ p →
        ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
          MeasureTheory.MemLp f p L.mu →
            MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) p L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(1), first clause, in one statement.** `P⋆` is a contraction of
`L^p(μ)` for every `p ∈ [1,∞]`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {p : ENNReal},
  1 ≤ p →
    p ≠ ⊤ →
      ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
        MeasureTheory.MemLp f p L.mu →
          MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) p L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(1), first clause, at finite `p`.** `P⋆` is a contraction of
`L^p(μ)` for every `p ∈ [1,∞)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_dens_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {p : ENNReal},
      1 ≤ p →
        p ≠ ⊤ →
          ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
            MeasureTheory.MemLp u p L.mu → MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (L.dens u) p L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm u p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_dens_le.doc:
**`P` is a contraction of `L^p(μ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the `eLpNorm` form of
`Stat.mass_dens_le`. In particular `P` is a bounded operator of `L²(λ)`, which is what
`lem:doubling_operator`(1) needs of it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNormEssSup_ps.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
      MeasureTheory.eLpNormEssSup (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNormEssSup f L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNormEssSup_ps.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(1), first clause, at `p = ∞`.** `P⋆` is a contraction of
`L^∞(μ)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_smul.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (c : ℝ)
  (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ), L.dens (c • u) = c • L.dens u

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_sink.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
  L.dens u GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_sink.doc: `P` at the sink: the wrap is the only incoming edge, so `(Pu)(s_f) = u(s₀)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_lad.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  (k : ℕ),
  L.dens u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k) =
    L.w1 k * u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k + 1)) + L.w2 k * u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k / 2)) +
      L.w3 k * u GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_lad.doc: `P` at a ladder state, as a three-atom average.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_gap_zero.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (Summable fun x => |u x| ^ 2 * L.lam x) →
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) →
          ∀ {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St}, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap y → L.dens (fun z => u z ^ 2) y = L.dens u y ^ 2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_gap_zero.doc:
**The Jensen gap of `P` vanishes on the chain at a fixed point in `L²(λ)`.**

The gap is non-negative pointwise and its `λ`-integral is zero, `P` preserving the `λ`-integral
and `Pu = u` on the chain; a convergent sum of non-negative terms vanishing forces each term to.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_of_co.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)) →
    ∀ {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St}, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap y → L.dens u y = u y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_of_co.doc: The converse inclusion: `P` fixes every function constant on the chain.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (Summable fun x => |u x| ^ 2 * L.lam x) →
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) →
          ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_const.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P` half.** A fixed point of the density action in `L²(λ)` is
constant on the chain.

Equality in Jensen for the reversed law makes `u` constant on the atoms of positive weight, and
the climbing atom `j ↦ j+1` has positive weight at every `j` with `j+1` on the chain: the ladder
is climbed from the source, exactly as `FixedPoints.fixed_const` descends it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St}, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap y → L.dens (fun x => 1) y = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_const.doc: **`P` fixes the constants** on the chain: the reversed law is a probability.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_congr_onCha.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {u v : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = v x) →
    ∀ (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.dens u y = L.dens v y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_congr_onCha.doc:
**`P` descends to `λ`-classes**, and unlike `P⋆` it needs no hypothesis to do so: each of its
three weights carries the factor `λ` of the state it reads (`Stat.w1`, `Stat.w2`, `Stat.w3`), so a
state off the chain is read with weight zero.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_add.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (u v : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ), L.dens (u + v) = L.dens u + L.dens v

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp_smul.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (c : ℝ) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.densLp hrow (c • F) = c • L.densLp hrow F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp_add.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F G : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.densLp hrow (F + G) = L.densLp hrow F + L.densLp hrow G

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp.congr_sim.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F F_1 : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  F = F_1 → L.densLp hrow F = L.densLp hrow F_1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) →
      GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp.doc: `P` acting on `L²(μ)`, as a map of the space into itself.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2_mul_piL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), L.densL2 hrow * L.piL2 = L.piL2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2_mul_piL2.doc: `P Π = Π`, read off the adjoint of `Π P⋆ = Π`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2_apply.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), (L.densL2 hrow) F = L.densLp hrow F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) →
      GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2.doc:
**`P` as a bounded linear operator on `L²(μ)`**, of norm at most `1` — the mirror of
`Stat.pstarL2`, and the operator the paper's `β̂ₙ` is measured on.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → (GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens.doc:
**The density action** `Pu := d((uλ)T)/dλ`, in closed form: the transported measure `(uλ)T`
of `Balance.mact`, divided by `λ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect_sub_mean.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.defect (F - inner ℝ L.oneLp F • L.oneLp) = L.defect F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect_oneLp.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none), L.defect L.oneLp = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect_apply.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.defect F = F - L.pstarLp F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_ne_k.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S → L.defectRange ≠ L.kerPi
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_ne_k.doc:
**`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(1), the proper half.** `(Id − P⋆)L²(λ)` is not all of `ker Π`:
were it, the open mapping theorem would bound `Id − P⋆` below on `ker Π`, against
`eq:doubling_inf`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_le_k.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none), L.defectRange ≤ L.kerPi
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_le_k.doc: The defect of any class has zero mean: `Π(Id − P⋆) = 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) → Submodule ℝ ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect.doc: **`Id − P⋆`** as a bounded operator of `L²(λ)`, on the loop closure.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.decayK.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  (∀ (j : ℕ), S.eps j = D.eps j) →
    ∀ {ℓ : ℕ},
      S.d < ℓ →
        1 ≤ ℓ →
          4 * ℓ ≤ K →
            ∀ {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ},
              0 < Z₁ →
                0 < Z₂ →
                  (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) →
                    (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) →
                      ∃ Cm Cp,
                        0 < Cm ∧
                          Cp ≤ Z₂ / Z₁ * 2 ^ D.p * ((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹ ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * ↑ℓ + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) ^ 2 * Cm ∧
                            ∀ (m : ℕ),
                              ℓ ≤ m →
                                m ≤ K / 2 →
                                  Cm * ↑m ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) ∧
                                    L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) ≤ Cp * ↑m ^ (-D.p)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.decayK.doc:
**`eq:doubling_decayK`.** Two constants sandwiching `λ^K` on `[ℓ, K/2]`, with a ratio
`C⁺/C⁻ ≤ (Z₂/Z₁) 2^{p_*} Q²` **free of `K`** — which is the `c₉` of the paper, since `Q` depends
on `c` and `ℓ` alone and `Z₁, Z₂` on `c` and `d` alone.

Stated with `Z₁ ≤ E(Z_ℓ) ≤ Z₂` — `eq:doubling_product` at the level `ℓ` — as hypotheses, which
`Decay.descOne_two_sided` (`Product.lean`) discharges for every `ℓ ≥ m₀`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.cutBalanceSeq_tr.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.CutBalanceSeq S (fun j => L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)) ↑(K / 2)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.cutBalanceSeq_tr.doc: The truncation's masses satisfy `eq:doubling_cut` up to `K/2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ctorIdx.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → ℕ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_sub_pstarL.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ} (hf : MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu),

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.block_ratio.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  (∀ (j : ℕ), S.eps j = D.eps j) →
    ∀ {ℓ : ℕ},
      S.d < ℓ →
        1 ≤ ℓ →
          4 * ℓ ≤ K →
            ∀ {j j' : ℕ},
              ℓ ≤ j →
                j < 2 * ℓ →
                  ℓ ≤ j' →
                    j' < 2 * ℓ →
                      L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j') ≤
                        ((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹ ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * ↑ℓ + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.block_ratio.doc:
**The block ratio, free of `K`.** On `[ℓ, 2ℓ)` any two masses differ by at most
`Q = ρ^ℓ + (η^ℓ)^{-1}`, with `ρ = (1−ε_max)^{-1}` and `η = c/(2ℓ+1)` — constants of `c` and `ℓ`
alone. This is what makes `c₉` independent of the cap.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_iff_eq.doc:
**The bridge.** `f =ᵐ[μ] g` iff `f` and `g` agree at every state of the chain.

`λ` charges every on-chain state (`Stat.pos`) and vanishes off it (`Stat.vanish`), so the only
`μ`-null set meeting the chain is empty. On the loop closure `OnChain` is vacuous and a.e.
equality is equality.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.abs_rpow_dens_le.doc: **Jensen for `P`**, at every state of the chain: `|Pu|^p ≤ P(|u|^p)` for `p ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.doc:
An invariant probability of the chain in play — `λ` of `def:doubling_setting`.

Positivity is **on chain**, and `λ` vanishes off it; see `OnChain`. On the loop closure
`OnChain` is vacuous and this is the paper's "positive at every state".

Invariance is carried in the **integral** form `∫ P⋆f dλ = ∫ f dλ` against bounded `f`, which is
the form every downstream use consumes (`prop:doubling_cut` tests it against `1_A`) and which
needs no summability side condition at the point of use. The pointwise form `λT = λ` is
equivalent on a countable space; that bridge is `inv_of_pointwise` in `PointwiseInv.lean`.

Positivity is a field rather than a theorem because every statement of the appendix downstream of
`lem:doubling_irreducible` quantifies over "an invariant probability" — the existence question is
`prop:doubling_phase`, which is separate and, for the family, hard.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting.doc:
The standing hypotheses of `def:doubling_setting`, minus the family.

The target row `P̂_B(s_f → ·)` is finitely supported **by hypothesis** (`row_supp`), so every
expression involving it is a `Finset.sum` and never a `tsum`; that kills a class of summability
side conditions before it appears.

`epsMax` is a field rather than `⨆ j, eps j` because the appendix only ever uses
`ε(j) ≤ ε_max < 1`, and an `iSup` in `ℝ` would drag `BddAbove` bookkeeping through every proof.
`lem:doubling_range` supplies `ε_max = c·2^(-s)` for the family.

GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain.doc:
The target row reaches only states of the chain.

Vacuous on the loop closure; on the truncation at `K` it is `d ≤ K`, which
`cor:doubling_truncation` assumes anyway (it takes `K ≥ 2d`). It is what makes `P⋆` descend to
`λ`-classes: the sink reads `f` at `1, …, d`, and off the chain a.e. equality says nothing.

GFNBounds.Doubling.PreStat.doc:
Every field of `Stat` except positivity. `PreStat.toStat` recovers positivity from
irreducibility, which is the second sentence of `lem:doubling_irreducible`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain.doc:
The states of the chain in play.

On the loop closure (`cap = none`) every state of `St`. On the truncation at `K` the `K + 2`
states `{s₀, 1, …, K, s_f}` of `lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`: the ladder states above `K`
carry no incoming edge from within the chain — a decrement from `j ≤ K` lands at most at `K − 1`
and a doubling that survives lands at `2j ≤ K` — so they are unreachable, and the invariant
probability vanishes on them.

This is why `Stat` below carries positivity only **on chain** and vanishing off it, rather than
global positivity: `St` is one type serving two chains, and the truncation genuinely does not live
on all of it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.LadderStep.le_succ_ad.type: ∀ {cap : Option ℕ} {a b : ℕ}, GFNBounds.Doubling.LadderStep cap a b → a ≤ b + 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.LadderStep.le_succ_ad.doc:
**The first half of `lem:doubling_excursion`.** `X_{n+1} ≥ X_n − 1`, in the form `X_n ≤
X_{n+1} + 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.LadderStep.doc:
One admissible step of the backward chain along the ladder: double, when that edge survives
the cap, or decrement. `s₀` is the index `0`, and `0 - 1 = 0` in `ℕ` makes it absorbing for the
decrement, which is harmless: the bound is asserted at an index where the path is already at `0`.

**Third bullet of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** A state of `I_i(ℓ)` below `⌈5a/2⌉` sees all of `J`
in its window.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Jlow_subset.type: ∀ (a : ℕ), GFNBounds.Doubling.Jlow a ⊆ Finset.Ico a (2 * a)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Jlow.doc: `J = {⌈5a/4⌉, …, 2a−1}`, the range carrying the reference law `ϖ_i`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Jhigh_subset_window.type: ∀ {a y : ℕ}, (5 * a + 1) / 2 ≤ y → y < 4 * a → GFNBounds.Doubling.Jhigh a ⊆ GFNBounds.Doubling.window y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Jhigh_subset_window.doc:
**Fourth bullet of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** A state of `I_i(ℓ)` at or above `⌈5a/2⌉` sees all
of `J'` in its window.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Jhigh_subset.type: ∀ (a : ℕ), GFNBounds.Doubling.Jhigh a ⊆ Finset.Ico (2 * a) (4 * a)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Jhigh.doc: `J' = {2a, …, ⌈5a/2⌉−1}`, the range the second case of `lem:doubling_doeblin` steps into.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Icc_succ_eq_Ioc.type: ∀ (a b : ℕ), Finset.Icc (a + 1) b = Finset.Ioc a b

GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble.doc:
Whether the doubling edge out of the ladder state `j` is present.

`cap = none` is the loop closure, where every doubling edge is present. `cap = some K` is the
truncation at `K` of `def:doubling_setting`: the edge `j → 2j` is deleted when `2j > K`, the
decrement out of such a state then carrying probability `1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.wrap.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ},
  GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.row.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ},
  ∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d,
    0 < S.row k → GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.recOn.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ}
  {motive : (a a_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St) → GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap a a_1 → Prop}
  {a a_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St} (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap a a_1),
  motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink ⋯ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ⋯) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (h : GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap (j + 1)),
          motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (2 * (j + 1))) ⋯) →
        (∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d) (hpos : 0 < S.row k),
            motive GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k) ⋯) →
          motive a a_1 t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.rec.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ}
  {motive : (a a_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St) → GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap a a_1 → Prop},
  motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink ⋯ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ⋯) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (h : GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap (j + 1)),
          motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (2 * (j + 1))) ⋯) →
        (∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d) (hpos : 0 < S.row k),
            motive GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k) ⋯) →
          ∀ {a a_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St} (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap a a_1), motive a a_1 t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.dec.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (j : ℕ),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.dbl.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (j : ℕ),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap (j + 1) →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (2 * (j + 1)))

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.casesOn.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ}
  {motive : (a a_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St) → GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap a a_1 → Prop}
  {a a_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St} (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge S cap a a_1),
  motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink ⋯ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ⋯) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (h : GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap (j + 1)),
          motive (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + 1)) (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (2 * (j + 1))) ⋯) →
        (∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d) (hpos : 0 < S.row k),
            motive GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k) ⋯) →
          motive a a_1 t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.type: GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting → Option ℕ → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → Prop
GFNBounds.Doubling.Edge.doc:
The positive transitions of `eq:doubling_policy`: the wrap `s₀ → s_f`, the decrement
`j+1 → j`, the doubling `j+1 → 2(j+1)` where that edge survives the cap, and the target row
`s_f → k` at every `k` the row charges.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.wm_pos.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m j : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → 1 ≤ j → 0 < D.wm m j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.wm_nonneg.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m j : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → 1 ≤ j → 0 ≤ D.wm m j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.wm_ge_shift.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {y j : ℕ}, 1 ≤ y → 1 ≤ j → D.c * ↑y ^ D.p * (↑j + 1) ^ (-D.p - 1) ≤ D.wm y j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.wm_ge_shift.doc: `w_y(j) ≥ c y^{p}(j+1)^{−p−1}`, the paper's first inequality of Step 1.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.window_nonempty.doc: The window is non-empty from `m = 2` on: `⌈m/2⌉ < m`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.windowSum_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ},
  1 ≤ m → ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, ↑j ^ (-D.p) / (↑j + 1) ≤ ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, ↑j ^ (-D.p - 1)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.windowSum_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ},
  1 ≤ m →
    ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, ↑j ^ (-D.p - 1) - ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, ↑j ^ (-D.p - 1 - 1) ≤
      ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, ↑j ^ (-D.p) / (↑j + 1)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.weight_bound.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  D.ell3 ≤ ℓ →
    ∀ {B : ℝ} {g : ℕ → ℝ}, (∀ (j : ℕ), |g j| ≤ B) → ∀ (y : ℕ), |D.descW ℓ g y - D.descP ℓ g y| ≤ B * D.c3 / ↑ℓ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.weight_bound.doc:
**`lem:doubling_weight`**, with both constants explicit: at every level `ℓ ≥ ℓ₃`, every
function `g` bounded by `B` and every state `y`,

  `|descW ℓ g y − descP ℓ g y| ≤ B c₃/ℓ`,   `c₃ = 32c₅cτ`, `ℓ₃ = max(1, ⌈16cτ⌉, ⌈96cτ/γ²⌉)`.

This is `eq:doubling_weight` in the form `theo:doubling_sharp` consumes.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.vartheta.doc:
`ϑ := α/(1+α)`, the rate exponent of `eq:doubling_rate`. Explicit, and — as the paper says —
not effective.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi_sum.type: ∀ {a : ℕ}, 20 ≤ a → ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico a (2 * a), GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi a z = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi_of_not_me.type: ∀ {a j : ℕ}, j ∉ GFNBounds.Doubling.Jlow a → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi a j = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi_nonneg.type: ∀ {a : ℕ}, 20 ≤ a → ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi a j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {a : ℕ},
  20 ≤ a → ∀ (j : ℕ), D.c / 4 * Real.log (8 / 5) * GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi a j ≤ D.c / (2 * (↑j + 1))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi_le.doc: `ϖ_i(j) ≤ 2/(ln(8/5)(j+1))` on `J`: the normalising sum is at least `½ ln(8/5)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi.doc: `ϖ_i`, the probability on the integers of `[⌈5a/4⌉,2a)` proportional to `j ↦ 1/(j+1)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_sub_descP_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₂ c₃ : ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    d < 2 * L →
      0 ≤ c₃ →
        0 ≤ c₂ →
          (∀ (ℓ y : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ) →
            ∀ {ℓ : ℕ}, L ≤ ℓ → ∀ (y : ℕ), |D.uu lam y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_sub_descP_le.doc:
**The weight step.** The profile differs from its own descent average by at most `c₂c₃/ℓ`.
Below `2ℓ` the two are equal, and above it this is `eq:doubling_pathid` (proved) together with
`lem:doubling_weight` (the hypothesis `hweight`).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_diff_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    d < 2 * L →
      20 ≤ L →
        32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
          0 < c₁ →
            0 ≤ c₃ →
              (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) →
                (∀ (ℓ y : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ) →
                  ∀ {ℓ : ℕ},
                    L ≤ ℓ →
                      ∀ (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ},
                        2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m →
                          2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m' → |D.uu lam m - D.uu lam m'| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_diff_le.doc:
**The two bullets of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`, merged.** At every level `ℓ ≥ L` and
every `i`, two indices above `2^iℓ` have profiles differing by at most
`c₂(1−ω)^i + 2c₂c₃/ℓ` — the paper's `3c₂c₃/ℓ`, improved to `2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_bounded_of_c.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) →
      D.m0 d ≤ ℓ → ∃ c₁ c₂, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_bounded_of_c.doc:
**`theo:doubling_decay`(2) in the `u` variable, unconditional.** The same preamble as
`Product.decay_two_sided_of_cutBal`, stopped one step earlier: it is the rescaled profile, not the
sequence, that `Sharp.lean` takes bounds on.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_bounded_expl.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    D.m0 d ≤ ℓ →
      ∀ {a b : ℝ},
        0 ≤ a →
          (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) →
            ∀ (j : ℕ),
              1 ≤ j →
                a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)) ≤ D.uu lam j ∧
                  D.uu lam j ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_bounded_expl.doc:
**`eq:doubling_decay` in the `u` variable, with the constants written out.** If the rescaled
profile lies in `[a, b]` on the initial block `1 ≤ j < 2ℓ`, `ℓ ≥ m₀`, then on the whole ladder it
lies in `[a e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ}, b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}]`, `c₄ = 16cτ`. This is the dependence clause of
`theo:doubling_decay`(2) made precise: the constants are functions of `c`, `d` (through `m₀`) and
`λ_1, …, λ_{2ℓ−1}` (through `a`, `b`) alone.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_bounded.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) →
      d < 2 * ℓ →
        1 ≤ ℓ →
          ∀ {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ},
            0 < Z₁ →
              Z₁ ≤ 1 →
                1 ≤ Z₂ →
                  (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) →
                    (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) →
                      ∃ c₁ c₂, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu_bounded.doc:
**`eq:doubling_decay`, in the `u` variable.** The rescaled profile is bounded above and below
by positive constants, on the whole ladder.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uu.doc: The rescaled profile `u_m := λ_m m^p` of `def:doubling_decay_notation`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uavg_of_cutBal.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞},
  D.CutBal d lam M₁ →
    ∀ {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → d < m → ↑m ≤ M₁ → D.uu lam m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.wm m j * D.uu lam j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uavg_of_avg.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {m : ℕ},
  1 ≤ m →
    lam m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.qm m j * lam j →
      D.uu lam m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.wm m j * D.uu lam j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.uavg_of_avg.doc: **`eq:doubling_uavg`, first line.** The same average, on the rescaled profile.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.two_step.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
    L ≤ z →
      z < 2 * L →
        ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z,
            D.pk z j *
              (GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L j *
                ∑ k ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window j, D.pk j k * GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L k) ≤
          1 - D.gam ^ 2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.two_step.doc:
**The two-step estimate.** `P(Y₂ ∈ I | Y₀ = z) ≤ 1 − γ²` for every `z ∈ I = [L, 2L)`.
This is the display the paper reaches by conditioning first on `Y₀,…,Y₁` and then on `Y₀`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.two_gam_eq.doc: **`2γ = c(τ−√τ)/p_*`**, the identity that turns the paper's window bound into `2γ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.thr_of_two_leve.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ y : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.thr_of_two_leve.doc: Every state `≥ 2ℓ` clears the threshold `32cτ`, at a level `ℓ` with `32cτ ≤ 2ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.thr_of_level.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ y : ℕ}, D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑y

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.thr_of_block.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ i : ℕ}, D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ → 1 ≤ i → 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑(2 ^ i * ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.thr_of_block.doc: The threshold holds on `I_i(ℓ)` for `i ≥ 1` and `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂`, since `2^i ℓ ≥ 2ℓ ≥ 32cτ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.thirty_two_lt.doc: The threshold used throughout: `32cτ ≤ y` forces `y > 32`, since `cτ > 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tail_sh.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun j => lam j * ↑j ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds C) →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun m => (D.p - 1) * ↑m ^ (D.p - 1) * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m) Filter.atTop (nhds C)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tail_sh.doc:
**`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, first line, as a limit.** If the rescaled profile `λ_j j^{p_*}`
converges to `C`, then `(p_*−1) m^{p_*−1} L(m) → C`, i.e. `L(m) = C m^{1−p_*}(1+o(1))/(p_*−1)`.
This is `tail_sharp` read at every `t > 0`; `theo:doubling_sharp` supplies the hypothesis.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tail_ra.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    0 < C →
      (∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → 0 < lam m) →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun j => lam j * ↑j ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds C) →
          Filter.Tendsto (fun m => (D.p - 1) * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m / (↑m * lam m)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tail_ra.doc:
**`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, second line.** If `λ_j j^{p_*} → C > 0` then
`(p_*−1) L(m)/(m λ_m) → 1`, i.e. `L(m)/λ_m = m(1+o(1))/(p_*−1)`: the first line divided by the
profile.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tail_ra.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    0 < c₁ →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
          Filter.Tendsto (fun m => GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m / lam m) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tail_ra.doc:
**`cor:doubling_tail`, "in particular `L(m)/λ_m → +∞`"**, for the sequence: the ratio
dominates `c₁ m/(c₂(p−1))` (`tail_ratio_ge`).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tailSeq.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    0 < c₁ →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
          Filter.Tendsto (GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_tailSeq.doc:
**`cor:doubling_tail`, "in particular `L(m) → 0`"**, for the sequence: squeezed between `0`
and `c₂(m^{−p} + m^{1−p}/(p−1)) → 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_of_cutB.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
      D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun m => lam m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * lam j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_of_cutB.doc:
**`eq:doubling_constant`, for the sequence itself.** Every real solution of the cut balance
at every `m > d` has `λ_m m^{p_*} → Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j λ_j`. Positivity is not needed (see SCOPE):
the solution is `extend d λ`, and `tendsto_extend` applies.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_ind.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ (j : ℕ),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun m => D.extend d (GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ind j) m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds (D.nu d j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_ind.doc: The rescaled profile of the solution with indicator data `e_j` converges to `ν_j`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_extend.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ (b : ℕ → ℝ),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun m => D.extend d b m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * b j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_extend.doc:
**Step 2, `eq:doubling_constant` on the whole space of data:** for every boundary data `b`,
`(extend d b)_m m^{p_*} → Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j b_j`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_climit_.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ (b : ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 < b j) →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun m => D.extend d b m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds (D.climit d b)) ∧ 0 < D.climit d b
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tendsto_climit_.doc:
**`theo:doubling_sharp` at the solution with positive data `b`:** the rescaled profile
converges to `C(b)`, and `C(b) > 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_sharp.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C t : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    ∀ {m₀ m : ℕ},
      m₀ ≤ m →
        1 ≤ m →
          (∀ (j : ℕ), m₀ ≤ j → |lam j * ↑j ^ D.p - C| ≤ t) →
            |(D.p - 1) * ↑m ^ (D.p - 1) * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m - C| ≤
              t * (1 + (D.p - 1) / ↑m) + |C| * ((D.p - 1) / ↑m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_sharp.doc:
**`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, first line, in explicit form.** If the rescaled profile is within
`t` of `C` past `m₀`, then `(p_*−1) m^{p_*−1} L(m)` is within `t(1 + (p_*−1)/m) + |C|(p_*−1)/m`
of `C` at every `m ≥ m₀`.

This is the corollary's content with the limit unwound: the paper's `t → 0` argument is the
statement read at every `t`. `tendsto_tail_sharp` below performs that conversion, and
`theo:doubling_sharp` (`Decay.sharp_of_cutBal`, `SharpFull.lean`) supplies the limit it needs.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_ratio_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    0 < c₁ →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
          ∀ {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → c₁ * (D.p - 1) * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m ≤ c₂ * D.p * ↑m * lam m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_ratio_le.doc:
**`eq:doubling_tailratio`, second pair, upper half.** `c₁(p−1) L(m) ≤ c₂ p m λ_m`, the
denominator-free form of `L(m)/λ_m ≤ c₂ p m/(c₁(p−1))`: the tail bound `tail_bounds` divided by
`λ_m ≥ c₁ m^{−p}`, with `(p−1) + m ≤ p m` for `m ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_ratio_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    0 < c₁ →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
          ∀ {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → c₁ * ↑m * lam m ≤ c₂ * (D.p - 1) * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_ratio_ge.doc:
**`eq:doubling_tailratio`, second pair, lower half.** `c₁ m λ_m ≤ c₂(p−1) L(m)`, the
denominator-free form of `L(m)/λ_m ≥ c₁ m/(c₂(p−1))`. This is what drives `L(m)/λ_m → +∞` and,
through `lem:doubling_percut`, the `√m` rate of `cor:doubling_family`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_bounds.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  Summable lam →
    0 < c₁ →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
          ∀ {m : ℕ},
            1 ≤ m →
              c₁ * (↑m ^ (1 - D.p) / (D.p - 1)) ≤ GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m ∧
                GFNBounds.Doubling.tailSeq lam m ≤ c₂ * (↑m ^ (-D.p) + ↑m ^ (1 - D.p) / (D.p - 1))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.tail_bounds.doc:
**`eq:doubling_tailratio`, both pairs.** With `c₁ j^{−p} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p}` on `j ≥ 1`,
the tail and the ratio of the tail to the mass at the cut are pinned to a power and to `m`.

The summability of `λ` is a hypothesis, as it must be: `eq:doubling_decay` alone gives it
(comparison with `j^{−p}`, `p > 1`), but the comparison is done here on the sums, not on the
summability.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_zero.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (L z : ℕ), D.surv L 0 z = GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L z

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_two_pow_le.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → ∀ (m z : ℕ), D.surv L (2 * m) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_two_pow_le.doc: `P(ς > 2m | Y₀ = z) ≤ (1−γ²)^m` at every state, the indicator dropped.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_two_pow.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → ∀ (r z : ℕ), D.surv L (2 * r) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r * GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_two_pow.doc:
**`eq:doubling_sojourn`, first line.** `P(ς > 2r | Y₀ = y) ≤ (1 − γ²)^r`, and — the sharper
form the induction needs — the bound is carried by the block indicator.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_succ.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (L r z : ℕ),
  D.surv L (r + 1) z = GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L z * ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z, D.pk z j * D.surv L r j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_partial_ze.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
    ∀ (z : ℕ) {zeta : ℝ},
      1 ≤ zeta →
        ∀ (R : ℕ),
          ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * R), zeta ^ n * D.surv L n z ≤
            (1 + zeta) * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range R, (zeta ^ 2 * (1 - D.gam ^ 2)) ^ r
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_partial_ze.doc: The `ζ`-weighted tail sum, paired two by two.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_partial_su.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
    ∀ (z R : ℕ), ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * R), D.surv L n z ≤ 2 * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range R, (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_partial_su.doc: Consecutive terms of the tail sum, paired: this is the paper's `ς̃ = ⌈ς/2⌉`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_of_out.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ}, ¬(L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) → ∀ (r : ℕ), D.surv L r z = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_le_pow.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → L ≤ z → z < 2 * L → ∀ (r : ℕ), D.surv L (2 * r) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_le_pow.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, first line, as stated in the paper.**

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_eq_zero_of.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} (r z : ℕ), z < L + r → D.surv L r z = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_eq_zero_of.doc:
The descent falls by at least one at each step, so it cannot stay in a block of width `L`
for `L` steps: `surv L r z = 0` as soon as `z < L + r`. This is what makes the tail sums of
`E(ς)` and `E(ζ^ς)` finite.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv_antitone.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → ∀ (r z : ℕ), D.surv L (r + 1) z ≤ D.surv L r z

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.surv.doc:
**`P(ς > r | Y₀ = z)`**, where `ς` is the exit time from `I = [L, 2L)`, as the recursion in
the number of steps that characterises it: `{ς > r} = {Y₀, …, Y_r ∈ I}`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_wm.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (m : ℕ), ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.wm m j = D.R0 m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_wm.doc:
**`eq:doubling_uavg`, second line.** The total weight of the window is `R_0(m)`, by definition
of `R_0` — recorded so that the descent recursion may cite it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_pk.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {z : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑z → ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z, D.pk z j = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_pk.doc: The transition law is a probability on `W(z)`: `Σ_{j ∈ W(z)} w_z(j)/R₀(z) = 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_nu_pos.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ}, 1 ≤ d → 0 < ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_nu_pos.doc:
**Step 3, second clause: `Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j > 0`.** At the data `λ_1 = … = λ_d = 1` the sum is
`C(1)`, which `theo:doubling_sharp` puts above the `c₁ > 0` of `theo:doubling_decay`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_kern.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ}, 2 ≤ m → ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.kern m j = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sum_kern.doc: The one-step law is a probability on the window.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojourn_block.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ i : ℕ},
  D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ →
    1 ≤ i →
      ∀ {y : ℕ},
        y ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.block i ℓ →
          (∀ (r : ℕ), D.surv (2 ^ i * ℓ) (2 * r) y ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r) ∧
            D.sojMean (2 ^ i * ℓ) y ≤ 2 / D.gam ^ 2 ∧
              ∀ (zeta : ℝ), 1 ≤ zeta → zeta ≤ 1 + D.gam ^ 2 / 6 → D.sojGF (2 ^ i * ℓ) zeta y ≤ 1 + D.c5 * (zeta - 1)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojourn_block.doc:
**`eq:doubling_sojourn`.** All three bounds, on the paper's own block `I_i(ℓ)` at `i ≥ 1`
and `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂`, for the exit time `ς` from that block.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean_of_out.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ}, ¬(L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) → D.sojMean L z = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean_of_in.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ},
  L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L → D.sojMean L z = 1 + ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z, D.pk z j * D.sojMean L j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean_nonneg.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → ∀ (z : ℕ), 0 ≤ D.sojMean L z

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean_le.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → z < 2 * L → D.sojMean L z ≤ 2 / D.gam ^ 2

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean_eq_sum.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} (z N : ℕ), z < L + N → D.sojMean L z = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, D.surv L n z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean_eq_sum.doc:
**The tail formula.** `E(ς) = Σ_{n<N} P(ς > n)` for every `N` past the block width — proved
from the two recursions, not assumed.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojMean.doc:
**`E(ς | Y₀ = z)`**, the expected sojourn in `I = [L,2L)`, as the recursion that characterises
it: leave at once outside the block, else one step plus the expectation after it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF_of_out.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} {zeta : ℝ} {z : ℕ}, ¬(L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) → D.sojGF L zeta z = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF_of_in.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} {zeta : ℝ} {z : ℕ},
  L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L → D.sojGF L zeta z = zeta * ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z, D.pk z j * D.sojGF L zeta j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
    z < 2 * L → ∀ {zeta : ℝ}, 1 ≤ zeta → zeta ≤ 1 + D.gam ^ 2 / 6 → D.sojGF L zeta z ≤ 1 + D.c5 * (zeta - 1)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF_le.doc:
**`eq:doubling_sojourn`, third line.** `E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = y) ≤ 1 + c₅(ζ−1)` for
`1 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 + γ²/6`, with `c₅ = 6/γ²`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF_eq_sum.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
    ∀ (zeta : ℝ) (z N : ℕ),
      z < L + N → D.sojGF L zeta z = 1 + (zeta - 1) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, zeta ^ n * D.surv L n z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF_eq_sum.doc: **The paper's expansion `ζ^ς = 1 + (ζ−1) Σ_{n<ς} ζⁿ`, in expectation.**

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sojGF.doc: **`E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = z)`**, as the recursion that characterises it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sixteen_lt_leve.doc: The level clears `16`: `2ℓ ≥ 32cτ > 32`, because `cτ = p_* + c > 1` (`one_lt_ctau`).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_rate_expl.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ C : ℝ},
  20 ≤ L →
    0 < c₁ →
      0 ≤ c₃ →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) →
          c₁ ≤ C →
            C ≤ c₂ →
              (∀ (ℓ i m : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ)) →
                ∀ (m : ℕ),
                  1 ≤ m →
                    |D.uu lam m - C| ≤
                      (c₂ * (4 ^ D.alph + 2 * c₃) + c₂ * ↑(max 1 ⌈↑L ^ (1 / D.vartheta)⌉₊) ^ D.vartheta) *
                        ↑m ^ (-D.vartheta)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_rate_expl.doc:
**`eq:doubling_rate`, with the constant written out.** With `ϑ = α/(1+α)`,
`α = log₂(1/(1−ω))` and `m₃ = max(1, ⌈L^{1/ϑ}⌉)`,
`|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ (c₂(4^α + 2c₃) + c₂ m₃^ϑ) m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_rate.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ C : ℝ},
  20 ≤ L →
    0 < c₁ →
      0 ≤ c₃ →
        (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) →
          c₁ ≤ C →
            C ≤ c₂ →
              (∀ (ℓ i m : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ)) →
                ∃ c₆, 0 < c₆ ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₆ * ↑m ^ (-D.vartheta)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_rate.doc:
**`eq:doubling_rate`.** There is `c₆ > 0` with `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ c₆ m^{−ϑ}` at every
`m ≥ 1`: the existential reading of `sharp_rate_explicit`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_of_cutBal.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) →
      ∃ C c₁ c₂ c₆,
        0 < c₁ ∧
          c₁ ≤ C ∧
            C ≤ c₂ ∧
              0 < c₆ ∧
                (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) ∧
                  Filter.Tendsto (fun m => lam m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds C) ∧
                    ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → |lam m * ↑m ^ D.p - C| ≤ c₆ * ↑m ^ (-D.vartheta)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_of_cutBal.doc:
**`theo:doubling_sharp`, with no hypothesis beyond the cut balance and positivity.**

`eq:doubling_sharp` is the convergence, `eq:doubling_rate` the bound with `ϑ = Decay.vartheta`,
and `c₁ ≤ C ≤ c₂` records the limit inside the decay window that `theo:doubling_decay`(2)
produces.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_limit.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    d < 2 * L →
      20 ≤ L →
        32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
          0 < c₁ →
            0 ≤ c₃ →
              (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) →
                (∀ (ℓ y : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ) →
                  ∃ C,
                    Filter.Tendsto (fun m => D.uu lam m) Filter.atTop (nhds C) ∧
                      c₁ ≤ C ∧
                        C ≤ c₂ ∧
                          ∀ (ℓ i m : ℕ),
                            L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_limit.doc:
**`eq:doubling_sharp`.** The rescaled profile `u_m = λ_m m^{p_*}` converges; its limit lies in
`[c₁,c₂]`; and the convergence carries the explicit error `c₂(1−ω)^i + 2c₂c₃/ℓ` at every level
`ℓ ≥ L` and every `i` with `2^iℓ ≤ m`.

This is the third bullet of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`, with the Cauchy criterion; the
paper's optimisation of the error over `ℓ` and `i` — `eq:doubling_rate` — is not carried out.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_explicit.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    D.m0 d ≤ ℓ →
      ∀ {a b : ℝ},
        0 < a →
          (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) →
            ∃ C,
              a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)) ≤ C ∧
                C ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ) ∧
                  Filter.Tendsto (fun m => lam m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds C) ∧
                    ∀ (m : ℕ),
                      1 ≤ m →
                        |lam m * ↑m ^ D.p - C| ≤
                          D.c6 d (b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)) * ↑m ^ (-D.vartheta)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp_explicit.doc:
**`theo:doubling_sharp` with every constant written out.** If the rescaled profile lies in
`[a, b]` on the initial block `1 ≤ j < 2ℓ`, `ℓ ≥ m₀`, `a > 0`, then the limit `C` lies in
`[a e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ}, b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}]`, `c₄ = 16cτ`, and `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ c₆ m^{−ϑ}` at every
`m ≥ 1` with `c₆ = c6 d (b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ})` — a formula in `c`, `d` and the initial block, which is
the paper's dependence clause "`c₆` depends on `c`, `d`, `λ_1..λ_{2m₀}` alone" made precise.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    d < 2 * L →
      20 ≤ L →
        32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
          0 < c₁ →
            0 ≤ c₃ →
              (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) →
                (∀ (ℓ y : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ) →
                  ∃ C c₆,
                    0 < c₆ ∧
                      c₁ ≤ C ∧
                        C ≤ c₂ ∧
                          Filter.Tendsto (fun m => lam m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds C) ∧
                            ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → |lam m * ↑m ^ D.p - C| ≤ c₆ * ↑m ^ (-D.vartheta)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.sharp.doc:
**`theo:doubling_sharp`, assembled.** The rescaled profile `λ_m m^{p_*}` converges to a limit
`C ∈ [c₁,c₂]` — this is `eq:doubling_sharp` — and the convergence carries the polynomial rate
`eq:doubling_rate` with the paper's exponent `ϑ = α/(1+α)`, `α = log₂(1/(1−ω))`.

`Decay.cutBal_unique` supplies the remaining clause of the theorem: `C` is determined by `c`, `d`
and `λ_1,…,λ_d`.

The input `hweight` is `lem:doubling_weight` in transform form (`Weight.lean`,
`Decay.weight_bound`); `SharpFull.lean` discharges it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.recOn.type:
{motive : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay → Sort u} →
  (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) →
    ((c p : ℝ) →
        (c_pos : 0 < c) →
          (c_lt_one : c < 1) →
            (p_ne : p ≠ 0) →
              (root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0) →
                motive { c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root }) →
      motive t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.rec.type:
{motive : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay → Sort u} →
  ((c p : ℝ) →
      (c_pos : 0 < c) →
        (c_lt_one : c < 1) →
          (p_ne : p ≠ 0) →
            (root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0) →
              motive { c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root }) →
    (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) → motive t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.rate_of_large.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₂ c₃ C : ℝ},
  20 ≤ L →
    0 < c₂ →
      0 ≤ c₃ →
        (∀ (ℓ i m : ℕ), L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ↑ℓ)) →
          ∀ {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → ↑L ≤ ↑m ^ D.vartheta → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (4 ^ D.alph + 2 * c₃) * ↑m ^ (-D.vartheta)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.rate_of_large.doc:
**The rate at a large index.** At every `m` with `L ≤ m^ϑ`, the level `ℓ := ⌈m^ϑ⌉` and the
index `i := ⌊log₂(m/ℓ)⌋` turn `Sharp.sharp_limit`'s error into `c₂(4^α + 2c₃) m^{−ϑ}`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.quarter_lt_gam.doc: `γ > ¼`, which is what makes the threshold `32cτ` cover `4cτ/y ≤ γ/2`. Not in the paper.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.qm_pos.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 < D.qm m j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.qm_eq.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (m j : ℕ), D.qm m j = D.c / ((↑j + 1) * (1 - D.eps m))

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_two_sided.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ} {d : ℕ},
  D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ →
    0 ≤ H →
      H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 →
        (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) →
          ∀ {m : ℕ}, 2 * ℓ ≤ m → Real.exp (-(D.c5 * H / ↑ℓ)) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b m ∧ D.prodW ℓ b m ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * H / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_two_sided.doc:
**`eq:doubling_product`, in the paper's own form**: at a level `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂` and a starting state
`m ≥ 2ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_two_sided.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    0 ≤ H →
      H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 →
        (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) →
          ∀ (z : ℕ), Real.exp (-(D.c5 * H / ↑ℓ)) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z ∧ D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * H / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_two_sided.doc:
**`eq:doubling_product`.** `e^{−c₅H/ℓ} ≤ E(∏_{n<N_ℓ}(1+b(Y_n)) | Y₀ = z) ≤ e^{c₅H/ℓ}`.

Stated at every starting state `z`, the paper's `m ≥ 2ℓ` being unnecessary: below `2ℓ` the
product is empty and `1` lies in the interval.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_step_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    0 ≤ H →
      H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 →
        (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) →
          ∀ {L : ℕ},
            32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
              2 * ℓ ≤ L →
                ∀ {A : ℝ}, 0 ≤ A → (∀ w < L, D.prodW ℓ b w ≤ A) → ∀ z < 2 * L, D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ A * (1 + D.c5 * H / ↑L)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_step_le.doc:
**One block of the paper's induction, upper half.** `φ_i ≤ φ_{i−1}(1 + c₅H/L)` at
`L = 2^i ℓ`: the block comparison `prodW_block_le` at `ζ = 1 + H/L`, followed by the third line
of `eq:doubling_sojourn`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_step_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    0 ≤ H →
      H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 →
        (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) →
          ∀ {L : ℕ},
            32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
              2 * ℓ ≤ L →
                ∀ {A : ℝ},
                  0 ≤ A → (∀ w < L, A ≤ D.prodW ℓ b w) → ∀ z < 2 * L, A * (1 - 2 * H / (D.gam ^ 2 * ↑L)) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_step_ge.doc:
**One block of the paper's induction, lower half.** `φ̲_i ≥ φ̲_{i−1}(1 − 2H/(γ²L))` at
`L = 2^i ℓ`: the block comparison `prodW_block_ge` at `x = H/L`, followed by the second line of
`eq:doubling_sojourn`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_of_lt.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ) {z : ℕ}, z < 2 * ℓ → D.prodW ℓ b z = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_of_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ) {z : ℕ},
  ¬z < 2 * ℓ → D.prodW ℓ b z = (1 + b z) * ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z, D.pk z j * D.prodW ℓ b j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_nonneg.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ → ∀ {b : ℕ → ℝ}, (∀ (y : ℕ), 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y) → ∀ (z : ℕ), 0 ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_nonneg.doc:
The product of non-negative factors is non-negative: the paper's "the factors being
positive".

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_level_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    0 ≤ H →
      H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 →
        (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) →
          ∀ (i z : ℕ), z < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ → D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * H / ↑ℓ * (1 - 1 / 2 ^ i))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_level_le.doc:
**The level invariant, upper half.** `Ψ(z) ≤ exp(c₅H/ℓ·(1 − 2^{−i}))` for every
`z < 2^{i+1}ℓ` — the paper's `φ_i ≤ ∏_{r≤i}(1 + c₅H2^{−r}/ℓ)`, with the partial geometric sum
kept, so that the induction on `i` is exact rather than asymptotic.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_level_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    0 ≤ H →
      H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 →
        (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) →
          ∀ (i z : ℕ), z < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ → Real.exp (-(4 * H / (D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ) * (1 - 1 / 2 ^ i))) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_level_ge.doc:
**The level invariant, lower half.** `Ψ(z) ≥ exp(−4H/(γ²ℓ)·(1 − 2^{−i}))` for every
`z < 2^{i+1}ℓ` — the paper's `φ̲_i ≥ e^{−4H/(γ²ℓ)}`, again with the partial sum kept.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_block_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ L : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
      2 * ℓ ≤ L →
        ∀ {b : ℕ → ℝ},
          (∀ (y : ℕ), 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y) →
            ∀ {zeta A : ℝ},
              0 ≤ zeta →
                (∀ (y : ℕ), L ≤ y → y < 2 * L → 1 + b y ≤ zeta) →
                  (∀ w < L, D.prodW ℓ b w ≤ A) → ∀ z < 2 * L, D.prodW ℓ b z ≤ A * D.sojGF L zeta z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_block_le.doc:
**The block step, upper half.** If `1 + b ≤ ζ` on `I = [L,2L)` and `Ψ ≤ A` below `L`, then
`Ψ(z) ≤ A · E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = z)` for every `z < 2L`.

This is the paper's `Ψ(z) = E(∏_{n<ς}(1+b(Y_n)) Ψ(Y_ς))` followed by `|b| ≤ ζ − 1` on the block,
with the strong Markov property at `ς` replaced by strong induction on the state.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_block_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ L : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L →
      2 * ℓ ≤ L →
        ∀ {b : ℕ → ℝ},
          (∀ (y : ℕ), 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y) →
            ∀ {x A : ℝ},
              x ≤ 1 →
                0 ≤ A →
                  (∀ (y : ℕ), L ≤ y → y < 2 * L → 1 - x ≤ 1 + b y) →
                    (∀ w < L, A ≤ D.prodW ℓ b w) → ∀ z < 2 * L, A * (1 - x * D.sojMean L z) ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_block_ge.doc:
**The block step, lower half.** If `1 − x ≤ 1 + b` on `I = [L,2L)` and `A ≤ Ψ` below `L`,
then `A · (1 − x·E(ς | Y₀ = z)) ≤ Ψ(z)` for every `z < 2L`.

This is the paper's `(1−x)^ς ≥ 1 − ςx`, in the form the induction can carry: the step produces
`(1−x)·A·(1 − x·E(ς) + x) = A·(1 − x·E(ς)) + A·x²·(E(ς) − 1)`, and `E(ς) ≥ 1` inside the block
is what makes the extra term non-negative.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_R0_eq_des.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ → ∀ {bb : ℕ → ℝ}, (∀ (y : ℕ), bb y = D.R0 y - 1) → ∀ (z : ℕ), D.prodW ℓ bb z = D.descOne ℓ z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW_R0_eq_des.doc:
The two recursions coincide at `b := R₀ − 1`: `(1 + (R₀(z) − 1))·(w_z(j)/R₀(z)) = w_z(j)`,
so `prodW ℓ (R₀ − 1) = descOne ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.prodW.doc:
**The weighted product of a descent.**
`prodW ℓ b z = E(∏_{n<N_ℓ}(1 + b(Y_n)) | Y₀ = z)`, as the recursion in the state that
characterises it: the factor at the current state times the average of the same quantity after
one step of the transition law `Decay.pk`, and `1` once the descent has fallen below `2ℓ`.

Well-founded because every `j ∈ W(z)` has `j < z` — `lem:doubling_descent`(1).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.pk_nonneg.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {z : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑z → ∀ {j : ℕ}, j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z → 0 ≤ D.pk z j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.pk.doc:
**The transition law of `lem:doubling_descent`.** `P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = z) = w_z(j)/R₀(z)` for
`j ∈ W(z)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_lt_ctau.doc:
`cτ > 1`: indeed `cτ = p_* + c` and `p_* > 1`. Not in the paper; it is what makes the
threshold `32cτ` automatically larger than the absolute constants Step 1 needs.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_le_sojMean.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑L → L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L → 1 ≤ D.sojMean L z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_le_sojMean.doc: `E(ς) ≥ 1` inside the block: one step is always taken there.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_le_prodW.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ → ∀ {b : ℕ → ℝ}, (∀ (y : ℕ), 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ b y) → ∀ (z : ℕ), 1 ≤ D.prodW ℓ b z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_le_prodW.doc:
The product transform is at least `1` when its factors are: `prodW ℓ b ≥ 1` for `b ≥ 0`
above `2ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_le_of_mem_w.type: ∀ {m j : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m → 1 ≤ j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_le_of_mem_w.doc: Every index of `W(m)` is a positive integer, `m` being positive.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_add_b_nonne.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} {b : ℕ → ℝ} {H : ℝ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    0 ≤ H → H ≤ D.gam ^ 2 * ↑ℓ / 6 → (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → |b y| ≤ H / ↑y) → ∀ (y : ℕ), 2 * ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ 1 + b y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.one_add_b_nonne.doc:
**Every factor of the product is positive.** `|b| ≤ H/(2ℓ) ≤ γ²/12 < 1` above `2ℓ`, which is
the paper's "every factor lies in `[½,3/2]`" in the only direction the recursion needs.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.omeg_le_case_on.doc: `(c/4) ln(5/4) ≤ 1`, so `ω ≤ (c/4) ln(8/5)`: the two cases of the proof combine.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.omeg.doc: **`ω := (c²/16) ln(5/4) ln(8/5)`**, the minorization constant of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ofC_c.type: ∀ {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1), (GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ofC hc0 hc1).c = c

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ofC.doc:
**`p_*(c)` packaged.** At `0 < c < 1` the Cramér equation `c(2^p − 1) = p` has a non-zero real
root (`lem:doubling_cramer_root`, since `c ≠ 1/ln 2`); this is the `Decay` carrying it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.nu_nonneg.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ}, 1 ≤ d → ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 ≤ D.nu d j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.nu_nonneg.doc:
**Step 3, first clause: `ν_j ≥ 0`.** The solution with indicator data is non-negative, so its
profile is, and so is the limit.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.nu_eq_zero.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ}, 1 ≤ d → ∀ {j : ℕ}, 2 * j ≤ d → D.nu d j = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.nu_eq_zero.doc:
**Step 3, third clause: `ν_j = 0` whenever `2j ≤ d`.** Above the cut the solutions with data
`1 + e_j` and `1` coincide (`extend_congr_high`), so the profile of `e_j`'s solution is eventually
`0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.nu.doc:
**The coefficients of `eq:doubling_constant`:** `ν_j := C(1 + e_j) − C(1)`, a difference of two
limits that `theo:doubling_sharp` provides, both data being positive.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.noConfusionType.type: Sort u → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay → Sort u

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.noConfusion.type: {P : Sort u} → {t t' : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay} → t = t' → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.noConfusionType P t t'

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.mk.sizeOf_spec.type:
∀ (c p : ℝ) (c_pos : 0 < c) (c_lt_one : c < 1) (p_ne : p ≠ 0) (root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0),
  sizeOf { c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root } =
    1 + sizeOf c + sizeOf p + sizeOf c_pos + sizeOf c_lt_one + sizeOf root

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.mk.noConfusion.type:
{P : Sort u} →
  {c p : ℝ} →
    {c_pos : 0 < c} →
      {c_lt_one : c < 1} →
        {p_ne : p ≠ 0} →
