          {root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0} →
            {c' p' : ℝ} →
              {c_pos' : 0 < c'} →
                {c_lt_one' : c' < 1} →
                  {p_ne' : p' ≠ 0} →
                    {root' : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c' p' = 0} →
                      { c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root } =
                          { c := c', p := p', c_pos := c_pos', c_lt_one := c_lt_one', p_ne := p_ne', root := root' } →
                        (c = c' → p = p' → P) → P

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.mk.injEq.type:
∀ (c p : ℝ) (c_pos : 0 < c) (c_lt_one : c < 1) (p_ne : p ≠ 0) (root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0) (c_1 p_1 : ℝ)
  (c_pos_1 : 0 < c_1) (c_lt_one_1 : c_1 < 1) (p_ne_1 : p_1 ≠ 0) (root_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c_1 p_1 = 0),
  ({ c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root } =
      { c := c_1, p := p_1, c_pos := c_pos_1, c_lt_one := c_lt_one_1, p_ne := p_ne_1, root := root_1 }) =
    (c = c_1 ∧ p = p_1)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.mk.inj.type:
∀ {c p : ℝ} {c_pos : 0 < c} {c_lt_one : c < 1} {p_ne : p ≠ 0} {root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0} {c_1 p_1 : ℝ}
  {c_pos_1 : 0 < c_1} {c_lt_one_1 : c_1 < 1} {p_ne_1 : p_1 ≠ 0} {root_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c_1 p_1 = 0},
  { c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root } =
      { c := c_1, p := p_1, c_pos := c_pos_1, c_lt_one := c_lt_one_1, p_ne := p_ne_1, root := root_1 } →
    c = c_1 ∧ p = p_1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.mk.type: (c p : ℝ) → 0 < c → c < 1 → p ≠ 0 → GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0 → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.mem_block.type: ∀ {i ℓ n : ℕ}, n ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.block i ℓ ↔ 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ n ∧ n < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.m0.doc:
**`m₀` of `theo:doubling_decay`**, `max(ℓ₂, ⌈6c₄/γ²⌉)`: the level at which
`eq:doubling_product` may be run at `b := R₀ − 1` and `H := c₄`, i.e. at which `c₄ ≤ γ²ℓ/6`.
With `R0Bound.lean`'s effective `c₄ = 16cτ` and `Escape.lean`'s effective `ℓ₂` it is explicit:
`m₀ = max(ℓ₂, ⌈96cτ/γ²⌉)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.levelL.doc:
**The level of the sharp block**, `L = max(ℓ₃, 20, d+1, m₀(d), ⌈32cτ⌉)`: past it every
hypothesis of `Sharp.sharp_limit` and `Decay.weight_bound` holds.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.le_term.doc: Term by term: `j^{−p−1} − j^{−p−2} ≤ j^{−p}/(j+1)`, since `(j−1)(j+1) ≤ j²`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.le_of_mem_windo.type: ∀ {ℓ m j : ℕ}, 2 * ℓ ≤ m → j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m → ℓ ≤ j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.le_of_mem_windo.doc:
Every index of the window of an `m ≥ 2ℓ` is at least `ℓ`: this is `⌈m/2⌉ ≥ ℓ`, and it is where
`lem:doubling_descent`(2) — the descent lands in `[ℓ,2ℓ)` — enters.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.kern_nonneg.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ}, 2 ≤ m → ∀ {j : ℕ}, j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m → 0 ≤ D.kern m j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.kern_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {z : ℕ},
  2 ≤ z → D.R0 z ≤ 2 → ∀ {j : ℕ}, j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z → D.c / (2 * (↑j + 1)) ≤ D.kern z j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.kern_ge.doc:
**Second bullet of the proof of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** One step from a state `z` with
`R₀(z) ≤ 2` gives every `j ∈ W(z)` mass at least `c/(2(j+1))`.

The paper's three ingredients: `(z/j)^p ≥ 1` because `j ≤ z − 1`; `q_z(j) ≥ c/(j+1)` because
`0 < 1 − ε(z) < 1`; and `R₀(z) ≤ 2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.kern_eq_pk.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (z j : ℕ), D.kern z j = D.pk z j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.kern_eq_pk.doc: The one-step law of `DescentLaw.lean` and the one of `Sojourn.lean` are the same function.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.kern.doc: The one-step transition law of the descent chain, `k_y(j) = w_y(j)/R₀(y)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.inner_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L j : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑j →
    (∀ k ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco j, k < L) →
      ∑ k ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window j, D.pk j k * GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L k ≤ 1 - D.gam
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.inner_le.doc:
**One step out of the block, from an already halved state.** If every halving of `j` leaves
the block, then the chance of staying in it at the next step is at most `1 − γ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB_eq_zero.type: ∀ {L z : ℕ}, z < L → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB L z = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.indB.doc: The indicator of the block `I = [L, 2L)`; `I_i(ℓ)` at `L = 2^i ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ind.doc: The indicator `e_j` of the index `j`, as boundary data.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.head_shift_le.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {y : ℕ}, 1 ≤ y → ∀ {z : ℝ}, ↑y / √2 ≤ z → z ^ (-D.p) ≤ D.sqTau * ↑y ^ (-D.p)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.head_shift_le.doc: **The head of the halving window.** Any `z ≥ y/√2` has `z^{−p} ≤ √τ y^{−p}`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halve_halve_lt.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {L z j k : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑z →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑j →
      z < 2 * L → j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco z → k ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco j → k < L
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halve_halve_lt.doc:
**Two halvings leave the block.** If `j ≤ z/√2`, `k ≤ j/√2` and `z < 2L`, then `k < L`.
This is what makes the paper's estimate two-step: one halving from `z < 2L` only reaches
`√2 L`, which is still inside the block.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco_subset.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {z : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑z → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco z ⊆ GFNBounds.Doubling.window z

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco_eq_fil.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {y : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑y → GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco y = {j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window y | ↑j * √2 ≤ ↑y}
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco_eq_fil.doc:
The interval `halveIco y` is exactly `{j ∈ W(y) : j√2 ≤ y}`, so `escape` really does bound
the transition probability of `eq:doubling_escape`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco.doc: The halving window `{j : ⌈y/2⌉ ≤ j ≤ ⌊y/√2⌋}`, as an interval of integers.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.half_le_R0.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {z : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑z → 1 / 2 ≤ D.R0 z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.half_le_R0.doc: `R₀(z) ≥ ½` above the threshold: `eq:doubling_R0`, first half.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.geom_sum_le_inv.type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, 0 ≤ x → x < 1 → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, x ^ i ≤ 1 / (1 - x)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.gam_lt_half.doc: `γ < ½`, as the statement of `lem:doubling_escape` asserts.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.foot_shift_ge.doc:
**The foot of the halving window.** With `a = ⌈y/2⌉`, `(a+1)^{−p} ≥ τ y^{−p}(1 − 4p/y)`.
This is the paper's `a+1 ≤ (y/2)(1+4/y)` followed by `(1+x)^{−p} ≥ 1 − px`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_zero.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (m : ℕ), D.extend d (fun x => 0) m = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_unique.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} {lam b : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ → 1 ≤ d → (∀ j ≤ d, lam j = b j) → ∀ (m : ℕ), lam m = D.extend d b m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_unique.doc: Nothing else with the same boundary data solves it: the coordinate map is injective.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_sum.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} {ι : Type u_1} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ),
  D.extend d (fun i => ∑ j ∈ s, f j i) m = ∑ j ∈ s, D.extend d (f j) m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_sum.doc: Linearity of `extend` in the data, over a finite sum.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_smul.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ),
  D.extend d (fun j => t * b j) m = t * D.extend d b m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_smul.doc: The extension is homogeneous in the boundary data.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_pos.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ),
  1 ≤ d → (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 < b j) → ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → 0 < D.extend d b m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_pos.doc: Positivity of the sequence is positivity of the boundary data.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_of_le.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ}, m ≤ d → D.extend d b m = b m

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_of_gt.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ},
  d < m → D.extend d b m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.qm m j * D.extend d b j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_nonneg.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ),
  (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 ≤ b j) → ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → 0 ≤ D.extend d b m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_nonneg.doc:
Non-negative data give a non-negative solution at every `m ≥ 1` — the induction of
`extend_pos` with `≤` in place of `<`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_eq_sum_i.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ (b : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ),
      1 ≤ m → D.extend d b m = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, b j * D.extend d (GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ind j) m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_eq_sum_i.doc:
Above index `0`, the solution is the sum of its data on `1..d` against the solutions with
indicator data: `(extend d b)_m = Σ_{j=1}^{d} b_j (extend d e_j)_m` for `m ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_cutBal.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b : ℕ → ℝ), 1 ≤ d → D.CutBal d (D.extend d b) ⊤

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_congr_hi.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ),
  (∀ (j : ℕ), d < 2 * j → j ≤ d → b₁ j = b₂ j) → ∀ (m : ℕ), d < m → D.extend d b₁ m = D.extend d b₂ m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_congr_hi.doc:
**The mechanism behind `ν_j = 0` for `2j ≤ d`.** Above the cut `d`, the solution does not see
the boundary data at an index `j` with `2j ≤ d`: every window of an `m > d` starts at
`⌈m/2⌉ ≥ (d+1)/2 > d/2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_add.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} (b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ),
  D.extend d (fun j => b₁ j + b₂ j) m = D.extend d b₁ m + D.extend d b₂ m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend_add.doc: The extension is additive in the boundary data.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.extend.doc:
The solution of `eq:doubling_avg` with boundary data `b` on `{0,…,d}`. Well-founded because
every `j ∈ W(m)` is below `m`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_sum.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ y : ℕ}, 1 ≤ ℓ → ℓ ≤ y → ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), D.exitLaw ℓ y z = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_sum.doc: **The exit law is a probability on `[ℓ,2ℓ)`.**

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_of_lt.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ y j : ℕ}, y < 2 * ℓ → D.exitLaw ℓ y j = if y = j then 1 else 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_of_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ y : ℕ},
  ¬y < 2 * ℓ → ∀ (j : ℕ), D.exitLaw ℓ y j = ∑ z ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window y, D.kern y z * D.exitLaw ℓ z j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_nonneg.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ}, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ (j y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ D.exitLaw ℓ y j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_nonneg.doc: The exit law is non-negative on the base block.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_mix.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ a : ℕ},
  ℓ ≤ a → ∀ {y : ℕ}, a ≤ y → ∀ (k : ℕ), D.exitLaw ℓ y k = ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico a (2 * a), D.exitLaw a y z * D.exitLaw ℓ z k
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.exitLaw_mix.doc:
**`π_y = ∑_{z ∈ [a,2a)} μ_y(z) π_z`.** The mixture identity of `lem:doubling_coupling`, third
bullet, with `μ_y` the exit law from the block `[a,2a)` and `π` the exit laws to `[ℓ,2ℓ)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_sum.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {y : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑y → 2 * D.gam - 4 * D.c * D.tau / ↑y ≤ ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco y, D.wm y j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_sum.doc:
**`lem:doubling_escape`, Step 1, un-normalised.** The paper's display

`Σ_{j=⌈y/2⌉}^{⌊y/√2⌋} w_y(j) ≥ 2γ − 4cτ/y`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_pk.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {z : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑z → D.gam ≤ ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco z, D.pk z j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_pk.doc: **`eq:doubling_escape` as a mass.** `Σ_{j ≤ y/√2} P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_of_level.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ y : ℕ},
  D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → D.gam ≤ (∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window y with ↑j * √2 ≤ ↑y, D.wm y j) / D.R0 y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_of_level.doc:
**`eq:doubling_escape` at the level `ℓ`**, exactly as `lem:doubling_escape` states it:
for every `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂` and every `y ≥ 2ℓ`, `P(Y₁ ≤ y/√2 | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape_filter.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {y : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑y → D.gam ≤ (∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window y with ↑j * √2 ≤ ↑y, D.wm y j) / D.R0 y

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {y : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑y → D.gam ≤ (∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.halveIco y, D.wm y j) / D.R0 y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.escape.doc:
**`eq:doubling_escape`.** `P(Y₁ ≤ y/√2 | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`, the transition law of
`lem:doubling_descent` being `w_y(j)/R₀(y)` on `W(y)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.eps_le_half.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {j : ℕ}, 1 ≤ j → D.eps j ≤ D.c / 2

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ell3.doc:
**`ℓ₃`, made effective.** `ℓ₃ := max(1, ⌈16cτ⌉, ⌈96cτ/γ²⌉)`: the first requirement is
`32cτ ≤ 2ℓ`, under which `eq:doubling_R0` and the one-step law are available; the second is
`c₄ ≤ γ²ℓ/6`, the hypothesis of `eq:doubling_product` at `H := c₄`, and simultaneously
`c₅c₄/ℓ ≤ 1`, which is what `e^x − 1 ≤ 2x` needs.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ell2_le_m0.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (d : ℕ), D.ell2 d ≤ D.m0 d

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.ell2.doc:
**`ℓ₂`, made effective.** `ℓ₂ := max(d+1, ⌈16cτ⌉)`, so that `y ≥ 2ℓ ≥ 2ℓ₂` gives `y ≥ 32cτ`,
which is all three of the paper's requirements at once.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.doeblin_low.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {a : ℕ},
  20 ≤ a →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑a →
      ∀ {y : ℕ},
        2 * a ≤ y →
          y < (5 * a + 1) / 2 →
            ∀ (j : ℕ), D.c / 4 * Real.log (8 / 5) * GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi a j ≤ D.exitLaw a y j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.doeblin_low.doc:
**Third bullet of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** A state `y ∈ I_i(ℓ)` below `⌈5a/2⌉` leaves the
block, in one step, with law at least `(c/4)ln(8/5) ϖ_i`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.doeblin.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {a : ℕ},
  20 ≤ a →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑a →
      ∀ {y : ℕ}, 2 * a ≤ y → y < 4 * a → ∀ (j : ℕ), D.omeg * GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.varpi a j ≤ D.exitLaw a y j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.doeblin.doc:
**`eq:doubling_doeblin`.** Every state of `I_i(ℓ) = [2a,4a)` leaves the block with law at
least `ω ϖ_i`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW_uu.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞},
  D.CutBal d lam M₁ → d < 2 * ℓ → ∀ (m : ℕ), ↑m ≤ M₁ → D.uu lam m = D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW_uu.doc:
**`eq:doubling_pathid`.** The rescaled profile is the fixed point of the descent transform:
`u_m = E(Z_ℓ u_{Y_{N_ℓ}} | Y_0 = m)`. Proved by strong induction on `m`, as the paper's is.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW_of_lt.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ}, m < 2 * ℓ → D.descW ℓ g m = g m

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW_of_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ},
  ¬m < 2 * ℓ → D.descW ℓ g m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.wm m j * D.descW ℓ g j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW_between.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  1 ≤ ℓ →
    ∀ {g : ℕ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ},
      (∀ (j : ℕ), ℓ ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ g j ∧ g j ≤ b) →
        ∀ (m : ℕ), ℓ ≤ m → a * D.descOne ℓ m ≤ D.descW ℓ g m ∧ D.descW ℓ g m ≤ b * D.descOne ℓ m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW_between.doc:
**The sandwich.** A function bounded between `a` and `b` on the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` has its
descent transform bounded between `a·E(Z_ℓ)` and `b·E(Z_ℓ)`.

This is where items (1) and (2) of `lem:doubling_descent` are consumed: the recursion terminates
(item 1) and its base case is reached inside `[ℓ,2ℓ)` (item 2).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descW.doc:
**The descent transform.** `descW D ℓ g m = E(Z_ℓ · g(Y_{N_ℓ}) | Y_0 = m)`, written as an
unnormalized recursion: the `R_0` of the transition law and the `R_0` of the weight `Z_ℓ` cancel.

Well-founded because every `j ∈ W(m)` has `j < m` — which is `lem:doubling_descent`(1).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_uu_diff_l.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  0 < c₁ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) →
      ∀ {ℓ : ℕ},
        20 ≤ ℓ →
          32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑ℓ →
            ∀ (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ},
              2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m →
                2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m' → |D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) m - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) m'| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_uu_diff_l.doc:
**The coupling step.** Two descent averages of the profile, started above `2^iℓ`, differ by at
most `c₂(1−ω)^i`. This is the first bullet of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp` minus its two
weight terms.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_one.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ}, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → D.descP ℓ (fun x => 1) y = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_one.doc: `descP ℓ 1 = 1`: the recursion preserves the constants, `k_y` being a probability.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_of_lt.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ}, m < 2 * ℓ → D.descP ℓ g m = g m

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_of_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ},
  ¬m < 2 * ℓ → D.descP ℓ g m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.kern m j * D.descP ℓ g j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_eq_sum.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) (y : ℕ),
  ℓ ≤ y → D.descP ℓ g y = ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), D.exitLaw ℓ y z * g z
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_eq_sum.doc:
**`lem:doubling_descent`(2), normalised.** The exit law is a law on the base block:
`descP ℓ g y = ∑_{z ∈ [ℓ,2ℓ)} exitLaw ℓ y z · g z` for every `y ≥ ℓ`.

Proved by strong induction on `y`, as the paper's item (2) is.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_diff_eq.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ} (u : ℕ → ℝ) {y y' : ℕ},
  ℓ ≤ y →
    ℓ ≤ y' → D.descP ℓ u y - D.descP ℓ u y' = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), u k * (D.exitLaw ℓ y k - D.exitLaw ℓ y' k)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_diff_eq.doc: The difference of two descent averages, as one sum against the difference of the exit laws.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_comp.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ a : ℕ},
  ℓ ≤ a → ∀ (g : ℕ → ℝ) (y : ℕ), D.descP ℓ g y = D.descP a (fun z => D.descP ℓ g z) y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descP_comp.doc:
**The strong Markov property at the block-exit time**, in the recursion's own terms:
descending to the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` is descending to the block `[a,2a)` and then continuing.

The paper's third bullet in the proof of `lem:doubling_coupling`. Here it needs only `ℓ ≤ a`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descOne_two_sid.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ},
  D.m0 d ≤ ℓ →
    ∀ (y : ℕ),
      Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)) ≤ D.descOne ℓ y ∧
        D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descOne_two_sid.doc:
**`eq:doubling_product` at `b := R₀ − 1`, `H := c₄`.** The expected weight of a descent is
`1 + O(1/ℓ)`, two-sidedly: `e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ} ≤ E(Z_ℓ | Y₀ = y) ≤ e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}` with `c₄ = 16cτ`.

This is the hypothesis `hlo`/`hhi` of `Decay.decay_block`, discharged.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descOne_of_lt.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ m : ℕ}, m < 2 * ℓ → D.descOne ℓ m = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descOne_of_ge.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ m : ℕ},
  ¬m < 2 * ℓ → D.descOne ℓ m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.wm m j * D.descOne ℓ j

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.descOne.doc: `E(Z_ℓ | Y_0 = m)`, the expected weight of a descent.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_two_sided.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) →
      D.m0 d ≤ ℓ → ∃ c₁ c₂, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j ∧ lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_two_sided.doc:
**`theo:doubling_decay`(2), unconditional.** Every positive sequence satisfying the cut
balance above `d` obeys `c₁ j^{−p_*} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p_*}` for every `j ≥ 1`, with no hypothesis
left beyond the cut balance and positivity: `eq:doubling_product` has discharged `hlo`/`hhi`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_two_sided.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    D.m0 d ≤ ℓ →
      ∀ {a b : ℝ},
        0 ≤ a →
          (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) →
            ∀ (j : ℕ),
              1 ≤ j →
                a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)) * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j ∧
                  lam j ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ) * ↑j ^ (-D.p)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_two_sided.doc:
**`eq:doubling_decay` with the constants written out** — `theo:doubling_decay`(2) and its
dependence clause. With `a ≤ λ_j j^{p_*} ≤ b` on `1 ≤ j < 2ℓ`, `ℓ ≥ m₀`, `0 ≤ a`:
`a e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ} j^{−p_*} ≤ λ_j ≤ b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ} j^{−p_*}` for every `j ≥ 1`, `c₄ = 16cτ`. The
existential form is `decay_two_sided_of_cutBal`; this is its witness.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_two_sided.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) →
      d < 2 * ℓ →
        1 ≤ ℓ →
          ∀ {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ},
            0 < Z₁ →
              Z₁ ≤ 1 →
                1 ≤ Z₂ →
                  (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) →
                    (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) →
                      ∃ c₁ c₂, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j ∧ lam j ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_two_sided.doc: **`eq:doubling_decay`.** `c₁ j^{−p_*} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p_*}` for every `j ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_block_of_.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞},
  D.CutBal d lam M₁ →
    D.m0 d ≤ ℓ →
      ∀ {a b : ℝ},
        0 ≤ a →
          (∀ (j : ℕ), ℓ ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) →
            ∀ {m : ℕ},
              ℓ ≤ m →
                ↑m ≤ M₁ →
                  a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)) ≤ D.uu lam m ∧
                    D.uu lam m ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / ↑ℓ)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_block_of_.doc:
**`eq:doubling_block`, unconditional.** One block of the rescaled profile bounds every index
above it, within `e^{±c₅c₄/ℓ}` — `theo:doubling_decay`(1), with `min`/`max` over `[ℓ,2ℓ)`
replaced by any pair bracketing the profile there, which is what `Decay.decay_block` takes and
what its two uses supply.

Stated at every `m ≥ ℓ`, the paper's `m ≥ 2ℓ` being unnecessary.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_block.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞},
  D.CutBal d lam M₁ →
    d < 2 * ℓ →
      1 ≤ ℓ →
        ∀ {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ},
          (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) →
            (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) →
              ∀ {a b : ℝ},
                0 ≤ a →
                  (∀ (j : ℕ), ℓ ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) →
                    ∀ {m : ℕ}, ℓ ≤ m → ↑m ≤ M₁ → a * Z₁ ≤ D.uu lam m ∧ D.uu lam m ≤ b * Z₂
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.decay_block.doc:
**`eq:doubling_block`.** One block of the profile bounds every index above it, within the
two-sided bound on `E(Z_ℓ)` that `lem:doubling_product` supplies.

`hlo` and `hhi` are `eq:doubling_product` at `b := R_0 − 1`, `H := c₄`; they are the block's only
unproved input, and are hypotheses here rather than hidden.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.cutBal_unique.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} {lam lam' : ℕ → ℝ},
  D.CutBal d lam ⊤ → D.CutBal d lam' ⊤ → (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → lam j = lam' j) → ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → lam m = lam' m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.cutBal_unique.doc:
**Fifth bullet of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`.** Two sequences satisfying
`eq:doubling_cut` at every `m > d` and agreeing on `λ_1,…,λ_d` agree everywhere; so `c`, `d` and
the boundary data determine the whole sequence, and with it the limit `C`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.cutBal_of_setti.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞},
  (∀ (j : ℕ), S.eps j = D.eps j) → GFNBounds.Doubling.CutBalanceSeq S lam M₁ → D.CutBal S.d lam M₁
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.cutBal_of_setti.doc: The bridge: a `Setting` whose `ε` is the family at `s = 1` gives `Decay.CutBal`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.cramer_mul.doc: `c(τ−1) = p_*`, the Cramér equation cleared of its denominator.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.coupling_above.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  20 ≤ ℓ →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑ℓ →
      ∀ (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ},
        2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m →
          2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m' →
            GFNBounds.Doubling.tvOn (Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ)) (D.exitLaw ℓ m) (D.exitLaw ℓ m') ≤ (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.coupling_above.doc:
**The coupling bound above a block.** Two descents started anywhere above `2^i ℓ` — not
necessarily in the same block — reach the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` with laws at total variation at
most `(1−ω)^i`.

This is `eq:doubling_coupling` composed with one further application of the mixture identity, at
`ω = 0`, where `tvOn_mix_le` degenerates to the triangle inequality. It replaces the paper's
*second* bullet in the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp` ("two states above `2^iℓ` have profiles
differing by at most `c₂(1−ω)^i + 3c₂c₃/ℓ`") and is strictly stronger: it needs neither the
block index of `m` nor a second descent at the level `2^jℓ`, and the constant it yields
downstream is `2c₂c₃/ℓ` rather than `3c₂c₃/ℓ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.coupling.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  20 ≤ ℓ →
    32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑ℓ →
      ∀ (i y : ℕ),
        y ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.block i ℓ →
          ∀ y' ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.block i ℓ,
            GFNBounds.Doubling.tvOn (Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ)) (D.exitLaw ℓ y) (D.exitLaw ℓ y') ≤ (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.coupling.doc:
**`eq:doubling_coupling`.** Two descents started in `I_i(ℓ)` reach the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)`
with laws at total variation at most `(1−ω)^i`.

By induction on `i`, exactly as the paper's proof.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.constant_functi.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∃ ν,
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 0 ≤ ν j) ∧
        0 < ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, ν j ∧
          (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 2 * j ≤ d → ν j = 0) ∧
            ∀ (lam : ℕ → ℝ),
              D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
                (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) →
                  Filter.Tendsto (fun m => lam m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, ν j * lam j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.constant_functi.doc:
**`prop:doubling_constant`, Steps 2 and 3, packaged in the paper's shape.** There are
`ν_1,…,ν_d ≥ 0` with `Σ ν_j > 0` and `ν_j = 0` for `2j ≤ d` such that every positive solution of the
cut balance at every `m > d` has `λ_m m^{p_*} → Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j λ_j`, i.e. `eq:doubling_constant`.
The witness is `D.nu d`, defined above as a difference of limits.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.constant_eq.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ},
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ {lam : ℕ → ℝ},
      D.CutBal d lam ⊤ →
        ∀ {C : ℝ},
          Filter.Tendsto (fun m => lam m * ↑m ^ D.p) Filter.atTop (nhds C) → C = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * lam j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.constant_eq.doc:
**`eq:doubling_constant`, in the paper's words:** the constant `C` of `theo:doubling_sharp` at
a positive solution is `Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j λ_j`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.climit_eq_sum.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ}, 1 ≤ d → ∀ (b : ℕ → ℝ), D.climit d b = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 d, D.nu d j * b j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.climit_eq_sum.doc: `C(b) = Σ_{j=1}^{d} ν_j b_j` for every data `b`: the `limUnder` is the linear functional.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.climit.doc:
`C(b) := lim_m (extend d b)_m m^{p_*}`, the constant `theo:doubling_sharp` attaches to the
solution of the cut balance with boundary data `b`. Stated as a `limUnder`; it is the actual limit
whenever `b` is positive on `1..d` (`tendsto_climit_of_pos`), and in fact for every `b`
(`climit_eq_sum`).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.casesOn.type:
{motive : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay → Sort u} →
  (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) →
    ((c p : ℝ) →
        (c_pos : 0 < c) →
          (c_lt_one : c < 1) →
            (p_ne : p ≠ 0) →
              (root : GFNBounds.Doubling.psi c p = 0) →
                motive { c := c, p := p, c_pos := c_pos, c_lt_one := c_lt_one, p_ne := p_ne, root := root }) →
      motive t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.c6.doc:
**`c₆` of `eq:doubling_rate`, written out**: `c₂(4^α + 2c₃) + c₂ m₃^ϑ` with
`m₃ = max(1, ⌈L^{1/ϑ}⌉)`, `L = levelL d` and `c₂` the upper decay constant.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.block_eq.type: ∀ (i ℓ : ℕ), GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.block i ℓ = Finset.Ico (2 ^ i * ℓ) (2 * (2 ^ i * ℓ))

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.avg_of_cutBal.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞},
  D.CutBal d lam M₁ → ∀ {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → d < m → ↑m ≤ M₁ → lam m = ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, D.qm m j * lam j
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.avg_of_cutBal.doc:
**`eq:doubling_avg`.** Dividing `eq:doubling_cut` by `1 − ε(m)` turns the balance across the
cut into an *average* of the sequence over the window below it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.alph_mul_one_su.doc: `α(1 − ϑ) = ϑ`, the identity the rate turns on.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.abs_descW_sub_d.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ →
    ∀ {b : ℕ → ℝ},
      (∀ (y : ℕ), 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.R0 y - 1| ≤ b y) →
        ∀ {B : ℝ} {g : ℕ → ℝ},
          (∀ (j : ℕ), |g j| ≤ B) → ∀ (y : ℕ), |D.descW ℓ g y - D.descP ℓ g y| ≤ B * (D.prodW ℓ b y - 1)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.abs_descW_sub_d.doc:
**`lem:doubling_weight`, in the form the sharp block consumes.** The unnormalised and the
normalised descent transforms of a function bounded by `B` differ by at most `B·(prodW − 1)`,
where `prodW` is the product transform at any `b` dominating `|R₀ − 1|` above `2ℓ`.

Proved by strong induction on the state; the step is `Decay.weight_step`. This replaces the
paper's pathwise `|Z_ℓ − 1| ≤ ∏_{n<N_ℓ}(1 + b̃(Y_n)) − 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.abs_descP_le.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {ℓ : ℕ},
  32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ 2 * ↑ℓ → ∀ {B : ℝ} {g : ℕ → ℝ}, (∀ (j : ℕ), |g j| ≤ B) → ∀ (y : ℕ), |D.descP ℓ g y| ≤ B
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.abs_descP_le.doc: The normalised transform of a function bounded by `B` is bounded by `B`: it is an average.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.abs_b_le_block.doc: Above a block floor `L ≥ ℓ`, the bound `|b(y)| ≤ H/y` reads `|b(y)| ≤ H/L`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_sub_one_le.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → |D.R0 m - 1| ≤ 16 * D.c * D.tau / ↑m

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_pos.doc: `R₀(m) > 0` at `m ≥ 2`: it is a sum of positive terms over a non-empty window.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_le_two_of.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {a : ℕ}, 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑a → 20 ≤ a → ∀ {z : ℕ}, a ≤ z → D.R0 z ≤ 2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_le_two_of.doc: `R₀(z) ≤ 2` at every state of the two blocks in play.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_eq.type:
∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ},
  1 ≤ m → D.R0 m = D.c / (1 - D.eps m) * (↑m ^ D.p * ∑ j ∈ GFNBounds.Doubling.window m, ↑j ^ (-D.p) / (↑j + 1))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_eq.doc: `R₀(m)` in the form the comparison uses: a constant times `m^p` times a window sum.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0_between.type: ∀ (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {m : ℕ}, 1 ≤ m → 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ↑m → 1 / 2 ≤ D.R0 m ∧ D.R0 m ≤ 2

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.R0.doc: `R_0(m) = Σ_{j ∈ W(m)} w_m(j)`, the total weight of the window — `eq:doubling_R` at `α = 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.Gamma_lt_one.doc:
**`eq:doubling_signs`, `Γ < 1`.** The gap is `2τ − p − 2 > 0`, the third inequality of
`eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.CutBal.doc: `eq:doubling_cut` as a predicate on a bare sequence, with `ε` the family at `s = 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.A_one_neg.doc:
**`eq:doubling_signs`, `A₁ < 0`.** The sign is `p + 3 − 4τ < 0`, the fourth inequality of
`eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.A_gap.doc: **`rem:doubling_parity`.** The two parities differ at order `1/m` by `A₀ − A₁ = cτ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay.doc:
The decay parameters: `c` in the standing range at `s = 1`, and a non-zero root `p` of the
Cramér equation `c(2^p − 1) = p`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.CutBalanceSeq.doc:
The recursion `eq:doubling_cut` as a predicate on a bare real sequence, with no invariance and
no normalisation.

This is the hypothesis `theo:doubling_decay` and `theo:doubling_sharp` actually carry
(`app_doubling.tex:1155`, `:1323`: "any positive sequence satisfying `eq:doubling_cut` at every
`m > d`"), and stating it this way is what lets `cor:doubling_truncation` apply them to `λ^K`
extended past the cap. `M₁` is the upper end of the range on which the recursion is asserted:
`⊤` on the loop closure, `K/2` on the truncation.

GFNBounds.Doubling.CVec.doc: Measures on the truncated chain: a finite-dimensional real vector space.

GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss_decomposition.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
            (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
              0 < zhat →
                GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e =
                  ((GFNBounds.Core.klD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) +
                        b * GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) -
                      Real.log zhat +
                    GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k
GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss_decomposition.doc:
**`eq:wFM_strong_bound`** (`proofs.tex:311–314`): decomposing the cross-entropy of the target
against `f̂_term` as forward KL plus self-entropy plus normalization,

  `𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} = KL(κ ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)) + b‖δf_init‖_{L^q(ν_T)} − log κ̂(𝒮) + 𝓗` .

`zhat` is `κ̂(𝒮)`; `il_mass_identity` is what turns `log κ̂(𝒮)` into `log(1 + δ)` downstream.

GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → MeasureTheory.Measure α → ℝ → ℝ → (α → ℝ) → (α → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss.doc:
**The KL-weak-FM loss `equ:weakFM`** (`introduction.tex:122`), in densities:

`𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} = b‖δf_init‖_{L^q(ν_T)} − 𝔼_{s∼κ} log f̂_term(s)`,

with `δf_init = e⁻` and `f̂_term = e⁺`. Real-valued: see this file's SCOPE on `hac`.

GFNBounds.Core.withDensity_bindDensity.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν → ∀ (f : α → ENNReal), ν.withDensity (GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν f) = (ν.withDensity f).bind ⇑κ
GFNBounds.Core.withDensity_bindDensity.doc:
**`T f` is a genuine density for `(f ν) π⋆`.** This is the well-definedness assertion of
`universality.tex:26–27`. Invariance is what it consumes, through absolute continuity; no
finiteness of `∫ f dν` is needed, the Lebesgue decomposition being available because the push of
a finite kernel is s-finite and `ν` is σ-finite.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversal_of_massPr.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p →
    (∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)), ∫ (x : α), ↑↑(P f) x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν) →
      (Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p‖) →
        p ≠ ⊤ → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversal P (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p)
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversal_of_massPr.doc:
**`theo:universality_L2_full` at `p < ∞`, on the paper's own hypotheses about `P`.**

This is `Core.UniversalityLp.weaklyUniversal_Lp` with `Mixing P Pi` replaced by what the paper
derives it from: `P` fixes the constants (`ν_B π⋆ = ν_B`), `P` preserves `ν_B`-integrals
(`π⋆` is a Markov kernel), and the mixing coefficients against the mean projection are summable.
`Π` is no longer a hypothesis at all — it is `meanProj`.

What is still assumed, and is the whole of the remaining debt: that `P` is a bounded operator on
`L^p(ν)` with those two properties, rather than the density action of a Markov kernel `π⋆`
constructed from it. See SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversal_of_kernel.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (p : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C),
  (Summable fun n => ‖GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p‖) →
    p ≠ ⊤ → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversal (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p)
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversal_of_kernel.doc:
**`theo:universality_L2_full`'s weak half, from the paper's own hypotheses about the kernel.**

`π⋆` is a Markov kernel, `ν` is finite and `π⋆`-invariant, `P⋆` is bounded on `L^p(ν)` with
constant `C` — the paper's requirement on the parameterization — and the mixing coefficients
`β_n = ‖P⋆^n − Π‖` are summable. Then `Θ = {π⋆} × L^p_+(ν)` is weakly `L^p`-universal for
`p < ∞`, with `Π` the mean projection of `proofs.tex:22`.

No operator is hypothesised: `P⋆` is built from `π⋆` here, `Π P⋆ = P⋆ Π = Π` is derived in
`Core.Flow` from `hone` and `hint`, and those two are theorems above. What remains assumed is
what the paper assumes — boundedness and summable mixing.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversal_Lp.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p → p ≠ ⊤ → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversal P Pi
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversal_Lp.doc:
**`theo:universality_L2_full`, weak half, with `def:universality`'s quantifier closed**:
for `p ≠ ∞`, under summable mixing and with `P` fixing the constants, the family
`Θ = {P} × L^p_+(ν)` is weakly `L^p`-universal — every pair of equal total mass is reachable,
each by its own outflow.

This is the paper's conclusion for `p < ∞`. What it still assumes rather than derives is
`Mixing P Pi` and `P 𝟏 = 𝟏`; see this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_of_tend.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [HasSolidNorm E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E]
  [inst_4 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} {one θ : E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P one = one →
      Pi θ = 0 →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun η => ‖GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi one θ η‖) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) →
          GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt P θ
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_of_tend.doc:
**Weak universality from a vanishing truncation.** Step 3 of `theo:universality_L2_full`
for `p < ∞`, with the analytic half — `‖ψ_η‖ → 0` as `η → +∞`, which is dominated convergence
on a concrete `L^p` — carried as the hypothesis it is. `Core.UniversalityLp` discharges it.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_of_kern.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (p : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C),
  (Summable fun n => ‖GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p‖) →
    p ≠ ⊤ →
      ∀ {f_init f_term : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
        ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_init x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_term x ∂ν →
          GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) (f_term - f_init)
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_of_kern.doc:
**The same, at one admissible pair**: two densities in `L^p(ν)` of equal total mass are
joined to arbitrary accuracy by a non-negative outflow against the kernel `π⋆`.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_of_equa.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p →
    (∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)), ∫ (x : α), ↑↑(P f) x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν) →
      (Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p‖) →
        p ≠ ⊤ →
          ∀ {f_init f_term : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
            ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_init x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_term x ∂ν → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt P (f_term - f_init)
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_of_equa.doc:
**The same, at one admissible pair**, in the paper's own terms: two densities in `L^p(ν)` of
equal total mass are joined to arbitrary accuracy by a non-negative outflow.

GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_Lp.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)}
  {θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p →
      Pi θ = 0 → p ≠ ⊤ → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt P θ
GFNBounds.Core.weaklyUniversalAt_Lp.doc:
**`theo:universality_L2_full`, its conclusion at `p < +∞`**: the family
`Θ = {P} × L^p_+(ν)` is weakly `L^p`-universal.

Steps 1 and 2 are `Core.Mixing` and `Core.Universality`; Step 3 is
`tendsto_truncation_norm` above, and this is their composition. The hypotheses are the two the
construction consumes — `P` fixes the constants and `Π θ = 0` — together with summable
mixing.

GFNBounds.Core.tv_le_two_fmL1.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        ∀ {z t zhat tv tvNC : ℝ},
          z = ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν →
            t = ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν →
              zhat = ∫ (x : α), max (e x) 0 ∂ν →
                0 < z →
                  0 < t →
                    tvNC ≤ (∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν) / zhat →
                      (tv ≤ tvNC + GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν (fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) fun x => k x / t) →
                        tv ≤ (2 * ∫ (x : α), |e x - k x| ∂ν) / t
GFNBounds.Core.tv_le_two_fmL1.doc:
**`equ:tv_chain` closed at `2Δ/t`, Step 2 in full** (`proofs.tex:209–232`):

  `TV(s_τ ‖ κ/t) ≤ Δ/(z + Δ) + Δ/t ≤ 2Δ/t`,

with `Δ := ‖e − k‖_{L¹(ν_B)}`. Term (i) enters through `hNC`, which is
**`theo:negative_control`** (`proofs.tex:52–61`) — quoted by the paper from `\citet{brunswicEGF}`
and proved nowhere, here or there. Term (ii) is `normalization_bound`. The step
`u/(z+u) ≤ Δ/(z+Δ)` is the monotonicity of `x ↦ x/(z+x)` on `[0,∞)`, and `z + Δ ≥ t` is
`equ:mass_defect`.

GFNBounds.Core.tvD_triangle.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {f₁ f₂ f₃ : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => f₁ x - f₂ x) ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => f₂ x - f₃ x) ν →
      GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν f₁ f₃ ≤ GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν f₁ f₂ + GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν f₂ f₃
GFNBounds.Core.tvD_triangle.doc:
**The triangle inequality Step 2 opens with** (`proofs.tex:209–212`), for densities against a
common measure. It is what discharges the hypothesis `htri` of `tv_le_two_fmL1` whenever the law
of `s_τ` is itself `f·ν_B`.

GFNBounds.Core.tvD_normalization_le.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {f g : α → ℝ} {a b : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable g ν →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] g →
        a = ∫ (x : α), f x ∂ν →
          b = ∫ (x : α), g x ∂ν →
            0 < a → 0 < b → (GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν (fun x => f x / a) fun x => g x / b) ≤ (∫ (x : α), |f x - g x| ∂ν) / a
GFNBounds.Core.tvD_normalization_le.doc:
**`equ:normalization_lemma`, second inequality** (`proofs.tex:217–220`):
`TV(α/a ‖ β/b) ≤ ‖α − β‖_{L¹}/a`, by `|a − b| ≤ ‖α − β‖_{L¹}`. Here `a` must be `α(𝒮)`.

GFNBounds.Core.tvD_normalization.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {f g : α → ℝ} {a b : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable g ν →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] g →
        b = ∫ (x : α), g x ∂ν →
          0 < a →
            0 < b →
              (GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν (fun x => f x / a) fun x => g x / b) ≤
                (∫ (x : α), |f x - g x| ∂ν + |a - b|) / (2 * a)
GFNBounds.Core.tvD_normalization.doc:
**`equ:normalization_lemma`, first inequality** (`proofs.tex:217–220`): for `α = f·ν` and
`β = g·ν` non-negative and finite with masses `a, b > 0`,

  `TV(α/a ‖ β/b) ≤ (‖α − β‖_{L¹} + |a − b|)/(2a)`,

by the paper's own splitting `β/b − α/a = (β − α)/a + β(1/b − 1/a)`. Only `b = β(𝒮)` is needed;
see this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.tvD_nonneg.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f g : α → ℝ), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν f g

GFNBounds.Core.tvD_comm.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f g : α → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν f g = GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν g f

GFNBounds.Core.tvD.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ℝ) → (α → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.tvD.doc:
**The ½-convention total variation of `app:notation`**, read between two densities against a
common dominating measure: `TV(f·ν ‖ g·ν) = ½ ∫ |f − g| dν`. This is the appendix's own
definition, `\TV(\mu\|\nu) := \tfrac12\int|\frac{d\mu}{d\rho}-\frac{d\nu}{d\rho}|d\rho`
(`proofs.tex:22`), with `ρ = ν`.

GFNBounds.Core.truncation_nonneg.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E)
  (one θ : E) (η : ℝ), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi one θ η

GFNBounds.Core.truncation.type:
{E : Type u_1} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → E → ℝ → E
GFNBounds.Core.truncation.doc:
The **truncation** `ψ_η := (η • 1 - Sθ)⁻`, which the appendix also writes
`(Sθ - η)⁺`. It is the whole of the defect.

GFNBounds.Core.tendsto_truncation_norm.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)],
  p ≠ ⊤ →
    ∀ (P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)) (θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun η => ‖GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) θ η‖) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
GFNBounds.Core.tendsto_truncation_norm.doc:
**Step 3 of `theo:universality_L2_full`, `p < +∞`**: the truncation vanishes in `L^p(ν)`.

`0 ≤ ψ_η ≤ (Sθ)⁺ ∈ L^p(ν)` and `ψ_η → 0` pointwise as `η → +∞`, so dominated convergence gives
`‖ψ_η‖_{L^p(ν)} → 0`. No hypothesis on `P`, `Pi` or `θ` is used: the statement is about the
truncation of the fixed `L^p` element `Sθ`.

GFNBounds.Core.sub_le_mul_log_div.type: ∀ {x y : ℝ}, 0 ≤ x → 0 ≤ y → (y = 0 → x = 0) → x - y ≤ x * Real.log (x / y)
GFNBounds.Core.sub_le_mul_log_div.doc:
The pointwise inequality behind `klD_nonneg`: `x − y ≤ x log(x/y)` for `x, y ≥ 0`, provided
`y = 0` forces `x = 0`. It is `log t ≤ t − 1` at `t = y/x`, and the proviso is where absolute
continuity enters — at `y = 0 < x` the true value is `+∞` and Lean's `log 0 = 0` is not it.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversal_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤ → GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversal P Pi
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversal_top.doc:
**`theo:universality_L2_full`'s `p = +∞` clause, for the family**: under summable `L^∞`-mixing
and with `P` fixing the constants, `Θ = {P} × L^∞_+(ν)` is strongly universal.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversal_of_kern.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C),
  (Summable fun n => ‖GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν ⊤‖) →
    GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversal (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν ⊤)
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversal_of_kern.doc:
**Strong universality at `p = +∞`, from the paper's hypotheses on the kernel.**

`π⋆` a Markov kernel, `ν` finite and `π⋆`-invariant, the density action bounded on `L^∞(ν)`, the
mixing coefficients summable there. `P⋆ 𝟏 = 𝟏` and `Π P⋆ = P⋆ Π = Π` are *derived*, in
`Core/Kernel.lean` and `Core/Flow.lean`; nothing is hypothesised about an operator.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)} {θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤ → Pi θ = 0 → GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt P θ
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_top.doc:
**`theo:universality_L2_full`'s `p = +∞` clause, at one admissible pair.**

"Taking `η := ‖Sθ‖_{L^∞(ν_B)}` gives `δf_init = δf_term = 0`, and the flow-matching constraint
holds exactly" (`proofs.tex:73`). No order hypothesis survives: `le_norm_smul_constOne` supplies
it, and what is left is the same bundle the weak half consumes — summable mixing, `P 𝟏 = 𝟏`,
`Π θ = 0`.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_of_le.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] [inst_3 : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} {one θ : E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P one = one →
      Pi θ = 0 → ∀ {η : ℝ}, (GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) θ ≤ η • one → GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt P θ
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_of_le.doc:
**Strong universality when the truncation vanishes.** If `Sθ ≤ η • 1` for some `η` — which
at `p = +∞` is `η := ‖Sθ‖_∞`, the appendix's own choice — then `ψ_η = 0`, the defect is `0`
and the flow-matching constraint `equ:FM_const` holds *exactly*.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_of_ke.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν) (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C),
  (Summable fun n => ‖GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν ⊤‖) →
    ∀ {f_init f_term : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
      ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_init x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_term x ∂ν →
        GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb) (f_term - f_init)
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_of_ke.doc:
**The same at one admissible pair**, in the paper's own terms: two densities in `L^∞(ν)` of
equal total mass are joined *exactly* — not approximately — by a non-negative outflow.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_of_ke.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (r : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ r)] {C C' : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C) (hb' : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν r C'),
  (Summable fun n => ‖GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν ⊤‖) →
    ∀ {θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
      (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν ⊤) θ = 0 →
        GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν r hinv hb')
          (GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r θ)
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_of_ke.doc:
**`proofs.tex:114`'s last sentence, inside `defect`**: the outflow constructed at `p = +∞`
realizes the infimum in `L^r(ν)` as well.

`IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν r C'` appears only to name the operator on `L^r(ν)`; the mathematics
uses no bound at `r`, the defect being exactly zero. `exists_outflow_memLp_of_top` is the same
statement without that artefact.

GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_inclT.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {r : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ r)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)}
  {Q : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.CompatibleAcrossTop ν r P Q →
    ∀ {θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
      GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt P θ → GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt Q (GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r θ)
GFNBounds.Core.stronglyUniversalAt_inclT.doc:
**The cross-`p` transfer**, `def:universality`'s "realization at one `p` implies it at every
`p ≥ 1`": a pair realized exactly in `L^∞(ν)` is realized exactly in `L^r(ν)`, by the same
outflow.

It is a statement *at one pair*. It does not say that the `L^r` family is strongly universal —
see this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.stable_bound.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ} {νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  {M : NNReal} {q z t zhat tv tvNC : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    ∀ [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν],
      ν ≤ ↑M • νT →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => e x - k x) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
              0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
                z = ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν →
                  t = ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν →
                    zhat = ∫ (x : α), max (e x) 0 ∂ν →
                      0 < z →
                        0 < t →
                          tvNC ≤ (∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν) / zhat →
                            (tv ≤ tvNC + GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν (fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) fun x => k x / t) →
                              tv ≤ GFNBounds.Core.stableConst ν M q t * GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss νT q e k
GFNBounds.Core.stable_bound.doc:
**`equ:stable_bound`** (`proofs.tex:160–162`), the first display of item (1) of
**`theo:RL_CV_bound_full`**:

  `TV(s_τ ‖ κ/t) ≤ C 𝓛`,  `C = 2C₀/t` .

`tv` is `TV(s_τ ‖ κ/t)` and `tvNC` is `TV(s_τ ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮))`; `hNC` is
**`theo:negative_control`**, an external input the paper quotes and does not prove, and `htri`
is the triangle inequality Step 2 opens with, which `tvD_triangle` supplies for any sampler with
a `ν_B`-density. Both are disclosed in this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss_eq_lqNormD.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (q : ℝ) (e k : α → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss νT q e k = GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => e x - k x
GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss_eq_lqNormD.doc:
The `L^q` norm of this file and the loss of `StableBound` are the same object: the file that
proves `theo:RL_CV_bound_full` measures `e − k`, this one measures `δf_init = e⁻`.

GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → ℝ → (α → ℝ) → (α → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss.doc:
**The stable loss `𝓛` of `equ:FMloss`** as `proofs.tex:193` reads it,
`𝓛 = ‖e − k‖_{L^q(ν_T)}`, at `q < ∞`.

GFNBounds.Core.stableConst.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → NNReal → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy.doc:
**The self-entropy `𝓗` of `proofs.tex:264–266`**, the floor of the loss:
`𝓗 := −∫ k(s) log k(s) dν_B(s)` for a probability `κ = k·ν_B`. It is not a Shannon entropy:
replacing `ν_B` by `cν_B` shifts it by `log c`, and it is of either sign.

GFNBounds.Core.reversal_snk_src.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(4)*, the wrap edge** (`proofs.tex:444`): `π_→^λ(s_f → s₀) = 1`, so `s_f` is
not terminal for the forward policy. The wrap edge is the only edge out of `s_f` in `Ĝ`, hence
the only in-edge of `s_f` the backward policy can use, so the reversal's row at `s_f` — a
probability row where `λ > 0` — is the point mass at `s₀`.

GFNBounds.Core.reversal_reversal.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
    (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ A x y) →
      ∀ {x : V}, lam x ≠ 0 → ∀ (y : V), GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) x y = A x y
GFNBounds.Core.reversal_reversal.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(2)*, reversal is an involution `λ`-almost everywhere** (`proofs.tex:406`):
`(T^λ)^λ = T` at every state carrying `λ`-mass.

`λ(x) ≠ 0` is the *only* hypothesis: if `λ(y) = 0` as well, both sides vanish — the left by the
convention `a/0 = 0` and the right by `IsInvariant.eq_zero_of_ne_zero`.

GFNBounds.Core.reversal_of_eq_zero.type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ} {x : V}, lam x = 0 → ∀ (y : V), GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A x y = 0
GFNBounds.Core.reversal_of_eq_zero.doc:
Off the support of `λ` the reversal is the zero row — the `λ`-negligible set of
`proofs.tex:405`, made visible.

GFNBounds.Core.reversal_nonneg.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ lam x) → (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ A x y) → ∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A x y

GFNBounds.Core.reversal_hatEdge.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(4)*, the support** (`proofs.tex:444`, "it is positive only where
`π̂_←(s'→s) > 0`, hence only on edges `s → s'` of `Ĝ`").

GFNBounds.Core.reversal_apply.type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (lam : V → ℝ) (A : V → V → ℝ) (x y : V), GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A x y = lam y * A y x / lam x

GFNBounds.Core.reversal.type: {V : Type u_1} → (V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → V → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.reversal.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(1)*, the `λ`-reversal `T^λ`** (`proofs.tex:405`, entrywise form at
`proofs.tex:408`): `T^λ(x → y) = λ(y) T(y → x)/λ(x)`, the disintegration of `T ⊗ λ` over its
first marginal `λ`, done by division on a finite space.

Where `λ(x) = 0` the Lean convention `a / 0 = 0` makes the row vanish; that is exactly the
`λ`-negligible set on which the paper leaves `T^λ` undetermined.

GFNBounds.Core.residuals_le_two_norm_def.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [HasSolidNorm E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E]
  [inst_4 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E),
  ‖GFNBounds.Core.resInit P θ fout‖ + ‖GFNBounds.Core.resTerm P θ fout‖ ≤ 2 * ‖GFNBounds.Core.defect P θ fout‖

GFNBounds.Core.residuals_le.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [HasSolidNorm E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E]
  [inst_4 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} {one θ : E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P one = one →
      Pi θ = 0 →
        ∀ (η : ℝ),
          ‖GFNBounds.Core.resInit P θ (GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η)‖ +
              ‖GFNBounds.Core.resTerm P θ (GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η)‖ ≤
            2 * (1 + ‖P‖) * ‖GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi one θ η‖

GFNBounds.Core.resTerm.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → E → E
GFNBounds.Core.resTerm.doc: The residual against the target, `δf_term = D⁺`.

GFNBounds.Core.resInit.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → E → E
GFNBounds.Core.resInit.doc: The residual against the initial flow, `δf_init = D⁻`.

GFNBounds.Core.posPart_mass.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν → ∫ (x : α), max (e x) 0 ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν + ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν
GFNBounds.Core.posPart_mass.doc:
**`equ:mass_identity`, Step 0** (`proofs.tex:200–202`): `E⁺` and `E⁻` having disjoint
supports and `E(𝒮) = z`, the corrected terminal flow has mass `κ̂(𝒮) = z + E⁻(𝒮) ≥ z`. In
densities this is `∫ e⁺ = ∫ e + ∫ e⁻`.

GFNBounds.Core.phat_isMarkov.type:
∀ {V : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G), GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkov B.phat
GFNBounds.Core.phat_isMarkov.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(4)*, `T = π̂_←`**: the loop closure is a Markov kernel on `𝒱`
(`proofs.tex:408`, "which on a finite marked graph is the loop closure `π̂_←` […] and not `π_←`
itself").

GFNBounds.Core.penalty_ge.type: ∀ {b N D δ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ δ → 0 ≤ D → 1 + N ≤ b → δ ≤ N * D → D ≤ b * D - Real.log (1 + δ)
GFNBounds.Core.penalty_ge.doc:
**`eq:lp_delta`** (`proofs.tex:315–318`): `b‖δf_init‖ − log(1+δ) ≥ ‖δf_init‖ ≥ 0`, by
`log(1+δ) ≤ δ` and the Hölder estimate `δ ≤ N‖δf_init‖` with `b ≥ 1 + N`.

GFNBounds.Core.ofReal_add_aux.type:
∀ (u v : ℝ),
  ENNReal.ofReal (u + v) + ENNReal.ofReal (-u) + ENNReal.ofReal (-v) =
    ENNReal.ofReal (-(u + v)) + ENNReal.ofReal u + ENNReal.ofReal v
GFNBounds.Core.ofReal_add_aux.doc: The same identity in `ℝ≥0∞`, which is where `T` consumes it.

GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_one_pos.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ lam x) → (∃ x, 0 < lam x) → 0 < GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam fun x => 1
GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_one_pos.doc:
`‖λ‖_{𝓜²(λ)} > 0`: `λ` is non-zero and finite, so its own density `1` has positive norm.
The paper's reason why the two contractions have norm exactly `1`.

GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_funAct_le.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam A →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
      ∀ (u : V → ℝ), GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u) ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam u
GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_funAct_le.doc: **`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, the function action is a contraction of `L²(λ)`**.

GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_densAct_le.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkov A →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
      ∀ (u : V → ℝ), GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u) ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam u
GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_densAct_le.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, the density action is a contraction of `𝓜²(λ)`** — the paper's own
route, through `d(μT)/dλ = T^λ u` and the contraction of the reversal's function action.

GFNBounds.Core.nrmL2_congr.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam a a' : V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), lam x ≠ 0 → a x = a' x) → GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam a = GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam a'

GFNBounds.Core.normalization_bound.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        ∀ {t zhat : ℝ},
          t = ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν →
            zhat = ∫ (x : α), max (e x) 0 ∂ν →
              0 < t →
                0 < zhat →
                  (GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν (fun x => k x / t) fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) ≤
                    (∫ (x : α), |e x - k x| ∂ν) / t
GFNBounds.Core.normalization_bound.doc:
**Term (ii) of Step 2** (`proofs.tex:217–221`): `TV(κ/t ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)) ≤ Δ/t`, by
`equ:normalization_lemma` at `α = κ`, `β = κ̂` and `equ:two_dominations`.

GFNBounds.Core.norm_posPart_le.type:
∀ {F : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_1 : Lattice F] [HasSolidNorm F] [IsOrderedAddMonoid F] (a : F),
  ‖a⁺‖ ≤ ‖a‖
GFNBounds.Core.norm_posPart_le.doc:
`‖a⁺‖ ≤ ‖a‖` in a normed lattice: `a⁺ ≤ |a|` and both are non-negative, so the solid
axiom applies.

GFNBounds.Core.norm_negPart_le.type:
∀ {F : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_1 : Lattice F] [HasSolidNorm F] [IsOrderedAddMonoid F] (a : F),
  ‖a⁻‖ ≤ ‖a‖

GFNBounds.Core.norm_le_norm_posPart_add_.type: ∀ {F : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_1 : Lattice F] [IsOrderedAddMonoid F] (a : F), ‖a‖ ≤ ‖a⁺‖ + ‖a⁻‖

GFNBounds.Core.norm_integral_le_holder.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
  ‖∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν‖ ≤ (ν Set.univ).toReal ^ (1 - 1 / p.toReal) * ‖f‖
GFNBounds.Core.norm_integral_le_holder.doc:
**Hölder against `𝟏`**: `|∫ f dν| ≤ ν(𝒮)^{1 − 1/p} ‖f‖_{L^p(ν)}`.

The constant is `‖𝟏‖_{L^{p*}(ν)}`, and it is what makes the mean functional continuous. At
`p = ∞` the exponent is `1` and the bound reads `|∫ f| ≤ ν(𝒮) ‖f‖_∞`.

GFNBounds.Core.norm_integralCLM_le.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)], ‖GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM ν p‖ ≤ (ν Set.univ).toReal ^ (1 - 1 / p.toReal)
GFNBounds.Core.norm_integralCLM_le.doc:
`‖∫ · dν‖ ≤ ν(𝒮)^{1 − 1/p}`: the constant of `norm_integral_le_holder` bounds the operator
norm, which is rule 3's explicit formula rather than a bare existential.

GFNBounds.Core.norm_densityActionCLM_le.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (p : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C), ‖GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb‖ ≤ C
GFNBounds.Core.norm_densityActionCLM_le.doc: `‖P⋆‖_{L^p→L^p} ≤ C`: the paper's constant bounds the operator norm, as rule 3 asks.

GFNBounds.Core.norm_defect_le_residuals.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] [inst_3 : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  (P : E →L[ℝ] E) (θ fout : E),
  ‖GFNBounds.Core.defect P θ fout‖ ≤ ‖GFNBounds.Core.resInit P θ fout‖ + ‖GFNBounds.Core.resTerm P θ fout‖

GFNBounds.Core.negPart_le_abs_sub.doc:
**Step 1's first pointwise inequality** (`proofs.tex:204`): `k ≥ 0` gives `e⁻ ≤ |e − k|`,
because on `{e < 0}` one has `|e − k| = k − e ≥ −e`.

GFNBounds.Core.negMass_ratio_le_min.doc:
The first term of `equ:il_tv_split` (`proofs.tex:299–303`): `δ/κ̂(𝒮) = δ/(1+δ) ≤ min(1, δ)`,
by the mass identity.

GFNBounds.Core.negMass_le.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν → 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k → ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν ≤ ∫ (x : α), |e x - k x| ∂ν

GFNBounds.Core.mixing_of_massPreserving.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p →
    (∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)), ∫ (x : α), ↑↑(P f) x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν) →
      (Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p‖) → GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p)
GFNBounds.Core.mixing_of_massPreserving.doc:
**The `Mixing` bundle, with only its summability half assumed.** `Core.Mixing` hypothesizes
`Pi * P = Pi` and `P * Pi = Pi`; here they are the two theorems above, and `Pi` is pinned to the
paper's mean projection rather than left arbitrary. What remains a hypothesis is the summability
of `β_n = ‖P^n − Π‖`, which the paper hypothesizes too.

GFNBounds.Core.memLp_of_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (r : ENNReal) (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)), MeasureTheory.MemLp (↑↑f) r ν
GFNBounds.Core.memLp_of_top.doc: An `L^∞(ν)` function is in every `L^r(ν)`: finiteness of `ν` and nothing else.

GFNBounds.Core.measurable_densityAction.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α)
  (f : α → ℝ), Measurable (GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f)
GFNBounds.Core.measurable_densityAction.doc: `P⋆ f` is measurable, with no hypothesis on `f`.

GFNBounds.Core.measurable_bindDensity.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α)
  (f : α → ENNReal), Measurable (GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν f)
GFNBounds.Core.measurable_bindDensity.doc: `T f` is measurable, with no hypothesis on `f`: a Radon–Nikodym derivative always is.

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_sub_eq_zero.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {f_init f_term : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_init x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f_term x ∂ν → (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p) (f_term - f_init) = 0
GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_sub_eq_zero.doc:
**`Π θ = 0` for a pair of equal total mass** — the paper's "`F_init` and `F_term` are both
probability distributions, so `∫ θ dν_B = 0`, that is `Π θ = 0`" (`proofs.tex:95`).

Only the equality of the two integrals is used; non-negativity of the densities is not.

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_idem.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)],
  ν Set.univ ≠ 0 → GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p * GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p = GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p
GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_idem.doc:
`Π` is idempotent — it is a projection. `Core.Mixing` does not assume this (it derives
`Pi * Pi = Pi` from summability); here it is immediate from `∫ 𝟏 dν = ν(𝒮)`.

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_constOne.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)],
  ν Set.univ ≠ 0 → (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p) (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p
GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_constOne.doc: `Π 𝟏 = 𝟏`: the constants are fixed by the mean projection.

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_comp_left.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  (∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)), ∫ (x : α), ↑↑(P f) x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν) →
    GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p * P = GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p
GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_comp_left.doc:
**`Mixing.proj_left`, derived**: `Π P = Π`, from mass preservation alone.

The paper's `Π P⋆ = Π` (`proofs.tex:87`): the density action of a Markov kernel preserves
`ν_B`-integrals, so it does not move the mean, and the mean is all `Π` reads.

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj_apply.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
  (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p) f = ((∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν) / (ν Set.univ).toReal) • GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj.congr_simp.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (p : ENNReal)
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)],
  GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p = GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p

GFNBounds.Core.meanProj.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
      (p : ENNReal) →
        [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] →
          [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)
GFNBounds.Core.meanProj.doc:
**The mean projection of `proofs.tex:22`**, `Π f = (∫ f dν / ν(𝒮)) • 𝟏`, as a continuous
linear map on `L^p(ν)`.

This is the `Pi` that `Core.Mixing`, `Core.Universality` and `Core.UniversalityLp` carry as a
hypothesis. It is the paper's `Π` — the projection onto the *invariant* densities — exactly when
the policy is ergodic; see this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.max_add_aux.type: ∀ (u v : ℝ), max (u + v) 0 + max (-u) 0 + max (-v) 0 = max (-(u + v)) 0 + max u 0 + max v 0
GFNBounds.Core.max_add_aux.doc: The real identity behind additivity of `P⋆`: `(u+v)⁺ + u⁻ + v⁻ = (u+v)⁻ + u⁺ + v⁺`.

GFNBounds.Core.mass_floor.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ} {νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  {M : NNReal} {q z t : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    ∀ [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν],
      ν ≤ ↑M • νT →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => e x - k x) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
              z = ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν →
                t = ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν → |z - t| ≤ GFNBounds.Core.holderConst ν M q * GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss νT q e k
GFNBounds.Core.mass_floor.doc:
**`equ:mass_floor`** (`proofs.tex:164–166`), the second display of item (1) of
**`theo:RL_CV_bound_full`**:

  `|F_init(𝒮) − κ(𝒮)| ≤ C₀ 𝓛` .

`z` is `F_init(𝒮)` by Step 0's `E(𝒮) = F_init(𝒮)`, which is the hypothesis `hz` — see this
file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.mass_defect_le.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν → |∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν - ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν| ≤ ∫ (x : α), |e x - k x| ∂ν

GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD_nonneg.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (q : ℝ) (f : α → ℝ),
  0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q f

GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD_le_loss_sub_selfE.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b N δ zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
          ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = 1 →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
                (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
                  δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν →
                    zhat = 1 + δ →
                      1 + N ≤ b →
                        (δ ≤ N * GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) →
                          (GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) ≤
                            GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e - GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k
GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD_le_loss_sub_selfE.doc:
**`proofs.tex:332–334`**: `𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} − 𝓗 ≥ ‖δf_init‖_{L^q(ν_T)}`, the inequality that
turns the loss into a bound on the initial defect, hence on `δ` through `equ:il_holder`.

GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → ℝ → (α → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD.doc:
The `L^q(ν_T)` norm of a density, at a real exponent: `‖f‖_{L^q(ν_T)} = (∫|f|^q dν_T)^{1/q}`.
This is `StableBound`'s `stableLoss` with its two densities not yet subtracted; see
`stableLoss_eq_lqNormD`.

GFNBounds.Core.loss_sub_selfEntropy_ge.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b N δ zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
            (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
              δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν →
                zhat = 1 + δ →
                  1 + N ≤ b →
                    (δ ≤ N * GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) →
                      ((GFNBounds.Core.klD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) +
                          GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) ≤
                        GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e - GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k
GFNBounds.Core.loss_sub_selfEntropy_ge.doc:
**`proofs.tex:320–334` in one inequality**: the loss exceeds the floor by at least the KL term
and the `L^q` penalty together,

  `KL(κ ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)) + ‖δf_init‖_{L^q(ν_T)} ≤ 𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} − 𝓗` .

This is `eq:wFM_strong_bound` composed with `eq:lp_delta`; the two displays `proofs.tex:322` and
`proofs.tex:332–334` are its two halves. `hHolder` is `equ:il_holder`, which `il_holder` proves
for `1 < q < ∞`.

GFNBounds.Core.loss_le_of_domination.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b ε : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
            0 < q →
              νT.AbsolutelyContinuous ν →
                ε < 1 →
                  (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, (1 - ε) * k x ≤ e x) →
                    GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e ≤ GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k + Real.log (1 / (1 - ε))
GFNBounds.Core.loss_le_of_domination.doc:
**`equ:il_domination` bounds the loss above** (`proofs.tex:344–354`): if
`F_init + F⋆_out π⋆ − F⋆_out ≥ (1−ε)κ` as measures, then `δf_init = 0`, `f̂_term = e` and

  `𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} ≤ 𝓗 + log(1/(1−ε))` .

The `L^q` penalty vanishes for every `q`, every admissible `b` and every `ν_T`; `hTac : ν_T ≪ ν_B`
is the half of the paper's `ν_B ∼ ν_T` that transports "`e⁻ = 0` `ν_B`-a.e." to `ν_T`. Only
`ε < 1` is used, not the paper's `ε ∈ [0,1)`: the estimate is the same one at a negative `ε`,
where `equ:il_domination` is a stronger hypothesis and `log(1/(1−ε))` a negative slack.

GFNBounds.Core.loss_ge_selfEntropy.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b N δ zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
          ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = 1 →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
                (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
                  δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν →
                    zhat = 1 + δ →
                      1 + N ≤ b →
                        (δ ≤ N * GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) →
                          GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k ≤ GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e
GFNBounds.Core.loss_ge_selfEntropy.doc:
**The floor of the loss**, the first half of the first bullet (`proofs.tex:325`):
`𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} ≥ 𝓗`. Gibbs' inequality supplies `KL ≥ 0`, and the mass identity is what makes
`κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)` a probability density so that Gibbs applies.

GFNBounds.Core.loss_eq_selfEntropy_of_do.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b N δ zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
          ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = 1 →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
                (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
