                  δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν →
                    zhat = 1 + δ →
                      0 ≤ N →
                        1 + N ≤ b →
                          0 < q →
                            νT.AbsolutelyContinuous ν →
                              (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, k x ≤ e x) →
                                GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e = GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k
GFNBounds.Core.loss_eq_selfEntropy_of_do.doc:
**Attainment at `ε = 0`** (`proofs.tex:364–365`): a flow satisfying `equ:il_domination` with
`ε = 0` — equivalently, satisfying the flow-matching constraint `equ:FM_const` for the pair
`(F_init, κ)` — has `𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} = 𝓗`, the floor.

GFNBounds.Core.lintegral_ofReal_ne_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {f : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν → ∫⁻ (x : α), ENNReal.ofReal (f x) ∂ν ≠ ⊤
GFNBounds.Core.lintegral_ofReal_ne_top.doc: The positive part of an integrable function has finite `ν`-integral.

GFNBounds.Core.lintegral_bindDensity.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν → ∀ (f : α → ENNReal), ∫⁻ (x : α), GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν f x ∂ν = ∫⁻ (x : α), f x ∂ν
GFNBounds.Core.lintegral_bindDensity.doc:
**`∫ T f dν = ∫ f dν`** — the non-negative half of `hint`. It is stochasticity of `π⋆` that
is used here, each fibre `π⋆(x)` being a probability measure; invariance enters only through the
absolute continuity that makes `T f` a density at all.

GFNBounds.Core.lintegral_add_ne_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {u v : α → ENNReal},
  AEMeasurable u ν → ∫⁻ (x : α), u x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ → ∫⁻ (x : α), v x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ → ∫⁻ (x : α), (u + v) x ∂ν ≠ ⊤
GFNBounds.Core.lintegral_add_ne_top.doc: `∫ (u + v) dν` is finite when both summands are.

GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow_nonneg.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E)
  (one θ : E) (η : ℝ), 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η

GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow_eq.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] [inst_3 : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (one θ : E) (η : ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η =
    η • one - (GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) θ + GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi one θ η
GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow_eq.doc: `f_out^η = η • 1 - Sθ + ψ_η`: the appendix's `f_out^η ν_B - ν_∞^η = ψ_η ν_B`.

GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow.type:
{E : Type u_1} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → E → ℝ → E

GFNBounds.Core.le_norm_smul_constOne.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (g : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)), g ≤ ‖g‖ • GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤
GFNBounds.Core.le_norm_smul_constOne.doc:
**The order hypothesis of `stronglyUniversalAt_of_le`, discharged at `p = +∞`**:
`g ≤ ‖g‖ • 𝟏` in the `L^∞(ν)` order.

`Core/UniversalityLp.lean`'s SCOPE names exactly this — "instantiating it at `L^∞(ν)` would need
`Sθ ≤ ‖Sθ‖_∞ • 𝟏` in the `Lp` order, which is not proved here". The `Lp` order is the a.e.
order (`MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_le`), so `ae_le_norm_top` is the whole of it.

GFNBounds.Core.klD_normalized_nonneg.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {δ zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
          ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = 1 →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
                (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
                  δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν → zhat = 1 + δ → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.klD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat
GFNBounds.Core.klD_normalized_nonneg.doc:
**Gibbs at the normalized corrected terminal density** (`proofs.tex:322`):
`KL(κ ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)) ≥ 0`. The mass identity `equ:il_mass_identity` is what makes `κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)` a
probability density, which is the hypothesis `klD_nonneg` consumes.

GFNBounds.Core.klD_nonneg.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k g : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable g ν →
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x / g x)) ν →
        0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
          0 ≤ᵐ[ν] g →
            (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, g x = 0 → k x = 0) → ∫ (x : α), g x ∂ν ≤ ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.klD ν k g
GFNBounds.Core.klD_nonneg.doc:
**Gibbs' inequality, in the form `proofs.tex:322` uses it**: `KL(κ ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮)) ≥ 0`. Stated on
densities against a common measure, for `κ` of mass at least that of the comparison, and under
the absolute continuity `hac` without which the left-hand side is `+∞` rather than a real.

GFNBounds.Core.klD_le_loss_sub_selfEntro.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b N δ zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
            (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
              δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν →
                zhat = 1 + δ →
                  1 + N ≤ b →
                    (δ ≤ N * GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) →
                      (GFNBounds.Core.klD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) ≤
                        GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e - GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k
GFNBounds.Core.klD_le_loss_sub_selfEntro.doc:
**The KL term is at most the excess of the loss over its floor** (`proofs.tex:322`), the
inequality Pinsker is applied to.

GFNBounds.Core.klD_integrand_eq.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {zhat : ℝ},
  0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
    (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
      0 < zhat →
        (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x / (max (e x) 0 / zhat))) =ᵐ[ν] fun x =>
          k x * Real.log (k x) - k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0) + k x * Real.log zhat
GFNBounds.Core.klD_integrand_eq.doc:
The pointwise identity behind `wklfmLoss_decomposition`: on `{k > 0}`, where absolute
continuity makes `e⁺ > 0`, `log(k/(e⁺/ẑ)) = log k − log e⁺ + log ẑ`; on `{k = 0}` both sides
vanish.

GFNBounds.Core.klD_integrable.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {zhat : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
        0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
          (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
            0 < zhat → MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x / (max (e x) 0 / zhat))) ν
GFNBounds.Core.klD_integrable.doc:
The integrand of `klD ν k (κ̂/κ̂(𝒮))` is integrable as soon as the two integrands of the
decomposition are: it is their difference plus a multiple of `k`, off a null set.

GFNBounds.Core.klD.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ℝ) → (α → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.klD.doc:
**The Kullback–Leibler divergence of `proofs.tex:302`, read between densities**:
`KL(k·ν ‖ g·ν) = ∫ k log(k/g) dν`. Mathlib's `InformationTheory.klDiv` is `ℝ≥0∞`-valued and
defined between measures through `Measure.rnDeriv`; this file works in densities throughout, and
proves the single property the appendix uses — non-negativity — directly. See this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.isReversalPair_comm.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {lam : V → ℝ} {A R : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R ↔ GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam R A

GFNBounds.Core.isLeast_opNorm_funAct.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam A →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
      (∃ x, 0 < lam x) →
        IsLeast
          {c | ∀ (u : V → ℝ), GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u) ≤ c * GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam u} 1

GFNBounds.Core.isLeast_opNorm_densAct.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkov A →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
      (∃ x, 0 < lam x) →
        IsLeast
          {c |
            ∀ (u : V → ℝ), GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u) ≤ c * GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam u}
          1
GFNBounds.Core.isLeast_opNorm_densAct.doc: **`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, the density action has operator norm exactly `1`**.

GFNBounds.Core.isInvariant_of_isInvProb.type:
∀ {V : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) {lam : V → ℝ}, B.IsInvProb lam → GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam B.phat
GFNBounds.Core.isInvariant_of_isInvProb.doc:
An invariant probability of the backward chain is an invariant measure in the sense of this
file.

GFNBounds.Core.isGLB_of_domination.type:
∀ (L : Set ℝ) (H : ℝ),
  (∀ x ∈ L, H ≤ x) → (∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ x ∈ L, x ≤ H + Real.log (1 / (1 - ε))) → IsGLB L H
GFNBounds.Core.isGLB_of_domination.doc:
**`inf_Θ 𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} = 𝓗`** (`proofs.tex:356–359`), on the set of achievable loss values:
a set of reals bounded below by `𝓗` that comes within `log(1/(1−ε))` of it for every
`ε ∈ (0,1)` has `𝓗` for greatest lower bound. `Θ` itself is not modelled — see this file's
SCOPE — and the two hypotheses are supplied by `loss_ge_selfEntropy` and
`loss_le_of_domination` at each member.

GFNBounds.Core.isFiniteMeasure_bind_with.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) {f : α → ENNReal},
  ∫⁻ (x : α), f x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ → MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ((ν.withDensity f).bind ⇑κ)
GFNBounds.Core.isFiniteMeasure_bind_with.doc: `(f ν) π⋆` is a finite measure as soon as `f` has finite `ν`-integral.

GFNBounds.Core.isBoundedDensityAction_id.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] (p : ENNReal),
  GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.id ν p 1
GFNBounds.Core.isBoundedDensityAction_id.doc:
**`IsBoundedDensityAction` is satisfiable**, so `weaklyUniversal_of_kernel` is not vacuous:
the identity kernel is Markov, every measure is invariant under it (`bind_id`), and its density
action is the identity, of operator norm `1`. It is of course not ergodic and has no summable
mixing; the point of this witness is only that the boundedness hypothesis excludes nothing by
itself.

GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_funAct_self_le.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam A →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
      ∀ (u : V → ℝ),
        GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u) (GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u) ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam u u
GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_funAct_self_le.doc:
**`eq:reversal_contraction`** (`proofs.tex:424–425`): the function action of a kernel leaving
`λ` invariant is a contraction of `L²(λ)`.

GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_densAct_funAct.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
    (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ A x y) →
      ∀ (u v : V → ℝ),
        GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u) v =
          GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam u (GFNBounds.Core.funAct A v)
GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_densAct_funAct.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, the adjointness identity in density/function form**
(`proofs.tex:433–441`): `⟪μT ∣ ν⟫_λ = ∫ v · (Tv-side) dλ`, here `⟪d(μT)/dλ ∣ v⟫_λ =
⟪u ∣ Tv⟫_λ`. Two finite sums swapped, as `Graph.ipL2_pdens_qact` does for `π̂_←` —
**without that lemma's `λ > 0` hypothesis**, invariance supplying what positivity supplied
there.

GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_densAct_densAct.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A R : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
    (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ A x y) →
      GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R →
        ∀ (u v : V → ℝ),
          GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u) v =
            GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam u (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam R v)
GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_densAct_densAct.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, the adjointness of the two density actions** (`proofs.tex:407`):
`⟪μT ∣ ν⟫_λ = ⟪μ ∣ νT^λ⟫_λ` for `μ, ν ∈ 𝓜²(λ)`, carried by their densities `u, v`.

GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_congr_right.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam a b b' : V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), lam x ≠ 0 → b x = b' x) → GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam a b = GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam a b'
GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_congr_right.doc:
`⟪a ∣ ·⟫_λ` does not see a change off the support of `λ`. The bookkeeping lemma that lets the
`λ`-a.e. identities above be used inside an inner product.

GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_congr_left.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam a a' b : V → ℝ},

GFNBounds.Core.ipL2_congr_left.doc: `⟪· ∣ b⟫_λ` does not see a change off the support of `λ`.

GFNBounds.Core.integral_toReal_bindDensi.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
    ∀ {f : α → ℝ},
      MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
        ∫ (x : α), (GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) x).toReal ∂ν =
          (∫⁻ (x : α), ENNReal.ofReal (f x) ∂ν).toReal

GFNBounds.Core.integral_le_of_le_smul.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {M : NNReal},
  ν ≤ ↑M • νT → ∀ {f : α → ℝ}, 0 ≤ᵐ[νT] f → MeasureTheory.Integrable f νT → ∫ (x : α), f x ∂ν ≤ ↑M * ∫ (x : α), f x ∂νT
GFNBounds.Core.integral_le_of_le_smul.doc:
**Step 3, the change of measure** (`proofs.tex:237`): with `ν_B ≤ M ν_T`, an integral of a
non-negative function against `ν_B` is at most `M` times its integral against `ν_T`. This is the
paper's `∫ φ dν_B = ∫ φ (dν_B/dν_T) dν_T ≤ ‖dν_B/dν_T‖_{L^∞(ν_T)} ∫ φ dν_T`, in the form that
needs no Radon–Nikodym derivative.

GFNBounds.Core.integral_le_measure_rpow_.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {q : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    ∀ (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] {h : α → ℝ},
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] h →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp h (ENNReal.ofReal q) ν →
          ∫ (x : α), h x ∂ν ≤ ν.real Set.univ ^ (1 - 1 / q) * (∫ (x : α), h x ^ q ∂ν) ^ (1 / q)
GFNBounds.Core.integral_le_measure_rpow_.doc:
**Step 3, first Hölder** (`proofs.tex:236`): on a finite measure,
`∫ h dν ≤ ν(𝒮)^{1−1/q} ‖h‖_{L^q(ν)}` for `h ≥ 0` and `1 ≤ q < ∞`, by Hölder against the constant
`1` with the conjugate exponents `q` and `q/(q−1)`.

GFNBounds.Core.integral_densityActionCLM.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (p : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
  ∫ (x : α), ↑↑((GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) F) x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑F x ∂ν
GFNBounds.Core.integral_densityActionCLM.doc: **`hint` on `L^p(ν)`**: `∫ P⋆ f dν = ∫ f dν`.

GFNBounds.Core.integral_densityAction.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
    ∀ {f : α → ℝ}, MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν → ∫ (x : α), GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), f x ∂ν
GFNBounds.Core.integral_densityAction.doc:
**`hint`, in the paper's own terms**: `∫ P⋆ f dν = ∫ f dν` for every `ν`-integrable `f`.

Stochasticity of `π⋆` is what is used — each fibre `π⋆(x)` is a probability measure, so the push
`(f ν) π⋆` has the mass of `f ν`. Invariance enters only through the absolute continuity that
makes `P⋆ f` a density.

GFNBounds.Core.integral_constOne.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal}, ∫ (x : α), ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) x ∂ν = (ν Set.univ).toReal

GFNBounds.Core.integralLM.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
      (p : ENNReal) → [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] → [Fact (1 ≤ p)] → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.integralLM.doc: The mean functional `f ↦ ∫ f dν`, as a linear map on `L^p(ν)`.

GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM_apply.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
  (GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM ν p) f = ∫ (x : α), ↑↑f x ∂ν

GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM.congr_simp.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (p : ENNReal)
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)],
  GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM ν p = GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM ν p

GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
      (p : ENNReal) → [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] → [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.integralCLM.doc:
The mean functional `f ↦ ∫ f dν` as a **continuous** linear map on `L^p(ν)`, with the
explicit operator-norm bound `ν(𝒮)^{1 − 1/p}` of `norm_integral_le_holder`.

GFNBounds.Core.integrable_toReal_bindDen.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
    ∀ {f : α → ℝ},
      MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => (GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) x).toReal) ν
GFNBounds.Core.integrable_toReal_bindDen.doc: `(T f⁺).toReal` is `ν`-integrable, with `∫ (T f⁺).toReal dν = ∫ f⁺ dν`.

GFNBounds.Core.integrable_of_Lp.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)), MeasureTheory.Integrable (↑↑f) ν
GFNBounds.Core.integrable_of_Lp.doc:
An element of `L^p(ν)` is `ν`-integrable: `ν` is finite and `1 ≤ p`, so `L^p(ν) ⊆ L^1(ν)`.
This is what lets the appendix write `∫ θ dν_B` for `θ ∈ L^p(ν_B)` at all.

GFNBounds.Core.inclTop_nonneg.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {r : ENNReal} {f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)}, 0 ≤ f → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r f
GFNBounds.Core.inclTop_nonneg.doc: The inclusion is order-preserving, the `Lp` order being the a.e. order on both sides.

GFNBounds.Core.inclTop.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
      [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] → (r : ENNReal) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν)
GFNBounds.Core.inclTop.doc:
**The inclusion `L^∞(ν) ↪ L^r(ν)`**, `ν` finite. It is the appendix's
"`f_out^η ∈ L^∞(ν_B) ⊂ L^r(ν_B)` for every `r ∈ [1,+∞]`, since `ν_B` is finite"
(`proofs.tex:114`).

GFNBounds.Core.il_tv_bound.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ} {q b N δ zhat tv tvNC : ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν = 1 →
      0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
          ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = 1 →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (k x)) ν →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => k x * Real.log (max (e x) 0)) ν →
                (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, max (e x) 0 = 0 → k x = 0) →
                  δ = ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν →
                    zhat = 1 + δ →
                      0 ≤ N →
                        1 + N ≤ b →
                          (δ ≤ N * GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0) →
                            tvNC ≤ δ / zhat →
                              (GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) ≤
                                  1 / √2 * √(GFNBounds.Core.klD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) →
                                (tv ≤ tvNC + GFNBounds.Core.tvD ν k fun x => max (e x) 0 / zhat) →
                                  tv ≤
                                    1 / √2 * √(GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e - GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k) +
                                      min 1
                                        (N * (GFNBounds.Core.wklfmLoss ν νT q b k e - GFNBounds.Core.selfEntropy ν k))
GFNBounds.Core.il_tv_bound.doc:
**`equ:il_tv_explicit`** (`proofs.tex:274–276`), the second display of the first bullet of
**`theo:IL_CV_bound`**:

  `TV(s_τ ‖ κ) ≤ (1/√2)√(𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} − 𝓗) + min(1, ‖dν_B/dν_T‖_{L^{q*}(ν_T)}(𝓛^q_{KL-wFM} − 𝓗))` .

`tv` is `TV(s_τ ‖ κ)` and `tvNC` is `TV(s_τ ‖ κ̂/κ̂(𝒮))`. Three inputs are hypotheses on reals:
`htri`, the triangle inequality, which `Core.tvD_triangle` supplies for any sampler with a
`ν_B`-density; `hNC`, which is **`theo:negative_control`**, quoted by the paper from
`\citet{brunswicEGF}` and proved nowhere; and `hPins`, which is **Pinsker's inequality**, absent
from Mathlib v4.31.0. All three are disclosed in this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.il_mass_identity.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν → ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = 1 → ∫ (x : α), max (e x) 0 ∂ν = 1 + ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν
GFNBounds.Core.il_mass_identity.doc:
**`equ:il_mass_identity`** (`proofs.tex:292–297`): `E⁺` and `E⁻` having disjoint supports and
`E(𝒮) = F_init(𝒮) = 1`, the corrected terminal flow has mass `κ̂(𝒮) = 1 + δ ≥ 1`. In densities
this is `∫ e⁺ = 1 + ∫ e⁻`, one line from `Core.posPart_mass`.

GFNBounds.Core.il_holder.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν]
  [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite νT] {e : α → ℝ} {q qstar : ℝ},
  qstar.HolderConjugate q →
    ν.AbsolutelyContinuous νT →
      MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => (ν.rnDeriv νT x).toReal) (ENNReal.ofReal qstar) νT →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => max (-e x) 0) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT →
          ∫ (x : α), max (-e x) 0 ∂ν ≤
            (GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT qstar fun x => (ν.rnDeriv νT x).toReal) *
              GFNBounds.Core.lqNormD νT q fun x => max (-e x) 0
GFNBounds.Core.il_holder.doc:
**`equ:il_holder`** (`proofs.tex:305–310`): `ν_B ≪ ν_T` gives
`δ = ∫ δf_init (dν_B/dν_T) dν_T ≤ ‖dν_B/dν_T‖_{L^{q*}(ν_T)} ‖δf_init‖_{L^q(ν_T)}`, by Hölder with
the conjugate exponents `q*` and `q`. Proved for `1 < q < ∞` only: Mathlib's Hölder needs a
`Real.HolderConjugate` pair, which excludes the endpoints. See this file's SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Core.holderConst.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → MeasureTheory.Measure α → NNReal → ℝ → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.holderConst.doc:
**`equ:stable_constants`, `C₀`** (`proofs.tex:152–156`):
`C₀ = ν_B(𝒮)^{1−1/q} ‖dν_B/dν_T‖^{1/q}_{L^∞(ν_T)}`, with the `L^∞` norm carried by `M`.

GFNBounds.Core.hatDist_le.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν → 0 ≤ᵐ[ν] k → ∫ (x : α), |k x - max (e x) 0| ∂ν ≤ ∫ (x : α), |e x - k x| ∂ν

GFNBounds.Core.graph_reversal_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) (lam : V → ℝ), B.reversal lam = GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam B.phat
GFNBounds.Core.graph_reversal_eq.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(4)*, the entrywise formula** (`proofs.tex:408`):
`π_→^λ(s → s') = λ(s') π̂_←(s' → s)/λ(s)` is the general finite `λ`-reversal of `π̂_←`, so
`theo:universality_graphs`*(2)*'s `Graph.BackwardPolicy.reversal` **is** `reversal`.

GFNBounds.Core.graph_qact_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G), B.qact = GFNBounds.Core.funAct B.phat
GFNBounds.Core.graph_qact_eq.doc:
`Graph.BackwardPolicy.qact`, the function action of `prop:morozov_rate`, is `funAct` of
`π̂_←`.

GFNBounds.Core.graph_pdens_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] {G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V}
  (B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G) (lam : V → ℝ), B.pdens lam = GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam B.phat
GFNBounds.Core.graph_pdens_eq.doc:
`Graph.BackwardPolicy.pdens`, the density action of `prop:morozov_rate`, is `densAct` of
`π̂_←`.

GFNBounds.Core.funAct_mul_self_le.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam A →
    ∀ {x : V},
      lam x ≠ 0 → ∀ (u : V → ℝ), GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u x * GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u x ≤ ∑ y, A x y * (u y * u y)
GFNBounds.Core.funAct_mul_self_le.doc:
**`eq:reversal_contraction` pointwise** (`proofs.tex:424`): `(Au)(x)² ≤ A(u²)(x)`, Jensen at
one state, for a row that is a probability distribution.

GFNBounds.Core.funAct_eq_densAct_reversa.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A R : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R →
    ∀ (u : V → ℝ) {y : V}, lam y ≠ 0 → GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam R u y = GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u y
GFNBounds.Core.funAct_eq_densAct_reversa.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, the other half** (`proofs.tex:442`, "exchanging the roles of `T` and
`T^λ`, legitimate by `eq:reversal_flip`"): `d(μT^λ)/dλ = Tu`, `λ`-almost everywhere.

GFNBounds.Core.funAct_apply.type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (A : V → V → ℝ) (u : V → ℝ) (x : V), GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u x = ∑ y, A x y * u y

GFNBounds.Core.funAct.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.funAct.doc:
The **function action** `(Au)(x) = ∑_y A(x→y)u(y)` of a kernel on `L²(λ)` — the paper's `Af`
of `proofs.tex:422`, and `Graph.BackwardPolicy.qact` for `π̂_←`.

GFNBounds.Core.fmL1_le_holderConst_mul_l.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {e k : α → ℝ} {νT : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  {M : NNReal} {q : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    ∀ [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν],
      ν ≤ ↑M • νT →
        MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => e x - k x) (ENNReal.ofReal q) νT →
          ∫ (x : α), |e x - k x| ∂ν ≤ GFNBounds.Core.holderConst ν M q * GFNBounds.Core.stableLoss νT q e k
GFNBounds.Core.fmL1_le_holderConst_mul_l.doc:
**Step 3 in full** (`proofs.tex:234–239`): `Δ ≤ C₀ 𝓛`, the two Hölder applications composed.
The constant produced is `ν_B(𝒮)^{1−1/q} M^{1/q}`, which is `equ:stable_constants`' `C₀` on the
nose.

GFNBounds.Core.exists_outflow_memLp_of_t.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)} {θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν ⊤ →
      Pi θ = 0 →
        ∃ fout,
          0 ≤ fout ∧
            (∀ (r : ENNReal), MeasureTheory.MemLp (↑↑fout) r ν) ∧ ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, ↑↑(P fout) x = ↑↑fout x + ↑↑θ x
GFNBounds.Core.exists_outflow_memLp_of_t.doc:
**The transfer, in the form that assumes nothing at `r`.** The `p = +∞` construction produces
a non-negative outflow that lies in *every* `L^r(ν)` and satisfies the flow-matching constraint
as an a.e. identity of functions, `P f_out = f_out + θ`.

This is the whole mathematical content of `proofs.tex:114`'s last sentence. Nothing is said here
inside `defect`, and so nothing is needed about how — or whether — `P` acts on `L^r(ν)`.

GFNBounds.Core.eq_of_domination_zero.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {k e : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable k ν →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable e ν → (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, k x ≤ e x) → ∫ (x : α), e x ∂ν = ∫ (x : α), k x ∂ν → e =ᵐ[ν] k
GFNBounds.Core.eq_of_domination_zero.doc:
**The `ε = 0` case of `equ:il_domination` is `equ:FM_const`** (`proofs.tex:359–362`): a
non-negative defect `E − κ` between measures of equal total mass is zero. In densities: `k ≤ e`
`ν_B`-a.e. with equal integrals forces `e = k` `ν_B`-a.e.

GFNBounds.Core.eq_meanProj_of_invariant.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P (GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p) →
    ∀ {g : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
      P g = g → g = ((∫ (x : α), ↑↑g x ∂ν) / (ν Set.univ).toReal) • GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p
GFNBounds.Core.eq_meanProj_of_invariant.doc:
**Summable mixing against the mean projection is an ergodicity hypothesis.**

The paper's `Π` is the projection onto the invariant densities and coincides with the mean
projection because `π⋆` is ergodic. `meanProj` is the mean projection by construction, so nothing
above proves it projects onto `ker (Id − P)` — but nothing above needs to: as soon as
`n ↦ ‖P^n − Π‖` is summable with `Π` the *mean* projection, every `P`-invariant element of
`L^p(ν)` is its own mean, hence a multiple of `𝟏`. The ergodicity has moved into the summability
hypothesis rather than disappeared, which is what this file's SCOPE records.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_smul_nonneg.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] {r : ℝ},
  0 ≤ r →
    ∀ {f : α → ℝ},
      MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
        (GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν fun x => r * f x) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => r * GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f x
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_smul_nonneg.doc: `P⋆` is homogeneous under a non-negative scalar.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_smul.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] (r : ℝ) {f : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
    (GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν fun x => r * f x) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => r * GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f x
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_smul.doc: **`P⋆` is homogeneous**, `ν`-a.e., under every real scalar.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_one.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν → GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν 1 =ᵐ[ν] 1
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_one.doc:
**`hone`**: `P⋆ 𝟏 = 𝟏` a.e. This is pure invariance — `𝟏 ν = ν`, so `(𝟏 ν) π⋆ = ν` and its
`ν`-density is `𝟏`; the negative part is the zero density and contributes nothing.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_neg.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α)
  (f : α → ℝ), (GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν fun x => -f x) = fun x => -GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f x
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_neg.doc: `P⋆(-f) = -P⋆ f`, by definition: negation swaps the positive and negative parts.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_id.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] {f : α → ℝ},
  AEMeasurable f ν → GFNBounds.Core.densityAction ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.id ν f =ᵐ[ν] f
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_id.doc: The identity kernel has the identity density action.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_congr.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α)
  {f g : α → ℝ}, f =ᵐ[ν] g → GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f = GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν g
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_congr.doc:
`P⋆` depends on `f` only through its `ν`-a.e. class, and by *equality* of functions. This is
what lets it descend to `L^p(ν)`.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_add.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
    ∀ {f g : α → ℝ},
      MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable g ν →
          (GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν fun x => f x + g x) =ᵐ[ν] fun x =>
            GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν f x + GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν g x
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction_add.doc:
**`P⋆` is additive**, `ν`-a.e., on `ν`-integrable densities.

The proof is the pointwise identity `(u+v)⁺ + u⁻ + v⁻ = (u+v)⁻ + u⁺ + v⁺` of `ofReal_add_aux`,
pushed through `T` — which is additive by `bindDensity_add` — and read back in `ℝ` where every
term is finite. Subtraction in `ℝ≥0∞` is never performed.

GFNBounds.Core.densityActionLM.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) →
      [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] →
        (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
          [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] →
            (p : ENNReal) →
              [Fact (1 ≤ p)] →
                {C : ℝ} →
                  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
                    GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C →
                      ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →ₗ[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)
GFNBounds.Core.densityActionLM.doc:
`P⋆` as a linear map on `L^p(ν)`. Linearity is `densityAction_add` and `densityAction_smul`
read on the `L^p` quotient, which is where the two a.e. identities become equalities.

GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM_constOne.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (p : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C),
  (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p

GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) →
      [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] →
        (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
          [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] →
            (p : ENNReal) →
              [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] →
                {C : ℝ} →
                  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
                    GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C →
                      ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)
GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM.doc:
**`P⋆` as a `ContinuousLinearMap` on `L^p(ν)`**, with the paper's own operator-norm bound `C`
as the continuity constant.

GFNBounds.Core.densityAction.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α → MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ℝ) → α → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.densityAction.doc:
**The density action `P⋆ f := d((f ν) π⋆)/dν` on signed densities.** A signed density is
split into its positive and negative parts, each pushed by `T = bindDensity`, and the two
densities subtracted. Nothing here supposes `f` integrable or even measurable — the statements
that need it say so.

GFNBounds.Core.densAct_eq_funAct_reversa.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (lam : V → ℝ) (A : V → V → ℝ) (u : V → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u = GFNBounds.Core.funAct (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) u
GFNBounds.Core.densAct_eq_funAct_reversa.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(3)*, half of "the density action of each is the function action of the
other"** (`proofs.tex:407`): `d(μT)/dλ = T^λ u`. It holds at every state, no hypothesis at all,
both sides vanishing together where `λ` does.

GFNBounds.Core.densAct_apply.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (lam : V → ℝ) (A : V → V → ℝ) (u : V → ℝ) (y : V),
  GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u y = (∑ x, lam x * A x y * u x) / lam y

GFNBounds.Core.densAct.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.densAct.doc:
The **density action** `μ ↦ μA` of a kernel on `𝓜²(λ)`, read on densities:
`(d(μA)/dλ)(y) = (∑_x λ(x)A(x→y)u(x))/λ(y)` for `u = dμ/dλ`. This is
`Graph.BackwardPolicy.pdens` for `π̂_←`.

GFNBounds.Core.defect_inclTop_eq_zero.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {r : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ r)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)}
  {Q : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.CompatibleAcrossTop ν r P Q →
    ∀ {θ fout : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)},
      GFNBounds.Core.defect P θ fout = 0 →
        GFNBounds.Core.defect Q (GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r θ) (GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r fout) = 0
GFNBounds.Core.defect_inclTop_eq_zero.doc: An exactly flow-matching outflow at `p = +∞` is exactly flow-matching at `r`.

GFNBounds.Core.defect_eq_truncation.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] [inst_3 : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} {one θ : E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    P one = one →
      Pi θ = 0 →
        ∀ (η : ℝ),
          GFNBounds.Core.defect P θ (GFNBounds.Core.liftedOutflow P Pi one θ η) =
            P (GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi one θ η) - GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi one θ η
GFNBounds.Core.defect_eq_truncation.doc:
**`equ:defect_is_truncation`** — the exact part cancels and only the truncation survives:
`D = (P - 1) ψ_η`.

The hypotheses are exactly the two the appendix uses: `P` fixes the constants (`P 1 = 1`,
from `ν_B π* = ν_B`) so that `η • 1` is a `0`-flow, and `Π θ = 0` (equal masses) so that the
Poisson equation solves exactly.

GFNBounds.Core.defect.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → E → E
GFNBounds.Core.defect.doc:
The **flow-matching defect** of an outflow `fout` against the pair `(f_init, f_term)`,
written as its density: `D = (P - 1) fout - θ` with `θ = f_term - f_init`
(`theo:universality_L2_full`, `proofs.tex:78`).

GFNBounds.Core.constOne.congr_simp.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (p : ENNReal)
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν], GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p

GFNBounds.Core.constOne.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) → (p : ENNReal) → [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)
GFNBounds.Core.constOne.doc:
The constant `𝟏` of `L^p(ν)`. It is an element of `L^p` because `ν` is finite, which is
the appendix's own reason (`proofs.tex:100`); on `L^p(ν_B)` it is the `𝟏` whose `0`-flow
property `(Id - P⋆) 𝟏 = 0` supplies the freedom in Step 2.

GFNBounds.Core.compatibleAcrossTop_densi.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (r : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ r)] {C C' : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν ⊤ C) (hb' : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν r C'),
  GFNBounds.Core.CompatibleAcrossTop ν r (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν ⊤ hinv hb)
    (GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν r hinv hb')
GFNBounds.Core.compatibleAcrossTop_densi.doc:
**The compatibility, discharged for a Markov kernel.** `densityAction κ ν` is a map on
functions `α → ℝ` and knows nothing about `p`; `coeFn_densityActionCLM` says the operator at
either exponent is represented by it, and `densityAction_congr` says it only sees the a.e. class.
The two continuous linear maps are therefore induced by one function-level map, which is exactly
what `CompatibleAcrossTop` asks.

GFNBounds.Core.comp_meanProj.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)},
  P (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) = GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p →
    P * GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p = GFNBounds.Core.meanProj ν p
GFNBounds.Core.comp_meanProj.doc:
**`Mixing.proj_right`, derived**: `P Π = Π`, from `P 𝟏 = 𝟏` and linearity.

The paper's `P⋆ Π = Π` (`proofs.tex:87`): `Π` lands in the constants, and invariance of `ν_B`
fixes the constants — "the constants are `0`-flows" (`proofs.tex:100`).

GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_truncation.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] (P Pi : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν))
  (θ : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)) (η : ℝ),
  ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.truncation P Pi (GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) θ η) =ᵐ[ν] fun x =>
    max (↑↑((GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) θ) x - η) 0
GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_truncation.doc:
The pointwise form of the truncation `ψ_η = (η • 𝟏 - Sθ)⁻`: its a.e. representative is
`x ↦ max (Sθ x - η, 0)`, which is the appendix's `(Sθ - η)⁺`.

GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_inclTop.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (r : ENNReal) (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)), ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r f) =ᵐ[ν] ↑↑f

GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_densityActionCLM.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [inst_1 : ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  (p : ENNReal) [inst_3 : Fact (1 ≤ p)] {C : ℝ} (hinv : ν.bind ⇑κ = ν)
  (hb : GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction κ ν p C) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
  ↑↑((GFNBounds.Core.densityActionCLM κ ν p hinv hb) F) =ᵐ[ν] GFNBounds.Core.densityAction κ ν ↑↑F
GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_densityActionCLM.doc: The `L^p` operator applied to `F` is represented by `P⋆` applied to any representative.

GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_defect_inclTop.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {r : ENNReal} [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ r)] {P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)}
  {Q : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν)},
  GFNBounds.Core.CompatibleAcrossTop ν r P Q →
    ∀ (θ fout : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)),
      ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.defect Q (GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r θ) (GFNBounds.Core.inclTop ν r fout)) =ᵐ[ν]
        ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.defect P θ fout)
GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_defect_inclTop.doc:
The two defects are the same function: `D` at `r` computed on the included data agrees a.e.
with `D` at `⊤`.

GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_defect.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {p : ENNReal} [inst_1 : Fact (1 ≤ p)]
  (P : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)) (θ fout : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ p ν)),
  ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.defect P θ fout) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => ↑↑(P fout) x - ↑↑fout x - ↑↑θ x
GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_defect.doc: The defect, read pointwise: `D = P f_out − f_out − θ` a.e.

GFNBounds.Core.coeFn_constOne.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]
  {p : ENNReal}, ↑↑(GFNBounds.Core.constOne ν p) =ᵐ[ν] fun x => 1

GFNBounds.Core.bind_withDensity_univ.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f : α → ENNReal), ((ν.withDensity f).bind ⇑κ) Set.univ = ∫⁻ (x : α), f x ∂ν
GFNBounds.Core.bind_withDensity_univ.doc:
**The mass of `(f ν) π⋆` is the mass of `f ν`** — stochasticity of the kernel, and not
invariance of the measure.

GFNBounds.Core.bind_withDensity_absolute.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α},
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν → ∀ (f : α → ENNReal), ((ν.withDensity f).bind ⇑κ).AbsolutelyContinuous ν
GFNBounds.Core.bind_withDensity_absolute.doc:
**`(f ν) π⋆ ≪ ν`, from invariance alone.** This is the main text's "invariance makes the
density action `P⋆ f := d((f ν_B) π⋆)/dν_B` well defined on `L¹(ν_B)`"
(`universality.tex:26–27`), and it is a theorem, not a hypothesis.

GFNBounds.Core.bind_id.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α), ν.bind ⇑ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.id = ν
GFNBounds.Core.bind_id.doc: Every measure is invariant under the identity kernel.

GFNBounds.Core.bind_add_measure.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (μ₁ μ₂ : MeasureTheory.Measure α),
  (μ₁ + μ₂).bind ⇑κ = μ₁.bind ⇑κ + μ₂.bind ⇑κ
GFNBounds.Core.bind_add_measure.doc: `bind` is additive in the measure: `(μ₁ + μ₂) π⋆ = μ₁ π⋆ + μ₂ π⋆`.

GFNBounds.Core.bind_absolutelyContinuous.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) {μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α},
  μ.AbsolutelyContinuous ν → (μ.bind ⇑κ).AbsolutelyContinuous (ν.bind ⇑κ)
GFNBounds.Core.bind_absolutelyContinuous.doc:
**A kernel push preserves domination**: `μ ≪ ν` implies `μ π⋆ ≪ ν π⋆`.

Mathlib has no lemma of this shape at `v4.31.0`, and it is the whole of what makes the density
action well defined. Nothing is asked of the kernel beyond measurability.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_zero.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α),
  GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν 0 =ᵐ[ν] 0
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_zero.doc: `T 0 = 0`: the zero density pushes to the zero measure.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_smul.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] {c : ENNReal},
  c ≠ ⊤ →
    ∀ {f : α → ENNReal},
      AEMeasurable f ν →
        ∫⁻ (x : α), f x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ → GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν (c • f) =ᵐ[ν] c • GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν f
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_smul.doc: **`T` is positively homogeneous**, `ν`-a.e., for a finite scalar.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_one.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν], ν.bind ⇑κ = ν → GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν 1 =ᵐ[ν] 1
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_one.doc:
**`T 𝟏 = 𝟏`** — the non-negative half of `hone`, and pure invariance: `𝟏 ν = ν`, so
`(𝟏 ν) π⋆ = ν π⋆ = ν` and `dν/dν = 𝟏`.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_ofReal_lt_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν],
  ν.bind ⇑κ = ν →
    ∀ {f : α → ℝ},
      MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν → ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) x < ⊤
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_ofReal_lt_top.doc: `T f⁺` has finite `ν`-integral, hence is a.e. finite.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_id.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν]
  {f : α → ENNReal}, AEMeasurable f ν → GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.id ν f =ᵐ[ν] f
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_id.doc: The identity kernel has the identity density action on non-negative densities.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_congr.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α)
  {f g : α → ENNReal}, f =ᵐ[ν] g → GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν f = GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν g
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_congr.doc:
`T` depends on `f` only through its `ν`-a.e. class, and the dependence is by *equality* of
functions, not merely a.e. equality: `ν.withDensity` already forgets the null sets. This is what
makes `T` descend to `L^p(ν)` without a quotient argument.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_add₃.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] {u v w : α → ENNReal},
  AEMeasurable u ν →
    AEMeasurable v ν →
      ∫⁻ (x : α), u x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ →
        ∫⁻ (x : α), v x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ →
          ∫⁻ (x : α), w x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ →
            GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν (u + v + w) =ᵐ[ν]
              GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν u + GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν v + GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν w
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_add₃.doc: `T` on a sum of three densities of finite integral.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_add.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν] {f g : α → ENNReal},
  AEMeasurable f ν →
    ∫⁻ (x : α), f x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ →
      ∫⁻ (x : α), g x ∂ν ≠ ⊤ →
        GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν (f + g) =ᵐ[ν] GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν f + GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity κ ν g
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity_add.doc: **`T` is additive**, `ν`-a.e., on densities of finite integral.

GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α → MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ENNReal) → α → ENNReal
GFNBounds.Core.bindDensity.doc:
**The density action `T f := d((f ν) π⋆)/dν`** of the main text (`universality.tex:26–27`),
on non-negative densities. It is well defined — that is, `(T f) ν = (f ν) π⋆` — as soon as `ν`
is `π⋆`-invariant; that is `withDensity_bindDensity`.

GFNBounds.Core.aemeasurable_ofReal.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {f : α → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν → AEMeasurable (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (f y)) ν
GFNBounds.Core.aemeasurable_ofReal.doc: The positive part of an integrable function is `ν`-a.e. measurable as an `ℝ≥0∞` density.

GFNBounds.Core.ae_le_norm_top.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α} (g : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)),
  ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂ν, ↑↑g x ≤ ‖g‖
GFNBounds.Core.ae_le_norm_top.doc:
**`g ≤ ‖g‖` a.e., on `L^∞(ν)`.** The essential supremum dominates a.e., and on `L^∞` it is
finite, so the `ℝ≥0∞` inequality `‖g x‖ₑ ≤ eLpNormEssSup g ν` may be read in `ℝ`.

This is the analytic content of `theo:universality_L2_full`'s "taking `η := ‖Sθ‖_{L^∞(ν_B)}`"
(`proofs.tex:73`): the choice is legitimate because the norm really does dominate the
function.

GFNBounds.Core.adjoint_finite.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkov A →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam A →
      (∃ x, 0 < lam x) →
        (GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) ∧
            GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A)) ∧
          (∀ (R : V → V → ℝ),
              GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R →
                ∀ (x : V), lam x ≠ 0 → ∀ (y : V), R x y = GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A x y) ∧
            (GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) ∧
                GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) A ∧
                  ∀ (x : V),
                    lam x ≠ 0 → ∀ (y : V), GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) x y = A x y) ∧
              (∀ (u v : V → ℝ),
                  GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u) v =
                    GFNBounds.Graph.ipL2 lam u (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) v)) ∧
                (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A = GFNBounds.Core.funAct (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) ∧
                    ∀ (u : V → ℝ) (x : V),
                      lam x ≠ 0 →
                        GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam (GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A) u x = GFNBounds.Core.funAct A u x) ∧
                  IsLeast
                    {c |
                      ∀ (u : V → ℝ),
                        GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam A u) ≤ c * GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam u}
                    1
GFNBounds.Core.adjoint_finite.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(1)*–*(3)* on a finite state space** (`proofs.tex:402–410`), with the
paper's `λ`-almost-everywhere qualifications read as "at every state carrying `λ`-mass".

The Polish hypothesis is **restricted to a `Fintype`**; see the module SCOPE. Item *(4)* is the
graph section below, together with `theo:universality_graphs`*(2)*.

GFNBounds.Core.abs_sub_posPart_le.type: ∀ {x y : ℝ}, 0 ≤ y → |y - max x 0| ≤ |x - y|
GFNBounds.Core.abs_sub_posPart_le.doc:
**Step 1's second pointwise inequality** (`proofs.tex:204`): `x ↦ x⁺` is `1`-Lipschitz and
`k⁺ = k`, so `|e⁺ − k| ≤ |e − k|`.

GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt.doc:
**Weak `L^p`-universality** of `def:universality`, for the family `Θ = {P} × E⁺` that
`theo:universality_L2_full` is about: the two residuals can be driven to `0` together by a
non-negative outflow.

GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversal.type:
{E : Type u_1} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversal.doc:
**`def:universality`**, weak form, with its quantifier closed: the family `Θ = {P} × E⁺`
is weakly `L^p`-universal when *every* admissible pair is reachable.

`Pi θ = 0` is the paper's "distributions of equal total mass" — the defect integrates to
`F_init(𝒮) − F_term(𝒮)`, so unequal masses floor the infimum away from `0`
(`universality.tex:10–14`), and `Pi` is the mean projection, so `Pi θ = 0` says exactly that
the masses agree.

GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt.weakl.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [HasSolidNorm E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E]
  [inst_4 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P : E →L[ℝ] E} {θ : E},
  GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt P θ → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversalAt P θ

GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversalAt.doc:
**Strong universality**: the infimum is realized — some non-negative outflow makes the
flow-matching constraint hold exactly.

GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversal.weaklyU.type:
∀ {E : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Lattice E] [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] [HasSolidNorm E]
  [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E}, GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversal P Pi → GFNBounds.Core.WeaklyUniversal P Pi

GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversal.type:
{E : Type u_2} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [Lattice E] → [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.StronglyUniversal.doc:
**`def:universality`, strong form, with its pair quantifier closed**: the family
`Θ = {P} × E⁺` is strongly universal when *every* admissible pair is realized exactly — not
merely approached. This is `WeaklyUniversal`'s twin in `Core/Universality.lean`, with
`WeaklyUniversalAt` replaced by `StronglyUniversalAt`.

As there, `Pi θ = 0` is the paper's "distributions of equal total mass".

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.tendsto_pow.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => P ^ n) Filter.atTop (nhds Pi)
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.tendsto_pow.doc:
Summable mixing forces `P ^ n → Pi` in operator norm — the appendix's
`‖P^{N+1} - Π‖ = β_{N+1} → 0`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.tendsto_partialSum.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    Filter.Tendsto (GFNBounds.Doubling.partialSum P Pi) Filter.atTop (nhds (GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi))
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.tendsto_partialSum.doc:
`S` is the limit of `GFNBounds.Doubling.partialSum`, which is the hypothesis every result
of `Doubling/Operator.lean` consumes.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.summable_terms.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Summable fun n => P ^ n - Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.summable_terms.doc: The family `n ↦ P ^ n - Pi` is summable: absolutely so, by hypothesis.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.summable_beta.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Summable (GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.beta P Pi)

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.summable.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - Pi‖
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.summable.doc: Summable mixing: `∑ β n < ∞` with `β n = ‖P ^ n - Pi‖`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.recOn.type:
{E : Type u_1} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] →
    [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] →
      {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} →
        {motive : GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Sort u} →
          (t : GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi) →
            ((proj_left : Pi * P = Pi) →
                (proj_right : P * Pi = Pi) → (summable : Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - Pi‖) → motive ⋯) →
              motive t

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.rec.type:
{E : Type u_1} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] →
    [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] →
      {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} →
        {motive : GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Sort u} →
          ((proj_left : Pi * P = Pi) →
              (proj_right : P * Pi = Pi) → (summable : Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - Pi‖) → motive ⋯) →
            (t : GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi) → motive t

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.proj_right.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → P * Pi = Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.proj_right.doc: `P Pi = Pi`: the invariant vectors are fixed by `P`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.proj_left.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E},
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Pi * P = Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.proj_left.doc: `Pi P = Pi`: the projection kills whatever one step of `P` changes.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.proj_idem.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Pi * Pi = Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.proj_idem.doc:
`Pi` is idempotent: `P ^ n → Pi` while `P ^ (n+1) Pi = Pi` throughout. Needed to feed
`resolvent_identities`, which carries idempotence as a hypothesis.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_solved.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → ∀ {θ : E}, Pi θ = 0 → (1 - P) ((GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) θ) = θ
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_solved.doc:
**The Poisson equation solves exactly on mean-zero data**, the form Step 2 consumes: if
`Pi θ = 0` then `(1 - P) (S θ) = θ`. The appendix's `equ:poisson_solved`
(`proofs.tex:96–98`).

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_right_appl.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → ∀ (θ : E), (GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) ((1 - P) θ) = θ - Pi θ
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_right_appl.doc: The Poisson equation, applied: `S ((1 - P) θ) = θ - Pi θ`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_right.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi * (1 - P) = 1 - Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_right.doc:
**The Poisson equation, right form**: `S (1 - P) = 1 - Pi`. This is `equ:poisson` of
`theo:universality_L2_full` and the `S(I-P) = I - Π` of `lem:sigma_mixing`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_left_apply.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → ∀ (θ : E), (1 - P) ((GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) θ) = θ - Pi θ
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_left_apply.doc: The Poisson equation, applied on the other side: `(1 - P) (S θ) = θ - Pi θ`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_left.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → (1 - P) * GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi = 1 - Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.poisson_left.doc: **The Poisson equation, left form**: `(1 - P) S = 1 - Pi`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.norm_S_le.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → ‖GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi‖ ≤ GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B P Pi
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.norm_S_le.doc:
`‖S‖ ≤ B`: the operator-norm bound behind `theo:universality_L2_full`'s
`‖Sθ‖ ≤ B_p ‖θ‖`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.norm_S_apply_le.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → ∀ (θ : E), ‖(GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S P Pi) θ‖ ≤ GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B P Pi * ‖θ‖
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.norm_S_apply_le.doc: `‖S θ‖ ≤ B ‖θ‖`, which is how `theo:universality_L2_full` states the bound.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.mk.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E},
  Pi * P = Pi → P * Pi = Pi → (Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - Pi‖) → GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.coercivity_div.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi →
    0 < GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B P Pi → ∀ (x : E), ‖x - Pi x‖ / GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B P Pi ≤ ‖(1 - P) x‖
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.coercivity_div.doc:
The quotient form of `lem:sigma_mixing`'s display. The hypothesis `0 < B` is free in the
paper, where `β̂_0 = 1` forces `B̂ ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.coercivity.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} [CompleteSpace E],
  GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → ∀ (x : E), ‖x - Pi x‖ ≤ GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B P Pi * ‖(1 - P) x‖
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.coercivity.doc:
**Mixing controls coercivity** — the "consequently" of `lem:sigma_mixing`, and the only
part of it the paper's downstream consumers use (`proofs.tex:872`).

Stated as a product rather than a quotient so that it says something at `B = 0` too: there
`Pi = P ^ 0 = 1` and `P = 1`, both sides are `0`, and the claim is true if contentless. In the
paper's normalization `β̂_0 = ‖I - Π‖ = 1`, so `B̂ ≥ 1` and that corner never arises.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.casesOn.type:
{E : Type u_1} →
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] →
    [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] →
      {P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E} →
        {motive : GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi → Sort u} →
          (t : GFNBounds.Core.Mixing P Pi) →
            ((proj_left : Pi * P = Pi) →
                (proj_right : P * Pi = Pi) → (summable : Summable fun n => ‖P ^ n - Pi‖) → motive ⋯) →
              motive t

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.beta_nonneg.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E) (n : ℕ),
  0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.beta P Pi n

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.beta.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → ℕ → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.beta.doc: The mixing coefficients `β_n = ‖P ^ n - Pi‖` of `equ:mixing_coefficients`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.S.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → E →L[ℝ] E

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B_nonneg.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] (P Pi : E →L[ℝ] E),
  0 ≤ GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B P Pi

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.B.doc:
The mixing sum `B = ∑_{n ≥ 0} β_n` of `equ:mixing_coefficients`; the appendix writes it
`B̂` at `p = 2`.

GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (E →L[ℝ] E) → (E →L[ℝ] E) → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.Mixing.doc:
The hypothesis shared by `lem:sigma_mixing` and Step 1 of `theo:universality_L2_full`:
a bounded operator `P` and a projection `Pi` onto its invariant vectors, whose mixing
coefficients `n ↦ ‖P ^ n - Pi‖` are summable.

`proj_left` and `proj_right` are the paper's `Π P_⋆ = P_⋆ Π = Π`, which on `L^p(ν_B)` hold
because the density action preserves `ν_B`-integrals and fixes the constants.

GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.symm.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {lam : V → ℝ} {A R : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R → GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam R A
GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.symm.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(2)*, the flip identity `eq:reversal_flip`** (`proofs.tex:418`):
`T^λ ⊗ λ = λ ⊗ T`. On a finite space it is the symmetry of the characterizing identity, obtained
by reading it at `(y,x)` instead of `(x,y)`.

GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.isInvarian.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A R : V → V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ lam x) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkov A → GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R → GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam R
GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.isInvarian.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(2)*, `λ` is `T^λ`-invariant** (`proofs.tex:416`): `λT^λ` is the second
marginal of `λ ⊗ T^λ = T ⊗ λ`, which is `λ`. It needs only that `A` is row-stochastic — not that
`λ` is `A`-invariant.

GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.eq_reversa.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {lam : V → ℝ} {A R : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R → ∀ {x : V}, lam x ≠ 0 → ∀ (y : V), R x y = GFNBounds.Core.reversal lam A x y
GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.eq_reversa.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(1)*, `λ`-a.e. uniqueness** (`proofs.tex:405`, "unique up to a
`λ`-negligible set"): any solution of the characterizing identity is the reversal at every state
carrying `λ`-mass.

GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.eq_of_ne_z.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {lam : V → ℝ} {A R R' : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair lam A R' → ∀ {x : V}, lam x ≠ 0 → ∀ (y : V), R x y = R' x y

GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.type: {V : Type u_1} → (V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.IsReversalPair.doc:
**`lem:adjoint`*(1)*, the characterizing identity** `λ ⊗ R = A ⊗ λ` (`proofs.tex:405`), read
entrywise on a finite space: `(λ ⊗ R)(x,y) = λ(x)R(x→y)` and `(A ⊗ λ)(x,y) = A(y→x)λ(y)`
(`proofs.tex:412`).

The relation is **symmetric in `A` and `R`** — swapping the two arguments of the identity swaps
the roles of the kernels — and that symmetry *is* item *(2)*'s flip identity `eq:reversal_flip`;
see `IsReversalPair.symm`.

GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn.toIsMarkov.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam A → (∀ (x : V), 0 < lam x) → GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkov A

GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn.row_sum.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {A : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn lam A → ∀ ⦃x : V⦄, lam x ≠ 0 → ∑ y, A x y = 1
GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn.row_sum.doc: `T(x → ·)` is a probability distribution at every `x` carrying `λ`-mass.

GFNBounds.Core.IsMarkovOn.doc:
A **`λ`-almost-everywhere Markov kernel**: non-negative, with the row at `x` summing to `1`
whenever `λ(x) ≠ 0`. This is what the `λ`-reversal is in general — where `λ` vanishes its row is
the zero row — and it is the honest reading of the paper's "`λ`-almost everywhere unique Markov
kernel" (`proofs.tex:405`).

{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] → ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α → MeasureTheory.Measure α → ENNReal → ℝ → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.IsBoundedDensityAction.doc:
**The paper's boundedness hypothesis on the parameterization**, and the only hypothesis of
`theo:universality_L2_full` that this file assumes rather than derives.

`theo:universality_L2_full` asks for "a Markov kernel on `𝒮` with finite
`L^p(ν_B) → L^p(ν_B)` operator norm", and the main text is explicit that this is a requirement on
the parameterization and not a theorem: "boundedness of `‖π⋆‖_{L^p(ν_B)}` […] is not automatic"
(`universality.tex:6–9`), "the definitions above do not guarantee that `‖π⋆‖_{L^p(ν_B)}` is
finite" (`proofs.tex:36`). The two fields are the two halves of "`P⋆` is a bounded operator of
`L^p(ν_B)`": that it maps `L^p` into `L^p`, and that it does so with a bound. `C` is the operator
norm bound, carried explicitly rather than as `∃ C`.

{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : MeasurableSpace α] →
    (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) →
      [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] →
        (r : ENNReal) →
          [inst_2 : Fact (1 ≤ r)] →
            (↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ ⊤ ν)) →
              (↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ r ν)) → Prop
GFNBounds.Core.CompatibleAcrossTop.doc:
**The compatibility an operator-level transfer consumes**: `Q` on `L^r(ν)` and `P` on
`L^∞(ν)` agree a.e. on the image of the inclusion.

It is a genuine hypothesis, not a triviality — a bounded operator on `L^r(ν)` is not determined
by one on `L^∞(ν)`, and neither space's operator is canonically the other's restriction.
`compatibleAcrossTop_densityActionCLM` discharges it for the density action of a Markov kernel,
where both operators are induced by the single function-level map `densityAction κ ν`.

GFNBounds.Balance.twoState_ratioBridge_c.type:
GFNBounds.Balance.Aop GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateK GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU 0 =
    -(1 / 2) ∧
  GFNBounds.Balance.Aop GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateK GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU 1 =
      1 / 2 ∧
    GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU = 3 / 2 ∧
      GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU = √(5 / 2) ∧
        (GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam fun x =>
              GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU x /
                  GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU -
                1) =
            0 ∧
          (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam fun x =>
                GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU x /
                    GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU -
                  1) =
              1 / 3 ∧
            (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam fun x =>
                  GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU x /
                      GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU -
                    1) ≤
                1 * (1 / 2) * GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateLam GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateU /

GFNBounds.Balance.twoState_hasDerivAt_lo.doc:
**The theorem, evaluated.** On `T(i→j) = 1/2`, `λ = (1/2,1/2)`, `μ* = (1,1/2)` — i.e.

Independently: `r_t = ((3+t)/(2(2+t)), (3+t)/2)`, so `ṙ = (−1/8, 1/2)` and

**`cor:gradient_formulas` evaluated for `g(x) = |x−1|`.** The same chain and the same
direction: `r = (3/4, 3/2)`, nowhere `1`, so `hasDerivAt_fmLoss_abs_ipL2` applies and

By hand off the paper's display: `π_→^λ[ε(r)λ]` has `λ`-density `π_← ε(r) ≡ (1/2)(−1) + (1/2)(1)
= 0`, so `(π_→^λ − r)[ε(r)λ]` has density `(0 + 3/4, 0 − 3/2) = (3/4, −3/2)` and
`⟨∇ ∣ δ⟩_λ = (1/2)(3/4)(1) + (1/2)(−3/2)(0) = 3/8`. From the loss:
`𝓛 = ν(0)|r_t(0)−1| + ν(1)|r_t(1)−1| = (1−r_t(0)) + (1/2)(r_t(1)−1)` near `t = 0`, whose

GFNBounds.Balance.twoState_hasDerivAt_fm.doc:
**`cor:gradient_formulas` evaluated.** On `π_←(i→j) = 1/2`, `λ = (1/2,1/2)`, `F_← = (1,1/2)`
— i.e. `u = (2,1)`, and `ν = F_←`, so `dν/dμ ≡ 1` — with `g(x) = (x−1)²`, the derivative of
`t ↦ 𝓛_{g,F_←}(F_← + tδ)` along `δ = (1,0)·λ` is `5/16`.

Computed by hand off the paper's display, twice, without the library.

*From the loss.* `r_t = ((3+t)/(2(2+t)), (3+t)/2)`, so `r = (3/4, 3/2)` and `ṙ = (−1/8, 1/2)`;
`𝓛̇ = ∑ ν(x) g'(r(x)) ṙ(x) = 1·2(3/4−1)(−1/8) + (1/2)·2(3/2−1)(1/2) = 1/16 + 1/4 = 5/16`.

*From the gradient.* `π_→^λ(rλ)` has `λ`-density `π_← r ≡ (1/2)(3/4) + (1/2)(3/2) = 9/8`, so the
second display gives `2(9/8 − 1 − r² + r)`, i.e. `5/8` at state `0` and `−5/4` at state `1`; then
`⟨∇ ∣ δ⟩_λ = (1/2)(5/8)(1) + (1/2)(−5/4)(0) = 5/16`. The two agree.

**`cor:db_gradient` evaluated.** On `π_←(i→j) = 1/2` and `λ = (1/2,1/2)`, so that
`λ₂ ≡ 1/4` and `π_→^λ = π_←`, take the edge flow `μ = u·λ₂` with `u` as in `twoStateEdgeU` —
`μ = (1/4, 3/4, 1/2, 1)` — and `ν̂ = μ`, so `dν̂/dμ ≡ 1`. For `g(x) = (x−1)²`, the derivative of
`t ↦ 𝓛_{DB,g,ν̂}(μ + tδ)` along `δ = 1·λ₂` is `−17/32`.

Computed by hand off the paper's display, twice, without the library.

*From the loss.* `F_t = m₁μ_t = (1 + t/2, 3/2 + t/2)` and `(μ_tK₂)(z,w) = π_←(w→z)F_t(w)`, so
`r̂_t = ((2+t)/(1+t), 1, 1, (3+t)/(4+t))`; at `t = 0`, `r̂ = (2, 1, 1, 3/4)` and
`ṙ̂ = (−1, 0, 0, 1/16)`. Hence
`𝓛̇ = ∑ ν̂ g'(r̂) ṙ̂ = (1/4)·2(2−1)·(−1) + 1·2(3/4−1)·(1/16) = −1/2 − 1/32 = −17/32`.

*From the gradient.* `φ = g'(r̂) = (2, 0, 0, −1/2)`, and `[φλ₂]K₂^{λ₂}` has `λ₂`-density
`(s,s') ↦ ∑_z π_←(s→z)φ(z,s)`, which is `1` at `s = 0` and `−1/4` at `s = 1`. So
`(K₂^{λ₂} − r̂)[φλ₂]` has `λ₂`-density `(1 − 2·2, 1 − 0, −1/4 − 0, −1/4 + 3/8)
= (−3, 1, −1/4, 1/8)`, and `⟨∇ ∣ δ⟩_{λ₂} = (1/4)(−3 + 1 − 1/4 + 1/8) = −17/32`. The two agree,
which fixes the sign and the normalization of the DB formula against something outside the
derivation.

The Lean proof applies `hasDerivAt_dbLoss_ipL2` itself, at `π_→^λ = π_←` (which `hpf` verifies on
this chain), so what is evaluated is the paper's `K₂^{λ₂}` — `dualEdgeKernelProd`, the forward
edge kernel of `lem:lift_wellposed` — and not the function action of `K₂`. That the two give the
same number here is `lem:lift_wellposed`'s duality, used rather than assumed.

GFNBounds.Balance.twoStateEdgeU.doc:
The `λ₂`-density of the edge flow used by `twoStateEdge_hasDerivAt_dbLoss`:
`u(0,0) = 1`, `u(0,1) = 3`, `u(1,0) = 2`, `u(1,1) = 4`.

  {B : GFNBounds.Graph.BackwardPolicy G} {lam gr uH wf : V → ℝ} {wmin wsup : ℝ} {u : ℝ → V → ℝ},
  G.PathConnected →
    B.PositiveOnEdges →
      B.IsInvProb lam →
        B.IsGreen gr →
          B.IsHitExp uH →
            0 < wmin →

                (∀ (x : V), wf x ≤ wsup) →
                  (∀ (t : ℝ) (x : V), 0 < u t x) →
                    GFNBounds.Balance.IsGradientFlow B.phat lam (fun x => lam x * wf x) GFNBounds.Balance.logSqDeriv u →
                      (∀ (x : V), lam x = GFNBounds.Graph.visits G gr x / (2 + B.sigmaBar uH)) ∧
                        GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam =

                          (∀ (t : ℝ),

                                    (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio B.phat lam (u t)) ≤
                                  ((GFNBounds.Balance.lossVal lam wf GFNBounds.Balance.logSq
                                          (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio B.phat lam (u 0)))⁻¹ +
                                      (wmin * √(GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam) /
                                            (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (u 0) * wsup *
                                              max 1
                                                √(GFNBounds.Balance.lossVal lam wf GFNBounds.Balance.logSq
                                                      (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio B.phat lam (u 0)) /
                                                    (wmin * GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam)))) ^
                                          2 *
                                        t)⁻¹) ∧
                            ∃
                              t₁ ∈
                                Set.Icc 0
                                  (GFNBounds.Balance.T0
                                    (GFNBounds.Balance.lossVal lam wf GFNBounds.Balance.logSq
                                      (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio B.phat lam (u 0)))
                                    (GFNBounds.Balance.cDelta wmin (GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam)
                                      (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (u 0))
                                      (GFNBounds.Balance.delta0
                                        (GFNBounds.Balance.eps0Sq wmin wsup (GFNBounds.Balance.BhatSigma G uH lam)
                                          (GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam))
                                        (GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u 0)) (GFNBounds.Balance.BhatSigma G uH lam)
                                        (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (u 0))))),
                              GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u 0) ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u t₁) ∧
                                GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u t₁) ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (u 0) ∧
                                  (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam fun x => u t₁ x / GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u t₁) - 1) ≤
                                      GFNBounds.Balance.eps0Sq wmin wsup (GFNBounds.Balance.BhatSigma G uH lam)
                                        (GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam) ∧
                                    ∃ cinf,
                                      (GFNBounds.Balance.Balanced B.phat lam fun x => cinf) ∧
                                        ∀ (t : ℝ),
                                          t₁ ≤ t →
                                            (GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam fun x =>
                                                u t x / GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u t₁) - cinf) ≤
                                              2 *
                                                  Real.exp
                                                    (-(GFNBounds.Balance.rhoSigma 2 wmin (GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam)
                                                            (GFNBounds.Graph.sigmaStar G uH) *
                                                          (t - t₁) /
                                                        (2 * GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (u t₁) ^ 2))) *
                                                GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam

It vanishes exactly at `r = 1` (`proofs.tex:805`), where `λ > 0` and `dν/dμ > 0` are what

GFNBounds.Balance.tendsto_atTop_of_monot.type:
∀ {f : ℝ → ℝ} {C : ℝ},
  MonotoneOn f (Set.Ici 0) → (∀ (τ : ℝ), 0 ≤ τ → f τ ≤ C) → ∃ l, Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop (nhds l)
GFNBounds.Balance.tendsto_atTop_of_monot.doc:
A function that is monotone on `[0,∞)` and bounded above there converges at `+∞`.
`Mathlib.tendsto_atTop_ciSup` wants **global** monotonicity; `τ ↦ f(max 0 τ)` supplies it and
agrees with `f` eventually.

GFNBounds.Balance.tendsto_atTop_of_deriv.type:
∀ {A B b beta : ℝ → ℝ} {CA CB : ℝ},
  (∀ (τ : ℝ), HasDerivAt A (b τ) τ) →
    (∀ (τ : ℝ), HasDerivAt B (beta τ) τ) →
      (∀ (τ : ℝ), 0 ≤ τ → |beta τ| ≤ b τ) →
        (∀ (τ : ℝ), 0 ≤ τ → A τ ≤ CA) → (∀ (τ : ℝ), 0 ≤ τ → |B τ| ≤ CB) → ∃ l, Filter.Tendsto B Filter.atTop (nhds l)
GFNBounds.Balance.tendsto_atTop_of_deriv.doc:
**The shape of Step 3's convergence argument, with the flow removed.** `A` grows, `B` drifts
no faster than `A` grows, both are bounded on `[0,∞)`: then `B` converges at `+∞`, because
`A ± B` are monotone and bounded and `B = ((A+B) − (A−B))/2`.
