GFNBounds.Balance.balanced_const.doc:
**A constant density is balanced**, on any kernel with an invariant `λ`: `μ = cλ` and
`λK = λ` give `μK = μ`. One half of "the unique maximizer is the balanced flow".

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam w h : V → ℝ} {gd : ℝ → ℝ} {g2 a M3 wsup eps : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
      0 ≤ g2 →
        0 ≤ M3 →
          0 ≤ a →
            0 ≤ wsup →
              (∀ (x : V), |w x| ≤ wsup) →
                (∀ (y : ℝ), |y - 1| ≤ a → |gd y - g2 * (y - 1)| ≤ M3 / 2 * (y - 1) ^ 2) →
                  (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
                    0 ≤ eps →
                      eps ≤ min a 1 / 4 →
                        ∀ {y : V},
                          lam y ≠ 0 →
                            |(GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y - 1) *
                                  (gd (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y) * (w y / (1 + h y)))| ≤
                              GFNBounds.Balance.C6 (GFNBounds.Balance.Cg g2 a M3) wsup *
                                GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam h) y ^ 2
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_.doc:
**`|(r−1)φ| ≤ C₆(Ah^⊥)²` with the paper's `C₆ = 4C_g‖w‖_{L^∞}`** (`proofs.tex:641`), the
same estimate with the printed constant.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam w h : V → ℝ} {gd : ℝ → ℝ} {g2 a M3 wsup eps : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
      0 ≤ g2 →
        0 ≤ M3 →
          (∀ (x : V), |w x| ≤ wsup) →
            (∀ (y : ℝ), |y - 1| ≤ a → |gd y - g2 * (y - 1)| ≤ M3 / 2 * (y - 1) ^ 2) →
              (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
                0 ≤ eps →
                  eps ≤ min a 1 / 4 →
                    ∀ {y : V},
                      lam y ≠ 0 →
                        |(GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y - 1) *
                              (gd (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y) * (w y / (1 + h y)))| ≤
                          64 / 27 * (GFNBounds.Balance.Cg g2 a M3 * wsup) *
                            GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam h) y ^ 2
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_.doc:
**`|(r−1)φ| ≤ (64/27)C_g‖w‖_{L^∞}(Ah^⊥)²`** — Step 3's pointwise estimate, *quadratic* in
`Ah^⊥` rather than the `ε|Ah^⊥|` of Step 1.

The chain is `|r−1| · C_g|r−1| · (4/3)‖w‖_{L^∞}` with `|r−1| ≤ (4/3)|Ah^⊥|` used twice, so the
constant is `(4/3)³ = 64/27 ≈ 2.370`. The paper prints `4`; see
`abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_phi_sq_le_C6`.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam w h : V → ℝ} {gd : ℝ → ℝ} {g2 a M3 wsup eps : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
      0 ≤ g2 →
        0 ≤ M3 →
          (∀ (x : V), |w x| ≤ wsup) →
            (∀ (y : ℝ), |y - 1| ≤ a → |gd y - g2 * (y - 1)| ≤ M3 / 2 * (y - 1) ^ 2) →
              (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
                0 ≤ eps →
                  eps ≤ min a 1 / 4 →
                    ∀ {y : V},
                      lam y ≠ 0 →
                        |(GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y - 1) *
                              (gd (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y) * (w y / (1 + h y)))| ≤
                          GFNBounds.Balance.C5 g2 a M3 wsup * eps *
                            |GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam h) y|
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_mul_.doc:
**`|(r−1)φ| ≤ C₅ε|Ah^⊥|`** (`proofs.tex:628`), with `C₅ = (16/3)C_g‖w‖_{L^∞}`. The chain is
`|r−1|·C_g|r−1|·(4/3)wsup` and `(r−1)² ≤ 4ε|Ah^⊥|`, whose product is exactly `16/3`.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_le_t.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam h : V → ℝ} {eps : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
      (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
        eps ≤ 1 / 4 →
          ∀ {y : V}, lam y ≠ 0 → |GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y - 1| ≤ 2 * eps / (1 - eps)

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_le_f.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam h : V → ℝ} {eps : ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
    (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
      eps ≤ 1 / 4 →
        ∀ {y : V},
          lam y ≠ 0 →
            |GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y - 1| ≤
              4 / 3 * |GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam h) y|

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_le_a.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam h : V → ℝ} {eps a : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
      (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
        0 ≤ eps →
          eps ≤ min a 1 / 4 → ∀ {y : V}, lam y ≠ 0 → |GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam (fun x => 1 + h x) y - 1| ≤ a
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_ratio_sub_one_le_a.doc:
**`|r−1| ≤ a`** — the two previous bounds chained, which is what puts `r` inside the window
`[1−a, 1+a]` on which `htaylor` speaks.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_mean_sub_le_energy.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam w : V → ℝ} {gd : ℝ → ℝ} {h : ℝ → V → ℝ}
  {g2 a M3 wsup eps T t₀ t₁ : ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
    (∀ (x : V), 0 < lam x) →
      (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
        ∑ x, lam x = 1 →
          0 ≤ g2 →
            0 ≤ M3 →
              0 ≤ a →
                0 ≤ wsup →
                  (∀ (x : V), |w x| ≤ wsup) →
                    (∀ (y : ℝ), |y - 1| ≤ a → |gd y - g2 * (y - 1)| ≤ M3 / 2 * (y - 1) ^ 2) →
                      0 ≤ eps →
                        eps ≤ min a 1 / 4 →
                          (GFNBounds.Balance.IsGradientFlow K lam (fun z => lam z * w z) gd fun s x => 1 + h s x) →
                            (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 T, ∀ (x : V), |h s x| ≤ eps) →
                              0 ≤ t₀ →
                                t₀ ≤ t₁ →
                                  t₁ ≤ T →
                                    |GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (h t₁) - GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam (h t₀)| ≤
                                      GFNBounds.Balance.C6 (GFNBounds.Balance.Cg g2 a M3) wsup *
                                        ∫ (s : ℝ) in t₀..t₁,
                                          GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam
                                              (GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam (h s))) ^
                                            2
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_mean_sub_le_energy.doc:
**`|m_{t₁} − m_{t₀}| ≤ C₆∫_{t₀}^{t₁}‖Ah^⊥‖²`** — Step 3's pointwise bound integrated.

Again not by the fundamental theorem applied to `ṁ`, which carries `g'`: the two functions
`τ ↦ C₆∫_{t₀}^τ‖Ah^⊥‖² ∓ m_τ` have non-negative derivative, hence are monotone, and only the
continuous integrand is integrated.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_meanL2_le_nrmL2.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ lam x) → ∑ x, lam x = 1 → ∀ (h : V → ℝ), |GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam h| ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam h

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_mass_le_nrmL2.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ lam x) → ∑ x, lam x = 1 → ∀ (a : V → ℝ), |∑ x, lam x * a x| ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam a
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_mass_le_nrmL2.doc:
**`‖a‖_{L²(λ)} ≥ |∫ a dλ|`** (`proofs.tex:809`: "since `λ` is a probability measure"),
Cauchy–Schwarz against `𝟏`. This is where `λ` being a probability is spent — `MassIdentity` does
not need it.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_log_sub_le_two_sq.doc:
**`|log y − (y−1)| ≤ 2(y−1)²` for `|y − 1| ≤ 1/2`.**

Both halves are one-sided logarithm bounds the library already has: `log y ≤ y − 1` is
`Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos`, and `(y−1)/y ≤ log y` is `sub_one_le_mul_log` divided by `y`. The
second gives `log y − (y−1) ≥ −(y−1)²/y ≥ −2(y−1)²`, the factor `2` being `1/y` at `y = 1/2`.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_le_nrmL2_div_sqrt.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {lamMin : ℝ},
  0 < lamMin → (∀ (x : V), lamMin ≤ lam x) → ∀ (a : V → ℝ) (x : V), √lamMin * |a x| ≤ GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam a
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_le_nrmL2_div_sqrt.doc:
**`‖·‖_{L^∞} ≤ ‖·‖_{L²(λ)}/√λ_min`**, the paper's `C_∞ = (min λ)^{−1/2}`
(`proofs.tex:613`), with `λ_min` a hypothesis rather than a minimum over a `MarkedGraph`. This is
`Graph.sqrt_minOver_mul_abs_le_nrmL2` with the graph removed; `λ ≥ 0` is not assumed, being
implied by `0 < λ_min ≤ λ`.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_le_Cinf_mul_nrmL2.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {lamMin : ℝ},
  0 < lamMin →
    (∀ (x : V), lamMin ≤ lam x) →
      ∀ (f : V → ℝ) (x : V), |f x| ≤ GFNBounds.Balance.Cinf lamMin * GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam f

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_le_Cinf_mean_add_p.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {lamMin : ℝ},
  0 < lamMin →
    (∀ (x : V), lamMin ≤ lam x) →
      ∑ x, lam x = 1 →
        ∀ (f : V → ℝ) (x : V),
          |f x| ≤
            GFNBounds.Balance.Cinf lamMin *
              (|GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam f| + GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam f))
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_le_Cinf_mean_add_p.doc: **`‖f‖_{L^∞} ≤ C_∞(|Πf| + ‖f^⊥‖)`** — the split Step 4 reads the sup bound through.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_inv_sq_sub_one_le.doc:
**`|1/(1+t)² − 1| ≤ 4ε`** for `|t| ≤ ε ≤ 1/4` (`proofs.tex:623`).

Proved directly rather than through the paper's `(2ε+ε²)/(1−ε)²`; see the module SCOPE for why
the two are not the same inequality, and for where each is tight.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_deriv_mean_le.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam w h : V → ℝ} {gd : ℝ → ℝ} {g2 a M3 wsup eps : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
      (∀ (x : V), 0 < lam x) →
        0 ≤ g2 →
          0 ≤ M3 →
            0 ≤ a →
              0 ≤ wsup →
                (∀ (x : V), |w x| ≤ wsup) →
                  (∀ (y : ℝ), |y - 1| ≤ a → |gd y - g2 * (y - 1)| ≤ M3 / 2 * (y - 1) ^ 2) →
                    (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) →
                      0 ≤ eps →
                        eps ≤ min a 1 / 4 →
                          |GFNBounds.Graph.meanL2 lam
                                (GFNBounds.Balance.lossGrad K lam (fun z => lam z * w z) gd fun z => 1 + h z)| ≤
                            GFNBounds.Balance.C6 (GFNBounds.Balance.Cg g2 a M3) wsup *
                              GFNBounds.Graph.nrmL2 lam (GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam h)) ^
                                2
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_deriv_mean_le.doc:
**`|ṁ| ≤ C₆‖Ah^⊥‖²`** (`proofs.tex:641`), Step 3's estimate on the drift of the mass.

`MassIdentity.integral_gradDensity` turns `∫D dλ` into `∫(r−1)φ dλ` — the step the paper opens
with, and the only place `P†` preserving `λ`-integrals is spent — and the pointwise bound is
integrated against `λ`.

GFNBounds.Balance.abs_Aop_le_two_sup.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam h : V → ℝ} {eps : ℝ},
  (∀ (x y : V), 0 ≤ K x y) →
    GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K → (∀ (x : V), |h x| ≤ eps) → ∀ (y : V), |GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam h y| ≤ 2 * eps
GFNBounds.Balance.abs_Aop_le_two_sup.doc:
**`|Ah| ≤ 2ε` pointwise** when `|h| ≤ ε`: `Ph(y)` is the average of `h` against the weights
`λ(x)K(x,y)/λ(y)`, which sum to `1` in `x` by invariance, so `|Ph| ≤ ε`; the identity costs
another `ε`. Where `λ` vanishes `P` returns `0` and the bound is `ε`.

GFNBounds.Balance.T0_eq.type:
∀ {L0 wmin lamMin U0 eps0 m0 sigStar : ℝ},
  0 < lamMin →
    0 < wmin →
      0 < U0 →
        0 < eps0 →
          0 < m0 →
            0 < sigStar →
              GFNBounds.Balance.T0 L0
                  (GFNBounds.Balance.cDelta wmin lamMin U0 (GFNBounds.Balance.delta0 eps0 m0 (sigStar / √lamMin) U0)) =
                4 * L0 * U0 ^ 6 * sigStar ^ 4 / (wmin ^ 2 * eps0 ^ 4 * m0 ^ 4 * lamMin ^ 5)

GFNBounds.Balance.StrictlyUnimodal.doc:
**Strict unimodality** (`proofs.tex:788`): `sign g'(x) = sign(x − 1)` for `x ≠ 1`, on the
domain `ℝ_+^*` of the generator. "Same sign, and non-zero" is `0 < g'(x)(x − 1)`.

Only the derivative is carried; `g` itself never appears. See the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Balance.OpBound₂.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → ((V → V → ℝ) → V → V → ℝ) → ℝ → Prop
GFNBounds.Balance.OpBound₂.doc: `b` is an operator-norm bound for `A` on `L²(λ₂)`.

GFNBounds.Balance.OpBound.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → ℝ) → ((V → ℝ) → V → ℝ) → ℝ → Prop
GFNBounds.Balance.OpBound.doc: `b` is an operator-norm bound for `A` on `L²(λ)`.

GFNBounds.Balance.Lgd_le.type:
∀ {g2 a M3 wsup wmin Bhat eps : ℝ},
  0 ≤ g2 →
    0 ≤ M3 →
      0 ≤ a →
        0 ≤ wsup →
          0 ≤ wmin →
            wmin ≤ wsup →
              1 ≤ Bhat →
                0 ≤ eps →
                  eps ≤ GFNBounds.Balance.eps1 g2 wmin (GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp g2 a M3 wsup) Bhat →
                    GFNBounds.Balance.Lgd g2 wsup (GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp g2 a M3 wsup) eps ≤ 5 / 2 * (g2 * wsup)
GFNBounds.Balance.Lgd_le.doc:
**`L ≤ (5/2)g''(1)‖w‖_{L^∞}`, sharper than the paper's `3g''(1)‖w‖_{L^∞}`**
(`proofs.tex:654`). The slack is `Kε ≤ g''(1)w_min/(2B̂) ≤ g''(1)‖w‖_{L^∞}/2`, using `B̂ ≥ 1`.
Nothing downstream uses it: `γ₀` is stated at the exact `L`.

GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp_pos.type: ∀ {g2 a M3 wsup : ℝ}, 0 < g2 → 0 ≤ M3 → 0 ≤ a → 0 < wsup → 0 < GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp g2 a M3 wsup

GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp_nonneg.type: ∀ {g2 a M3 wsup : ℝ}, 0 ≤ g2 → 0 ≤ M3 → 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ wsup → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp g2 a M3 wsup

GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp_mul_eps_mul_Bhat_.type:
∀ {g2 wmin Bhat eps kap : ℝ},
  0 ≤ g2 * wmin → 0 ≤ kap → 0 ≤ Bhat → eps ≤ GFNBounds.Balance.eps1 g2 wmin kap Bhat → kap * eps * Bhat ≤ g2 * wmin / 2
GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp_mul_eps_mul_Bhat_.doc:
**`Kεδ ≤ g''(1)w_min/2` at `ε ≤ ε₁`** — the arithmetic that names `ε₁`: it is *exactly* the
threshold at which the expansion error eats half of the coercivity, no more and no less.

GFNBounds.Balance.Kexp.doc:
**`K := 2C₄ + C₅`** (`proofs.tex:631`), the constant of `eq:gradient_expansion`. The `2` is
`‖A†‖ ≤ 2`.

GFNBounds.Balance.IsGradientFlow.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (ℝ → ℝ) → (ℝ → V → ℝ) → Prop
GFNBounds.Balance.IsGradientFlow.doc:
**`μ̇_t = −∇^λ 𝓛_{g,ν}(μ_t)`** (`proofs.tex:569`, `:613`, `:880`), the gradient flow, written
on a finite state space as what it is there: an **ODE in `ℝ^V`**, one scalar equation per state.

`u t x` is the `λ`-density of `μ_t` at the state `x`. Existence of such a curve is not claimed
anywhere in this file; every statement below hypothesises one.

GFNBounds.Balance.Invariant.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → Prop
GFNBounds.Balance.Invariant.doc:
**`λ` is invariant for the kernel `K`**: `λK = λ`, written as a finite sum. This is the
paper's "`λ` is `T`-invariant", and — read on the density action `P` of `T` — it is exactly the
paper's `P𝟏 = 𝟏`.

GFNBounds.Balance.H_proj_eq_zero.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {H Pi : E →L[ℝ] E},
  (∀ (x y : E), inner ℝ (Pi x) y = inner ℝ x (Pi y)) →
    (∀ (x y : E), inner ℝ (H x) y = inner ℝ x (H y)) → (∀ (x : E), Pi (H x) = 0) → ∀ (x : E), H (Pi x) = 0
GFNBounds.Balance.H_proj_eq_zero.doc:
**`ΠH = 0` gives `HΠ = 0`** when both `Π` and `H` are self-adjoint. Used once, to see that
`h_k − Πh_0` satisfies the same recursion as `h_k` — which is what makes the iteration stay
inside `ker Π`, where the coercivity is a bound on the whole quadratic form.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.scale.doc:
The normalisation `m(1) = 2` divides by this. It is positive because neither closed band
contains `1`.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.one_notM.doc:
**`1 ∉ U⁻ ∪ U⁺`** — the bands do not contain `1`, which is what makes the frozen loss
*positive* and not merely constant.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.noConfus.type: Sort u → GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands → GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands → Sort u

{P : Sort u} →
  {t t' : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands} → t = t' → GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.noConfusionType P t t'

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.mk.sizeO.type:
∀ (a b c d : ℝ) (a_pos : 0 < a) (a_lt_b : a < b) (b_lt_one : b < 1) (one_lt_c : 1 < c) (c_lt_d : c < d),

        c_lt_d := c_lt_d } =
    1 + sizeOf a + sizeOf b + sizeOf c + sizeOf d + sizeOf a_pos + sizeOf a_lt_b + sizeOf b_lt_one + sizeOf one_lt_c +
      sizeOf c_lt_d

{P : Sort u} →

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.mk.injEq.type:
∀ (a b c d : ℝ) (a_pos : 0 < a) (a_lt_b : a < b) (b_lt_one : b < 1) (one_lt_c : 1 < c) (c_lt_d : c < d)
  (a_1 b_1 c_1 d_1 : ℝ) (a_pos_1 : 0 < a_1) (a_lt_b_1 : a_1 < b_1) (b_lt_one_1 : b_1 < 1) (one_lt_c_1 : 1 < c_1)

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.mk.inj.type:
∀ {a b c d : ℝ} {a_pos : 0 < a} {a_lt_b : a < b} {b_lt_one : b < 1} {one_lt_c : 1 < c} {c_lt_d : c < d}
  {a_1 b_1 c_1 d_1 : ℝ} {a_pos_1 : 0 < a_1} {a_lt_b_1 : a_1 < b_1} {b_lt_one_1 : b_1 < 1} {one_lt_c_1 : 1 < c_1}
  {c_lt_d_1 : c_1 < d_1},
  { a := a, b := b, c := c, d := d, a_pos := a_pos, a_lt_b := a_lt_b, b_lt_one := b_lt_one, one_lt_c := one_lt_c,
        c_lt_d := c_lt_d } =
      { a := a_1, b := b_1, c := c_1, d := d_1, a_pos := a_pos_1, a_lt_b := a_lt_b_1, b_lt_one := b_lt_one_1,
        one_lt_c := one_lt_c_1, c_lt_d := c_lt_d_1 } →
    a = a_1 ∧ b = b_1 ∧ c = c_1 ∧ d = d_1

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.mk.congr.type:
∀ (a a_1 : ℝ) (e_a : a = a_1) (b b_1 : ℝ) (e_b : b = b_1) (c c_1 : ℝ) (e_c : c = c_1) (d d_1 : ℝ) (e_d : d = d_1)
  (a_pos : 0 < a) (a_lt_b : a < b) (b_lt_one : b < 1) (one_lt_c : 1 < c) (c_lt_d : c < d),

    { a := a_1, b := b_1, c := c_1, d := d_1, a_pos := ⋯, a_lt_b := ⋯, b_lt_one := ⋯, one_lt_c := ⋯, c_lt_d := ⋯ }

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.mk.type: (a b c d : ℝ) → 0 < a → a < b → b < 1 → 1 < c → c < d → GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.mem_Icc_.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x : ℝ}, x ∈ F.upper → x ∈ Set.Icc F.c F.d
∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x : ℝ}, x ∈ F.lower → x ∈ Set.Icc F.a F.b

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m_pos_of.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {t : ℝ}, F.b < t → t < F.c → 0 < F.m t
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m_pos_of.doc:
Between the bands — in particular on a punctured neighbourhood of `1` — `m` is positive. This
is the paper's "the integrand is nonnegative and positive near `1`".

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m_pos.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {t : ℝ}, t ∉ Set.Icc F.a F.b → t ∉ Set.Icc F.c F.d → 0 < F.m t
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m_pos.doc: **`m > 0` off the bands' closures** (`proofs.tex:760`, as repaired on 2026-09-08).

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m_eq_zer.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {t : ℝ}, t ∈ Set.Icc F.a F.b ∪ Set.Icc F.c F.d → F.m t = 0
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m_eq_zer.doc: **`m ≡ 0` on the bands** (`proofs.tex:760`), on the closed `[a,b] ∪ [c,d]`.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.m.doc:
**The multiplier `m` of `prop:nonlinear_freezing`** (`proofs.tex:760`): `C^∞`, nonnegative,
bounded by `8/scale`, equal to `2` at `1`, and vanishing exactly on `[a,b] ∪ [c,d]`.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.interval.type:
∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) (p q : ℝ),
  IntervalIntegrable (fun t => F.m t * (t - 1)) MeasureTheory.volume p q

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.g_pos.doc:
**`g > 0` away from `1`**, the second admissibility clause (`proofs.tex:760`, proof
`proofs.tex:770`): the integrand is nonnegative on `[1, x]`, negative-signed on `[x, 1]`, and
strictly positive somewhere on either, because `m > 0` between the bands.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.g_eq_of_.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x y : ℝ}, (∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc x y, F.m t = 0) → F.g x = F.g y
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.g_eq_of_.doc:
**`g` is constant on each band** (`proofs.tex:776`: "`g'` vanishing identically on each band
makes `g` constant on each of the two intervals"), proved from the vanishing of the integrand
rather than from a mean-value argument.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.g_const_.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x y : ℝ}, x ∈ Set.Icc F.c F.d → y ∈ Set.Icc F.c F.d → F.g x = F.g y
∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x y : ℝ}, x ∈ Set.Icc F.a F.b → y ∈ Set.Icc F.a F.b → F.g x = F.g y

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.deriv_g_.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x : ℝ}, x ∈ F.bands → deriv F.g x = 0
∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) {x : ℝ}, x ∈ Set.Icc F.a F.b ∪ Set.Icc F.c F.d → deriv F.g x = 0
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.deriv_g_.doc:
**`g' ≡ 0` on `U⁻ ∪ U⁺`** (`proofs.tex:760`, `:770`) — the property the whole proposition turns
on, here on the closed bands.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.deriv_g.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands), deriv F.g = fun x => F.m x * (x - 1)
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.deriv_g.doc:
**`g'(x) = m(x)(x−1)`** (`proofs.tex:770`), by the fundamental theorem of calculus, the
integrand being continuous.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.deriv_de.doc:
**`g''(1) = 2`**, the third admissibility clause (`proofs.tex:760`, proof `proofs.tex:770`:
"`g''(1) = m(1) = 2`").

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.d.doc: right endpoint of the upper band

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.continuo.type: ∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands), Continuous fun t => F.m t * (t - 1)

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.contDiff.doc: **`g` is `C^∞`** (`proofs.tex:760`, `:770`): its derivative is `m ·(x−1)`, and `m` is `C^∞`.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.casesOn.type:
{motive : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands → Sort u} →
  (t : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands) →
    ((a b c d : ℝ) →
        (a_pos : 0 < a) →
          (a_lt_b : a < b) →
            (b_lt_one : b < 1) →
              (one_lt_c : 1 < c) →
                (c_lt_d : c < d) →
                  motive
                    { a := a, b := b, c := c, d := d, a_pos := a_pos, a_lt_b := a_lt_b, b_lt_one := b_lt_one,
                      one_lt_c := one_lt_c, c_lt_d := c_lt_d }) →
      motive t

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.c.doc: left endpoint of the upper band

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.bound.doc: The explicit bound `‖m‖_∞ ≤ 8/scale`, the constant every growth estimate below inherits.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.b.doc: right endpoint of the lower band

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.admissib.type:
∀ (F : GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands),
  ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) F.g ∧
    F.g 1 = 0 ∧
      (∀ (x : ℝ), x ≠ 1 → 0 < F.g x) ∧
        deriv (deriv F.g) 1 = 2 ∧ (∀ (x : ℝ), |F.g x| ≤ F.bound * (1 + |x| ^ 2)) ∧ ∀ x ∈ F.bands, deriv F.g x = 0
GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.admissib.doc:
**`prop:nonlinear_freezing`, admissibility** (`proofs.tex:760`, proof `proofs.tex:770`): `g` is
a `C^∞` admissible generator — `g(1) = 0`, `g > 0` elsewhere, `g''(1) = 2`,
`|g(x)| ≤ C(1 + |x|²)` — with `g' ≡ 0` on `U⁻ ∪ U⁺`.

The constant is `C = 8/scale`, explicit as the house rule requires.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.abs_g_le.doc:
**`|g(x)| ≤ C(1 + |x|²)`**, the fourth admissibility clause as the paper states it
(`proofs.tex:760`), with `C = 8/scale` explicit.

**`|g(x)| ≤ (‖m‖_∞/2)(x−1)²`**, the quantitative form of the fourth admissibility clause
(`proofs.tex:770`), with the explicit `‖m‖_∞ ≤ 8/scale`.

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.a.doc: left endpoint of the lower band

GFNBounds.Balance.FreezingBands.doc:
**The two bands of `prop:nonlinear_freezing`**: `U⁻ = (a, b)` with `0 < a < b < 1` and
`U⁺ = (c, d)` with `1 < c < d`.

The strict inequalities `b < 1` and `1 < c` are the paper's `U⁻ ⊂ (0,1)`, `U⁺ ⊂ (1,+∞)` read so
that a continuous multiplier can vanish on the closures and still satisfy `m(1) = 2`; see the
module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Balance.DetailedBalance.type: {V : Type u_1} → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (V → V → ℝ) → Prop
GFNBounds.Balance.DetailedBalance.doc:
**Detailed balance of `(F, π_→)` with respect to `π_←`** (`proofs.tex:530`):
`F(s) π_→(s → s') = F(s') π_←(s' → s)` at every pair.

GFNBounds.Balance.Cg.doc:
**`C_g := g''(1) + aM₃/2`** (`proofs.tex:628`), the Lipschitz constant of `g'` at `1` on the
window `[1−a, 1+a]`.

GFNBounds.Balance.C7_nonneg.type: ∀ {c6 g2 wmin : ℝ}, 0 ≤ c6 → 0 ≤ g2 * wmin → 0 ≤ GFNBounds.Balance.C7 c6 g2 wmin

GFNBounds.Balance.C6_pos.type: ∀ {g2 a M3 wsup : ℝ}, 0 < g2 → 0 ≤ M3 → 0 ≤ a → 0 < wsup → 0 < GFNBounds.Balance.C6 (GFNBounds.Balance.Cg g2 a M3) wsup

GFNBounds.Balance.C4.doc:
**`C₄ := ‖w‖_{L^∞}(4g''(1) + 3M₃)`** (`proofs.tex:626`), the constant of the pointwise
remainder in the expansion of `φ`.

GFNBounds.Balance.BhatSigma_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (G : GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V) (uH lam : V → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Balance.BhatSigma G uH lam = GFNBounds.Graph.sigmaStar G uH / √(GFNBounds.Graph.minOver G lam)

GFNBounds.Balance.BhatSigma.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → GFNBounds.Graph.MarkedGraph V → (V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → ℝ

GFNBounds.Balance.Balanced.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → Prop

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_smul.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (lam : V → ℝ) (K : V → V → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (u : V → ℝ) (y : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (fun z => c * u z) y = c * GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam u y

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_perpL2.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {K : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K →
    ∀ (h : V → ℝ) {y : V},
      lam y ≠ 0 → GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (GFNBounds.Balance.perpL2 lam h) y = GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam h y
GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_perpL2.doc:
**`Ah = Ah_⊥`** — the first of the four facts `proofs.tex:621` recalls. `λ`-almost
everywhere: where `λ` vanishes both sides are `−h(y)` and `−h_⊥(y)`, which differ by the mean.

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_eq_ratio_sub_one_m.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam u : V → ℝ} {y : V},
  u y ≠ 0 → GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam u y = (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam u y - 1) * u y
GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_eq_ratio_sub_one_m.doc:
**`(P−I)u = (r−1)u` at a state** (`proofs.tex:813`): `Au y = (r(y) − 1)u(y)` whenever
`u y ≠ 0`.

The hypothesis is on `u`, not on `λ`. Where `λ(y) = 0` the identity holds anyway, both sides being
`−u(y)` under Lean's `x/0 = 0`; where `λ(y) ≠ 0` and `u(y) = 0` it **fails**, the left side being
`(μT)(y)/λ(y)` and the right side `0`. See the module SCOPE.

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_eq_ratio_sub_one.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam u : V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), u x ≠ 0) → GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam u = fun y => (GFNBounds.Balance.ratio K lam u y - 1) * u y
GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_eq_ratio_sub_one.doc: **`(P−I)u = (r−1)u`**, unapplied, for a nowhere-vanishing density — the form a norm consumes.

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (lam h : V → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam h = fun y => GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam K h y - h y

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_const.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {lam : V → ℝ} {K : V → V → ℝ},
  GFNBounds.Core.IsInvariant lam K → ∀ (c : ℝ) {y : V}, lam y ≠ 0 → GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (fun x => c) y = 0

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_apply.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (lam h : V → ℝ) (y : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam h y = GFNBounds.Core.densAct lam K h y - h y

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop_add.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (lam : V → ℝ) (K : V → V → ℝ) (a b : V → ℝ) (y : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam (fun x => a x + b x) y = GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam a y + GFNBounds.Balance.Aop K lam b y

GFNBounds.Balance.Aop.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Balance.Aop.doc:
**The paper's `A = P − I`** (`eq:linearized_flow`, `proofs.tex:566`; `proofs.tex:741`), acting
on densities: `P` is `Core.densAct`, the density action of the kernel `K` on `𝓜²(λ)`.

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj_sub.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (a b : V → ℝ) (x : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K (fun y => a y - b y) x = GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K a x - GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K b x

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj_smul.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (a : V → ℝ) (x : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K (fun y => c * a y) x = c * GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K a x

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj_eq.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (φ : V → ℝ),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K φ = fun x => GFNBounds.Balance.funAct K φ x - φ x

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj_const.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : V), ∑ y, K x y = 1) → ∀ (c : ℝ) (x : V), GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K (fun x => c) x = 0

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj_apply.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (φ : V → ℝ) (x : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K φ x = GFNBounds.Balance.funAct K φ x - φ x

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj_add.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] (K : V → V → ℝ) (a b : V → ℝ) (x : V),
  GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K (fun y => a y + b y) x = GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K a x + GFNBounds.Balance.Adj K b x

GFNBounds.Balance.Adj.type: {V : Type u_1} → [Fintype V] → (V → V → ℝ) → (V → ℝ) → V → ℝ
GFNBounds.Balance.Adj.doc:
**The paper's `A† = P† − I`**, acting on functions: `P†` is the function action
`(P†φ)(x) = ∑_y K(x,y)φ(y)`, the `L²(λ)`-adjoint of `P` by `lem:adjoint`*(3)*.
